jobs.title: Crew Member - HOYTS Docklands
jobs.description:
**Let’s talk about HOYTS:**
Working at HOYTS means being part of the team that keeps the magic of the movies alive. Our Cinema Crew Members play a hands-on role in creating smooth, enjoyable experiences for every guest - from the moment they arrive to the moment the credits roll.

Life at HOYTS isn’t always like a movie - working here can be physical, loud and fast-paced. There are some physical aspects to being a Cinema Crew Member that you need to be aware of. The document HERE provides details of the physical requirements involved during a typical HOYTS Crew Member shift.

Please watch the video linked HERE, to catch a glimpse of life as a HOYTS Crew Member.

As a Crew Member, you’ll help bring the HOYTS experience to life by:

* Welcoming guests with a friendly, genuine attitude
* Keeping our cinemas clean, comfortable, and looking their best
* Supporting operations across ticketing, food & beverage, floor service - including serving HOYTS’ iconic popcorn and choc tops
* Assisting with stock rotation, session checks, and cleaning duties
* Helping bring promotions and special experiences to life

**Who We’re Looking For:**
We’re looking for team members who bring enthusiasm, reliability and a positive attitude.

**At HOYTS, we value people who are:**
1. Customer-focused

* You enjoy helping people, answering questions and making someone’s day a little easier or more enjoyable

2. Eager to learn and grow

* You’re open to trying new tasks, picking up new skills and building confidence as you rotate through different parts of the cinema

3. A supportive teammate

* You like working with others, stepping in when someone needs a hand and celebrating wins together - big or small

4. Adaptable in a fast-paced environment

* Cinemas get busy, especially on weekends and holidays. You stay calm, keep things moving and enjoy the buzz of a lively shift

5. Availability & Reliability

* We’re seeking team members who can commit to a flexible roster, especially during peak times like weekends, evenings, public holidays, and school holidays. Regular availability during these periods is essential. Please be ready to share your availability when applying

Why HOYTS?

At HOYTS, we’re passionate about creating unforgettable experiences that bring people together and our Cinema Crew are the heart and soul of making that magic happen. Our cinemas are lively, welcoming, and genuinely fun places to work, where team members support one another and celebrate every success together.

The HOYTS Group is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. All hiring decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

**When you join HOYTS, you’ll benefit from:**

* A vibrant, inclusive, and team-focused environment where your contributions truly matter
* Exciting perks like discounted movie tickets, tasty food and beverage offers, and exclusive Crew events
* The chance to develop a broad, versatile skill set across entertainment, retail, and hospitality and beyond. Our industry is all-encompassing, offering a unique, hands-on experience that helps you grow in many directions
* Real opportunities to build new skills, gain valuable experience, and advance your career in a fast-paced, dynamic workplace
* Crew Members are employed on a permanent part-time basis, giving you the opportunity to really own your role and build long-lasting connections. As a part-time team member, you’ll have guaranteed minimum hours and access to paid leave entitlements. A standard shift is generally a minimum of 4 hours, and you’ll be rostered for at least 8 hours per week. Your agreed part-time hours will always be scheduled within your stated availability, and rosters are released each Friday in Australia, for the week commencing the following Thursday.

Join us at HOYTS, where your work makes a difference and every day brings opportunities.

**To note:**

* Your position is classified under the Broadcasting, Recorded Entertainment and Cinemas Award 2020 as a Cinema Worker Level 2. Your hourly pay rate is based on this classification and varies by age
* Please note that candidates must have valid working rights in Australia to be considered

Ready to Join the HOYTS Crew?

HOYTS is one of Australia’s most exciting entertainment destinations and we’d love to welcome you to the team.

If you're ready for a role that’s exciting, fast-paced and full of opportunity, press APPLY NOW!

jobs.title: MS&T Fill & Finish Value Stream Lead
jobs.description:
**Entity:** CSL Behring

**Job Category:** Engineering

**Job Family:** Project Delivery

**Job Type:** Full Time

**Location****:** Broadmeadows, Victoria, Australia

**Employer Reference:** R-288327

**Job Description**

**The Opportunity**

The Process Engineering function at CSL Behring is recruiting for a **Manufacturing Science & Technology (MS&T) Filling Value Stream Lead** (Engineer or Scientist) to join our dynamic team at the Broadmeadows site. This exciting full-time permanent role will lead time-important frontline technical support within the filling production space and develop in partnerships the MS&T strategy within the Fill & Finish space in support of our life-saving parenteral manufacturing operations and strategic project execution.

You will apply fundamental scientific and engineering knowledge to the design, implementation and life cycle management of complex process and technology.

You will work with a broad range of local and global counterparts spanning three continents and functions as diverse as Manufacturing, Operational Analytics, Engineering, Quality, Technical Transfer, Validation, Research & Development and Regulatory Affairs.

**The Role**

Reporting to the **Director, MS&T Site Lead**, your responsibilities will include:

* Identifying key pro-active indicators to measure process performance across the fill and finish value stream and adjust, improve or update the process to optimise and realise quality and/ or yield opportunities
* Delivering day to day prioritisation of MS&T re-active support across the fill and finish value stream to manage workload
* Supporting the development of MS&T fill and finish value stream strategy in partnership with the MS&T site lead and stakeholders to plan and prioritise proactive improvements
* Developing processes for the fill and finish MS&T function to prioritise work, identify the highest value improvements and facilitate scoping and execution of implementation within internal PE functions (Process Technology, Qualification, Validation, Execution Systems etc.) and across key partner functions (Value Stream, Project Delivery, Quality Assurance etc.)
* Building the structure in conjunction with other MS&T value stream leads and MS&T Principals to capture and build process understanding
* Interacting with global counterparts and colleagues to identify synergies across multiple facilities in order to prioritise activities
* Owning and interpreting key value stream KPI's to ensure the process is reliably and repeatably producing
* Structuring with MS&T Principals ways to test theories and prove root cause using data, internal and external expertise and lab based capabilities
* Assuring compliance with safety and regulatory requirements during all phases of MS&T activity
* Providing cGMP compliant processes and facilities suitable for FDA and global regulatory approval
* Generating regular Product/Process performance overviews that are translated to a language relevant to stakeholders

**Your skills and experience**

* MS/MBA/BS/BA in Engineering or Life Sciences
* 7+ years experience in Science/ Engineering within a pharmaceutical manufacturing operation or in a pharmaceutical operation
* Experience leading matrix teams or leading teams directly desirable
* Ability to understand “the big picture” and approach problem solving in a proactive team manner
* Functional knowledge of cGMPs and manufacturing operations in FDA regulated facility
* Understanding of project management principles and project lifecycle phases
* Knowledge of Validation, CMC and facility regulatory submission requirements
* Demonstrated experience leading complex scientific investigations
* Experience with complex processes, technology and analytics
* Direct experience with regulated environments (i.e., cGMP, OSHA, EPA)
* Strong resourcefulness, drive, communication, collaboration, and conflict management skills
* Demonstrated ability to thrive in cross-functional, multicultural and international teams

**About CSL Behring**

CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients' needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world's largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/.

**Our Benefits**

For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL.

**You Belong at CSL**

At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.

To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

CSL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you are an individual with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, please visit https://www.csl.com/accessibility-statement.

jobs.title: Infrastructure & Capital Projects – Senior Associate / Manager
jobs.description:
**Description**

**About Alvarez & Marsal**

Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 10,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.

**The Team**

As infrastructure investment, energy transition and industrial development continue to reshape Australia, we are growing our Infrastructure & Capital Projects Advisory practice and are looking for talented Senior Consultants and Managers to join our team. This is an opportunity to work on some of Australia's largest and most complex infrastructure and capital projects while accelerating your career in a high-growth, entrepreneurial environment.

You will work alongside experienced infrastructure advisors, former industry executives and senior government stakeholders, helping clients make critical investment and delivery decisions that shape communities, industries and the national economy. Our team advises governments, infrastructure owners, investors and private sector participants throughout the project lifecycle — from strategic planning and business cases through to procurement, financing and delivery — across sectors including transport, energy, water, social infrastructure, defence, industrial development, and ports and logistics.

**How you will contribute**

As a Senior Consultant or Manager, you will:

***Support Major Infrastructure Investments***

* Contribute to strategic and commercial advisory engagements for major infrastructure projects and programs
* Assist clients in evaluating investment options, delivery models and procurement approaches
* Support the development of business cases, investment cases and infrastructure strategies

***Deliver Commercial and Financial Analysis***

* Build and analyse financial models to support infrastructure investment decisions
* Undertake commercial, economic and quantitative analysis
* Assess project risks, funding options and financing alternatives
* Develop insights that help clients make informed decisions

***Support Transactions and Procurement Processes***

* Assist with market engagement activities and transaction processes
* Support the evaluation of procurement submissions and commercial proposals
* Contribute to the development of commercial frameworks and negotiation strategies

***Work Closely with Clients***

* Engage directly with government agencies, infrastructure owners and private sector stakeholders
* Prepare presentations, reports and briefing materials for senior decision-makers
* Participate in workshops, stakeholder consultations and project governance activities

***Grow Your Skills and Career***

* Learn from experienced infrastructure leaders and industry specialists
* Develop expertise across infrastructure financing, commercial strategy and major project delivery
* Take increasing responsibility for project management and client engagement activities

**Qualifications**

* 3–7 years of experience in infrastructure advisory, project finance, commercial advisory, consulting, government, engineering, investment analysis or related fields
* Exposure to major infrastructure projects, capital programs or investment transactions
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Experience developing financial models, business cases, commercial analysis or investment assessments
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* The ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams
* Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
* A proactive and solutions-focused mindset
* Tertiary qualifications in Commerce, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Law, Business, Public Policy or a related discipline
* Curiosity, strong commercial acumen and a passion for infrastructure and nation-building projects
* Confidence working with a range of stakeholders, and a collaborative, proactive approach to problem solving

**Your journey at A&M**

We recognize that our people are the driving force behind our success, which is why we prioritize an employee experience that fosters each person's unique professional and personal development. Our robust performance development process promotes continuous learning, rewards your contributions, and fosters a culture of meritocracy. With top-notch training and on-the-job learning opportunities, you can acquire new skills and advance your career.

We prioritize your well-being, providing benefits and resources to support you on your personal journey. Our people consistently highlight the growth opportunities, our unique, entrepreneurial culture, and the fun we have together as their favorite aspects of working at A&M. The possibilities are endless for high-performing and passionate professionals.

jobs.title: Kitchen Assistant
jobs.description:
Become a skilled multitasker, keeping the kitchen in order and creating kitchen harmony!

* Contribute to the delivery of 5-star dining experiences
* A hospitality job where you're rewarded for your work
* No late nights!

**About the Role**

We have an exciting opportunity to join our supportive team as a Kitchen Assistant at **Nellie Melba Retirement Village**in **Wheelers Hill**. This is a **casual** position working ***Monday to Sunday 1130-1830*** at a **base hourly rate of $29.14 to $29.69, plus 25% casual loading**.

Your primary responsibility will be washing dishes and ensuring all kitchen equipment, crockery, cutlery, and utensils are cleaned to a high standard. From meals and activities to maintenance and support, our teams work together so residents can feel confident everything is taken care of – because behind that promise is the standard we’ve always held ourselves to: it’s got to be good enough for mum and dad.

We’re in a period of real transformation, focusing on stronger commercial outcomes, smarter ways of working, and continuing to set the standard in retirement living and aged care.

**Ryman Perks**

* Work in a facility that operates more like a family business. We are well resourced and have great care ratios
* Fun, friendly and supportive team environment
* Monthly employee recognition
* Receive a complementary designer uniform
* Receive a Ryman Team Benefits card with discounts from 45+ well-known brands

At Ryman, we support an environment where everyone feels welcome to be themselves. We embrace diversity and celebrate individual uniqueness, encouraging anyone wanting to work for Ryman to apply for our vacant positions.

If you share those values and you're looking for a career where your work truly makes a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
### **General information**

Name

Application Security Specialist

Site / Location

Melbourne Support Centre

Ref #

12387216

Entity

Australia Post

Opening Date

26-Aug-2026

Suburb

Richmond

Work Type

Permanent Full Time

### **Description & Requirements**

Working in tech at Australia Post is where innovation and problem solving meets great people and agile working. You’ll work with bright people on building and maintaining products and services that you and every other Australian get to benefit from every day. Whether you’re working from our modern office or your one at home, you’ll be part of a culture of collaboration and connection, making long-lasting impact right across Australia.

**About the opportunity**

As our Application Security Specialist, you’ll play a critical role in protecting Australia Post’s digital ecosystem by identifying, testing and validating security risks across web applications, APIs and modern technology platforms. You'll work closely with engineering teams, architects, product owners and cyber specialists to embed security throughout the software development lifecycle and help teams deliver innovative solutions securely and at pace. This role is ideal for a hands-on penetration tester who enjoys uncovering vulnerabilities, influencing outcomes and partnering with teams to drive meaningful security improvements.

You’ll also

* Lead penetration testing and security validation activities across web applications, APIs and modern technology environments.
* Partner with engineering teams to uplift secure SDLC practices through threat modelling, security guidance and practical remediation support.
* Drive the adoption and optimisation of application security tooling, including SAST, SCA, DAST and CI/CD security controls.
* Leverage AI-assisted security testing techniques and tooling, ensuring all testing activities remain authorised, governed and human-led.

**About you**

You’re a curious, collaborative and technically strong security professional who enjoys getting hands-on with offensive security activities while helping others build secure solutions. You can confidently communicate complex technical findings to a broad range of stakeholders and influence security outcomes through strong relationships, practical advice and a risk-based approach. You enjoy solving complex problems, continuously learning and working across diverse technologies at enterprise scale.

You’ll also need

* Strong hands-on penetration testing experience across web applications and APIs, including scoping, execution, reporting and remediation verification.
* Experience in Application Security, Security Engineering or DevSecOps, including SAST, SCA and CI/CD security integration.
* Exposure to cloud environments (AWS, Azure and/or GCP), threat modelling, secure solution design and AI/LLM security concepts and testing approaches.

**What else is in it for you?**

* Join one of Australia’s largest and most complex technology environments, protecting digital, cloud, mobile and operational technology platforms used by millions of Australians
* Work alongside a highly skilled, diverse and collaborative Cyber Defence team where knowledge sharing and continuous learning are part of everyday work
* Gain exposure to a broad range of technologies, security tools and emerging threats, creating endless opportunities for technical growth and development
* Bring your whole self to work every day and be met by a welcoming bunch of people who respect and support you
* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements, like the opportunity to work from home two days per week
* Opportunities for growth and development through formal programs or mentorship
* Exclusive team member discounts and offers for more cash in your pocket, evolving policies for flexible working, leave types and access to health and wellbeing resources

**All walks, one route**

It takes a lot of us to deliver for every Australian – and it’s important to us that our people behind the parcels reflect the people receiving them. We come from all walks. Different backgrounds, different ages, different genders, different sexualities and different abilities, but we all believe in the same purpose.

We welcome people all ages, genders and backgrounds – including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, LGBTQIA+ communities, and refugees. We’re a Disability Confident Recruiter, committed to making our hiring process and workplace inclusive and barrier-free. We’re also working hard to remove bias and build a gender-equitable experience for everyone who joins us. If you’ve got questions about accessibility, reach out to our Diversity & Inclusion team at inclusivecareers@auspost.com.au or on 03 8737 9415.

jobs.title: Associate Sitecore Developer
jobs.description:
Build and support the digital experiences behind one of Australia’s most loved retail brands.

MECCA is continuing to invest in the technology that powers its customer experience across web, commerce and content. We’re looking for a Junior Sitecore Developer to join the digital technology team and help deliver practical improvements across MECCA’s Sitecore environment. This is a great opportunity for an early-career developer to work with an experienced team, learn a leading enterprise CMS platform, and contribute to customer-facing digital products at real scale.

**The Role You Can Play**

* **Enterprise platform exposure** - build experience across Sitecore and the broader digital technology landscape
* **Customer-facing impact** - contribute to web and content experiences used by MECCA customers every day
* **Learning and growth** - work alongside experienced developers, product owners and digital stakeholders
* **Modern retail technology** - gain exposure to e-commerce, content management, integrations and digital delivery
* **Supportive team environment** - join a collaborative team where you can ask questions, build confidence and keep developing your craft
* **Recognised brand** - be part of one of Australia’s most distinctive and fast-growing retail businesses

**Key Responsibilities Include**

* Building and updating Sitecore components, templates, layouts and content-driven features
* Supporting the development, maintenance and enhancement of MECCA’s Sitecore platform
* Troubleshooting defects, small enhancements and continuous improvement across digital channels
* Working with senior developers to understand requirements and turn them into practical technical changes
* Helping test, validate and document changes before they move through release
* Working with product, digital, content and technology teams to support a high-quality customer experience

**What You Will Bring**

* Some hands-on experience in software development, ideally using .NET / C#, JavaScript, HTML and CSS
* Understanding of modern web development fundamentals, including responsive web and front-end basics
* Comfortable working with Git or a similar source control tool

jobs.title: Senior DevSecOps Engineer (AWS)
jobs.description:
##### **About us**

FrankieOne is solving one of the largest problems in financial services, legacy identity infrastructure. Onboarding end-consumers for banks, crypto companies and telcos has historically been painful for everyone involved. It's a massive global problem, and FrankieOne exists to fix it.

We're a VC-backed, product-led global fintech that has connected over 300 global identity and fraud providers into a single platform, delivering a unified API, a unified view, and one damn fine onboarding experience.

Our infrastructure powers tier 1 banks, global BNPL players, the majority of neobanks in Australia, and some of the fastest-growing fintechs in the world. Today we operate in 46 countries and we're continuing to scale rapidly.

##### **We are an AI-first company**

This isn't a line we put in the ad to look current. Our engineering teams run Claude Code every day, we lean heavily into spec-driven development, and we build our own tooling and MCP servers so agents can reach the systems they need. We want someone who is genuinely excited about this shift, has opinions about where agents help and where they fall over, and wants to push how far we can take it.

##### **Who we are looking for**

We're looking for a Senior DevSecOps Engineer to join our small, high-impact team. This isn't a role where you blend into the background. On a small team, everything you do is amplified.

Banks and other security-conscious organisations trust us with sensitive data. The security, stability and reliability of our operations is paramount.

You're comfortable owning a piece of work end to end, asking questions when the path isn't obvious, and making sensible calls without waiting to be told. You'll have a Lead who backs you, reviews your thinking and gives you room to grow.

You're also happy to get your hands dirty. Wrangling Lambda functions, writing Terraform, and helping design and build infrastructure for major new service capabilities.

##### **You have**

* At least 3 years building and running secure, highly available web applications and integration services in AWS.
* Hands-on experience with containerised services in AWS ECS, covering setup, security, management and monitoring.
* Solid working knowledge of Terraform.
* A good grasp of AWS networking fundamentals.
* Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions or similar.
* Confident scripting in at least one of Python, TypeScript or Bash.
* Experience with observability and monitoring platforms.
* Comfort working in Linux environments day to day.
* Real experience using coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex on production work.
* AWS certifications highly regarded, for example DevOps Engineer or Solutions Architect.

##### **Nice to haves**

* Experience with spec-driven development.
* Experience building MCP servers or other agent tooling.
* Experience with autonomous sandboxed coding agents.
* Experience with Cloudflare.
* Experience with Kubernetes.
* An interest in platform engineering and developer experience.

##### **You will**

* Own projects through to delivery, working closely with the DevSecOps Lead on scope and approach.
* Use agents heavily in your own work, and help the rest of engineering do the same by building the tooling, guardrails and patterns that make it safe.
* Work with team members and product owners to solve operational issues and build automation and improvements.
* Manage end-to-end deployment processes and maintain our CI/CD practices alongside the development team.
* Work with our security function on implementation and remediation, tightening controls, implementing policies and improving our security posture.
* Keep improving the service and technology stack.
* Work closely with the DevSecOps Lead, VP of Engineering and Head of Security.
* Participate in on-call rotation, one week in every six, remunerated.

##### **What success looks like**

First month: full induction. You'll understand the company culture, the product, the codebase and your team. You'll have all the tools you need, including your AI tooling set up the way you like it, and we'll aim to have you making your first meaningful contribution to production infrastructure inside two weeks.

By 3 months: you've added your own stamp to the infrastructure. You're making real improvements to our infrastructure and security posture, working with less oversight and building trust with the team and wider stakeholders.

By 6 months: you're delivering a significant piece of work from scoping through to production, spotting problems before they bite and bringing solutions to the team. You've found at least one thing an agent should be doing for us that isn't yet, and made it happen.

jobs.description:
**Exhibitions Coordinator, Victorian First Peoples Art and Design Fair**

**Salary:** $100,894 - $114,476 plus superannuation

**Fixed term / Ongoing role:** Fixed term, 6 months

**Usual hours of work:** Full time (flexibility may be available)

**Usual work location:** 121 Exhibition St, Melbourne, VIC (flexibility may be available)

**Aboriginal Designated**

**ONLY ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER PEOPLE ARE ELIGIBLE TO APPLY AS THIS POSITION IS EXEMPT UNDER THE SPECIAL MEASURES PROVISION OF S12(1) OF THE EQUAL OPPORTUNITY ACT (VIC).**

**The Role**

This is a rewarding and challenging opportunity for an experienced Exhibitions Coordinator to support Creative Victoria's First Peoples Art and Design Fair. Working with the Principal Project Manager, you will guide the production and delivery of the biennial art fair and act as a liaison between art centres, collectives, galleries and independent artists. The successful applicant will bring extensive knowledge of Victoria's First Peoples cultural and creative sectors, strong community and sector networks, and high-level stakeholder and project management skills to deliver effective outcomes. The role requires flexibility, including evening and weekend work and occasional overnight travel, as well as travel when required.

**Main Accountabilities**

* Cultural capability and community engagement
* Stakeholder management and partnership building
* Exhibition and event delivery
* Project management and coordination
* Communication and negotiation

**The Team**

The position of Exhibitions Coordinator forms part of the Office of the Chief Executive branch within Creative Victoria.

The Office of the Chief Executive branch has two units, the First Peoples unit and the Communications and Engagement unit, and one team, the Executive Office. The branch supports the Chief Executive in leading Creative Victoria to efficiently and effectively deliver on the priorities of the Department, Minister and Victorian Government. It leads priorities to enhance self-determination and coordination of First Peoples policies and programs in the creative industries portfolio, while raising the profile of Victoria's creative industries and Creative Victoria's initiatives, investments, programs and opportunities.

Creative Victoria is the state government body dedicated to championing, growing and supporting Victoria's creative industries and the benefits they bring to Victorians. Creative Victoria prioritises First Peoples self-determination to strengthen the connection between Victoria's creative industries, Community and Country.

**About You**

You will have demonstrated connection and knowledge of Victorian Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts, culture and the creative sector, with the ability to work respectfully and effectively with artists, Elders, art centres, collectives, galleries and community stakeholders. You will also have demonstrated experience engaging diverse stakeholders, developing productive relationships and mutually beneficial partnerships, responding to stakeholder needs and achieving stakeholder outcomes. Experience in exhibition, arts and event coordination, including planning, managing timelines and competing priorities and budgets, developing systems and procedures, and delivering exhibitions, art fairs, cultural events or related projects will be highly valued.

**Further Information**

For a confidential discussion, please contact **Troy Walsh, Director First Peoples** on **0427 341 325** or**troy.walsh@creative.vic.gov.au**.

The Department is committed to creating and maintaining a child safe organisation. We have zero tolerance of child abuse and are committed to taking the necessary steps to protect children from harm by adopting a preventative, proactive and participatory approach to child safety in accordance with the Child Safe Standards.

Successful candidates will be required to undergo a National Police Records Check prior to commencing employment with the Department. For further information on the position, please refer to the attached position description.

Please note: We are committed to inclusive recruitment. If you require an adjustment to participate in any stage of the recruitment process or have a particular requirement to be communicated with by either telephone or email only, please notify the DJSIR Talent Acquisition Team on 0472 875 685, or via email at recruitment@ecodev.vic.gov.au with the position number in the subject line.

**How to Apply**

Please click the `Apply Now' button. **As part of the application process, you will need to provide a copy of your resume and a cover letter.**

In your cover letter, tell us why you want to work with DJSIR and what draws you to this role. We are interested in understanding how your experiences, whether from community, culture or professional settings, have shaped your experience. You may choose to share why this opportunity resonates with you, a story that demonstrates your cultural leadership and problem-solving approach, how you have created positive change for mob in your community or workplace, or your vision for supporting First Nations staff and cultural safety at DJSIR.

While addressing the key selection criteria, feel free to draw on examples from any setting that show your skills, knowledge and experience. We value both traditional and non-traditional pathways to leadership.

**Applications close at 23:59pm on 9 September 2026.**

**For the purpose of employment in Aboriginal Designated or Aboriginal Prioritised positions within the Victorian public sector, candidates will be asked to provide Confirmation of Aboriginality. This can be confirmed by a Confirmation of Aboriginality form signed by an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation and affixed with the common seal of that organisation. Recognising that access to formal Confirmation of Aboriginality documents can occasionally be problematic, an alternative process can be discussed by emailing** **firstpeoples.workforce@ecodev.vic.gov.au****.**

jobs.title: Classroom Teacher- English - Start 2027
jobs.description:
**Overview**

**Work Type:** Fixed-term - Full-time

**Salary:** Salary not specified

**Grade:** Classroom Teacher

**Occupation:** Classroom teacher

**Location:** Melbourne - Western suburbs

**Reference:** 1537045

### **Selection Criteria**

**SC1** Demonstrated knowledge of the relevant curriculum, including the ability to incorporate the teaching of literacy and numeracy skills. Demonstrated experience in responding to student learning needs.

**SC2** Demonstrated experience in planning for and implementing high impact teaching strategies, guided by how students learn, and evaluating the impact of learning and teaching programs on student learning growth.

**SC3** Demonstrated experience in monitoring and assessing student learning. Demonstrated experience in using data to inform teaching practice and providing feedback on student learning growth and achievement to students and parents.

**SC4** Demonstrated interpersonal and communication skills. Demonstrated experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with students, parents, colleagues and the broader school community to support student learning, agency, wellbeing and engagement.

**SC5** Demonstrated behaviours and attitudes consistent with Department values. Demonstrated experience in reflecting upon practice and engaging in professional learning to continually improve the quality of teaching.

### **Role**

The classroom teacher classification comprises two salary ranges- range 1 and range 2. The primary focus of the classroom teacher is on the planning, preparation and teaching of programs to achieve specific student outcomes. The classroom teacher engages in critical reflection and inquiry in order to improve knowledge and skills to effectively engage students and improve their learning.

As the classroom teacher gains experience his or her contribution to the school program beyond the classroom increases. All classroom teachers may be required to undertake other duties in addition to their rostered teaching duties provided the responsibility is appropriate to the salary range, qualifications, training and experience of the teacher.

Classroom teacher Range 2

Range 2 classroom teachers play a significant role in assisting the school to improve student performance and educational outcomes determined by the school strategic plan and state-wide priorities and contributing to the development and implementation of school policies and priorities.

A critical component of this work will focus on increasing the knowledge base of staff within their school about student learning and high quality instruction to assist their school to define quality teacher practice.

Range 2 classroom teachers will be expected to:

* Have the content knowledge and pedagogical practice to meet the diverse needs of all students
* Model exemplary classroom practice and mentor/coach other teachers in the school to engage in critical reflection of their practice and to support staff to expand their capacity
* Provide expert advice about the content, processes and strategies that will shape individual and school professional learning
* Supervise and train one or more student teachers
* Assist staff to use student data to inform teaching approaches that enable targets related to improving student learning outcomes to be achieved.

Classroom teacher Range 1

The primary focus of the range 1 classroom teacher is on further developing skills and competencies to become an effective classroom practitioner with structured support and guidance from teachers at higher levels and the planning, preparation and teaching of programs to achieve specific student outcomes. These teachers teach a range of students/classes and are accountable for the effective delivery of their programs. Range 1 classroom teachers are skilled teachers who operate under general direction within clear guidelines following established work practices and documented priorities and may have responsibility for the supervision and training of one or more student teachers.

At range 1, teachers participate in the development of school policies and programs and assist in the implementation of school priorities.

The focus of a range 1 classroom teacher is on classroom management, subject content and teaching practice. New entrants to the teaching profession in their initial teaching years receive structured support, mentoring and guidance from teachers at higher levels.

Under guidance, new entrants to the teaching profession will plan and teach student groups in one or more subjects and are expected to participate in induction programs and other professional learning activities that are designed to ensure the integration of curriculum, assessment and pedagogy across the school.

Teachers at range 1 are responsible for teaching their own classes and may also assist and participate in policy development, project teams and the organisation of co-curricula activities.

### **Responsibilities**

The role of classroom teacher may include but is not limited to:

* Direct teaching of groups of students and individual students;
* Contributing to the development, implementation and evaluation of a curriculum area or other curriculum program within the school;
* Undertaking other classroom teaching related and organisational duties as determined by the School Principal;
* Participating in activities such as parent/teacher meetings; staff meetings; camps and excursions;
* Undertaking other non-teaching supervisory duties.

### **Who May Apply**

Teachers currently registered or eligible for registration with the Victorian Institute of Teaching and qualified to teach and/or have demonstrated experience in the curriculum area(s) specified for the position.

### **Diversity and Inclusion**

The department is committed to diversity and inclusion and developing a workforce that is representative of the community we service. We value diversity and inclusion in all forms - culture, gender, religion, ethnicity, LGBTIQA+, disability and neurodiversity. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for roles within the Department. The Department recognises that the provision of safe, respectful and inclusive workplaces is essential to high performance and promotes flexible work and diversity across all schools and Department workplaces. It is our policy to provide reasonable adjustments for staff with disability (see Workplace adjustment guidelines).

Additional support and advice on the recruitment process is available to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander candidates from the Koorie Outcomes Division (KOD) via [email protected]

Applicants seeking part-time employment are encouraged to apply for any teaching service position and, if they are the successful candidate, request a reduced time fraction. Such requests will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis and will be subject to the operational requirements of the school.

### **Child Safe Standards**

Victorian government schools are child safe environments. Our schools actively promote the safety and wellbeing of all students, and all school staff are committed to protecting students from abuse or harm in the school environment, in accordance with their legal obligations including child safe standards. All schools have a Child Safety Code of Conduct consistent with the department's exemplar available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/child-safe-standards/policy

### **DE Values**

The department's employees commit to upholding the department's Values: Responsiveness, Integrity, Impartiality, Accountability, Respect, Leadership and Human Rights. The department's Values complement each school's own values and underpin the behaviours the community expects of Victorian public sector employees, including those who work in Victorian Government Schools. Information on the department values is available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/values-department-vps-school-employees/overview

### **Other Information**

* **This is a multi campus college and travel between campuses may be required.**
* **Please submit responses to Selection Criteria with your application**
* **A probationary period of 3 months will apply**

### **Conditions of Employment**

All staff employed by the Department and schools have access to a broad range of employment conditions and working arrangements.

* Appointment of successful applicants will be made subject to a satisfactory pre-employment conditions check.
* **Probationary period of 3 months will apply during the first 12 months of employment**
* Induction and support programs provided.

Detailed information on all terms and conditions of employment is available on the Department's Human Resources website at http://www.education.vic.gov.au/hrweb/Pages/default.aspx

### **Qualification Requirements**

To be eligible for employment, transfer or promotion in the principal or teacher class:

* The person must have provisional or full registration approved by the Victorian Institute of Teaching; and
* if the person completed an Australian postgraduate level initial teaching program or course of study on or after 1 January 2024, they must demonstrate that they have satisfactorily completed a postgraduate level accredited initial teacher education program that has been accredited by an Australian State or Territory Teacher Regulatory Authority as satisfying the requirements of the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership 'Accreditation of initial teacher education programs in Australia: Standards and Procedures'; and
* a person who graduated from a Victorian Initial Teacher Education (ITE) program after 1 July 2016 must also demonstrate that they have passed the literacy and numeracy test for initial teacher education (LANTITE) requirements (this condition is satisfied where the LANTITE requirement is part of the Victorian ITE program completed by the person).

Details of qualification requirements as updated from time to time can be found at Recruitment in Schools.

### **Location Profile**

Victoria University Secondary College is a multi campus school, comprising of a Junior Campus located in Deer Park, a Senior Campus with a Trade Training Centre located in Cairnlea and a Flexible Learning Option - iCAN centre located in St Albans. Our college has approximately 1500 students from years 7 to 12 and services the residential area of Cairnlea, Deer Park, St Albans and environs in the western suburbs of Melbourne. Our college provides a broad range of personal, academic and practical experiences for our students who come form diverse cultural and social backgrounds. Victoria University Secondary College challenges students to, **Create the Future** by adhering to our school values of **Aspiring to Achieve**, S**trengthening the Community** and R**especting Themselves and Others**.

jobs.title: Retail Manager
jobs.description:
About the Role

Smolbitez Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced and motivated **Retail Manager** to oversee the day-to-day operations of our growing retail food business in Melbourne.

The successful candidate will be responsible for managing store operations, supervising staff, monitoring stock levels, coordinating suppliers, maintaining customer service standards, and supporting the development and growth of the business.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage and coordinate the daily operations of the retail store.
* Supervise, train and support retail staff to ensure efficient store operations.
* Prepare staff rosters and coordinate staffing requirements.
* Monitor sales performance, customer service and overall store performance.
* Conduct regular **stock level checks** and ensure sufficient inventory is maintained.
* Manage stock ordering, receiving, storage and inventory control.
* Monitor stock usage, wastage and product availability.
* Coordinate with suppliers and manage supplier relationships.
* Research and identify potential new products, ingredients and suppliers.
* Assist with **new product research, development and testing** to expand the company's product range.
* Research market trends and customer preferences to identify new product opportunities.
* Maintain high standards of product quality, presentation, cleanliness and customer service.
* Monitor operating costs and assist in improving business efficiency.
* Handle customer enquiries, feedback and complaints professionally.
* Ensure workplace health, safety and food safety procedures are followed.
* Assist with promotional activities and initiatives to improve sales performance.
* Maintain operational records and provide reports to management.
* Assist management with business development and continuous improvement initiatives.

Essential Skills and Experience

The successful candidate must have:

* **A minimum of 2 years' retail management experience is essential.**
* Previous experience supervising and managing retail staff.
* Experience in stock control, inventory management and supplier coordination.
* Strong understanding of retail store operations and customer service.
* Experience with staff rostering and workforce coordination.
* Strong communication, organisational and time-management skills.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced retail environment.
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
* Understanding of workplace health, safety and food safety requirements.
* Ability to research market trends and evaluate new product opportunities.
* Experience or demonstrated ability in **new product research and development** is highly regarded.
* **Established supplier networks or sourcing resources in Malaysia are highly regarded**, particularly for Malaysian food products, ingredients and related products.

What We Offer

* Full-time position.
* Annual salary of **AUD $80,000 + superannuation**.
* Opportunity to work in a growing Australian food retail business.
* Supportive and professional working environment.
* Opportunity to take responsibility for retail operations, product development and business growth.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume outlining your relevant qualifications, skills and **retail management experience**, including experience in stock management, supplier coordination and product development where applicable.

Pay: $80,000.00 per year

Work Location: In person

Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. We bring together the talent of our approximately 786,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep process and industry expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships to deliver end-to-end solutions and measurable outcomes at scale. Through our Reinvention Services, we offer broad expertise across Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent, with advanced capabilities in AI and Data, Industry and Process, and Technology. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $70 billion in FY25 revenue. Visit us at **www.accenture.com**.

The **HSE Manager – Client Site Safety & Programs** provides regional and portfolio level leadership for client site and offsite Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) programs. This role bridges field execution and enterprise strategy by translating Accenture HSE standards, client contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements into consistent, scalable, and auditable field implementation

The role owns program deployment, regional oversight, and performance management while providing escalation support and technical leadership for higher risk or complex client engagements.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Program Deployment & Oversight**

* Deploy and operationalize client site and offsite HSE programs across assigned regions, accounts, or portfolios.
* Translate enterprise HSE standards and client safety requirements into practical field execution guidance.
* Ensure consistent implementation of audits, inspections, training validation, and incident response processes.
* Own defined program elements such as training governance, contractor safety controls, and site readiness processes.

**Regional / Portfolio Leadership**

* Serve as the primary escalation point for HSE Leads and site level safety resources.
* Provide technical direction, coaching, and quality assurance for audits, investigations, and corrective actions.
* Prioritize resources and support based on risk, client exposure, and incident trends.
* Step into client facing or field roles for high risk, high visibility, or escalated engagements.

**Incident & Emergency Management**

* Lead or oversee complex incident investigations and ensure effective root cause analysis and closure.
* Review incident trends, audit results, and near miss data to identify systemic risks.
* Drive corrective and preventive action plans and verify effectiveness.
* Support Stop Work Authority decisions and client escalations when required.

**Training & Site Readiness Governance**

* Own governance of training, authorization, and site readiness requirements across assigned scope.
* Ensure employees, subcontractors, and vendors meet client and regulatory requirements prior to mobilization.
* Validate training effectiveness and competency, not just completion.
* Partner with central HSE teams to ensure training functions as a risk control mechanism.

**Client & Stakeholder Engagement**

* Act as an HSE lead for assigned client accounts or regions.
* Support interpretation and implementation of client safety requirements and contractual obligations.
* Partner with Legal, HR, Procurement, and Global HSE on complex or ambiguous requirements.
* Represent Accenture in client audits, safety reviews, and joint investigations as needed.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Identify gaps and inconsistencies in field execution and recommend program improvements.
* Contribute to development of global tools, templates, and guidance.
* Support integration of acquisitions or new service offerings into existing HSE programs.
* Champion continuous improvement and safety culture maturity across regions.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent field experience in HSE, Industrial Hygiene, or a related discipline.
* 7-10 years of progressive HSE experience with direct field or client site work.
* Demonstrated experience leading regional programs, portfolios, or multi site operations
* Strong working knowledge of relevant, applicable safety regulations
* Working knowledge of ISNetworld, Avetta, ComplyWorks platforms.
* Proven experience leading audits, investigations, and corrective action programs
* Professional certification (CSP (or international equivalent such as Chartered OHS Professional (Australia), CMIOSH (UK), or NEBOSH International Diploma)
* Experience supporting high risk industries or complex client environments
* Strong client facing communication and escalation management skills

If you require any accommodations or adjustments for interviews and/or at work, please reach out to exectalent@accenture.com or contact us at +61 2 9005 5000 (Australia) or +64 44666056 (New Zealand).

**Overview**

**Work Type:** Fixed-term - Part-time

**Salary:** Salary not specified

**Grade:** Education Support - Level 1, Range 2

**Occupation:** Education and training

**Location:** Melbourne - Northern suburbs

**Reference:** 1540397

### **Location Profile**

Northcote High is a vibrant co-educational school in the inner north of Melbourne. The school has a rich intellectual culture that promotes connection with the community and with learning. Northcote High is a proudly local school appreciated by its community with an enrolment of almost 1700 students and 150 staff.

Our teachers explicit focus on classroom instruction, on building relationships and on knowing students as learners is fundamental to maintaining outstanding outcomes for students. We are focused on creating the conditions for success through a commitment to shared practice, reflective collegial work and implementing the schools agreed frameworks to support and extend all learners. Teachers as learners is an integral part of our vision and values, and we provide a comprehensive school led professional learning and enrichment program. The expertise and dedication of the staff is undoubtedly a strength of the school and our goal to be an employer of choice is supported by the range of development opportunities we seek for our staff.

In 2026 the school is celebrating its centenary and being one of only a few public high schools to continuously offer an excellent secondary education throughout this time. We remain steadfastly focused on maintaining a tradition of academic excellence, whilst developing innovative teaching and learning programs to equip our students with the skills required for a changing future. Our vibrant co-curricular programs provide valuable opportunities for students to learn, grow and build community in and beyond the school. International engagement is also a feature of the school. We celebrate a sister school program in China for over 25 years, and a vibrant international student program.

Key documents for applicants such as our Teaching and Learning Framework, curriculum models, AIP and Strategic Plan can be viewed on our school website.

For more information visit www.nhs.vic.edu.au

### **Selection Criteria**

**SC1** Demonstrated capacity to perform duties consistent with established guidelines and frameworks, including coordinating and supporting others in respect to specific work functions relevant to the role.

**SC2** Demonstrated capacity to work and collaborate with others in a team environment.

**SC3** Demonstrated capacity to communicate effectively in a team environment, including high level oral and written communication skills.

**SC4** Possess the technical knowledge and expertise relevant to the position.

**SC5** Demonstrated capacity to provide advice and support to management and other school staff in respect to the work area.

**SC6** A commitment to professional learning and growth for both self and others.

### **Role**

An education support class position at this range will perform tasks that are carried out in accordance with guidelines, accepted practice, and school policy under supervision and direction. This may include coordination of other education support class staff within the work area or educational program.

An education support class position supports the educational services being provided to students but must not include duties of a teacher as defined in clause 2.6.1 of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006 (Vic) or its successor. Supervision of students can be required individually or in groups up to 4 in controlled circumstances and where the responsibility for students remains clearly with a teacher.

Certification and/or qualifications of up to three years can be required at this level (noting that Registered Nurse is not included at this level, the first level for which is Level 1 range 3).

A role at this range may include:

* Specific support tasks to achieve outcomes. Typically, this will involve accountability for a single function, (e.g. ensuring data is properly maintained) or the co-ordination of a work area under the direction of the principal or a manager.
* Assisting teachers, within an educational program, by undertaking specific support tasks or the coordination of the support function.
* Supervised health and wellbeing support tasks, medical intervention support tasks, or other specialised student/teacher support roles (e.g. enrolled nurses performing the role as described in schedule 3). These roles require specific qualifications and/or training, including roles where further training must be undertaken from time to time. The role is for a specific purpose, for which there will be direct accountability as opposed to support roles that are carried out by a range of staff performing routine tasks under direction.
* Technical tasks that require a sound knowledge of basic technical and/or scientific principles that are used to develop and adapt work methods and make judgements where there are clear guidelines and limited options. Routine technical support in libraries, science, and information technology would be typical examples.

An education support class position at this range commencing at the base will initially be limited to undertaking routine tasks that are carried out under close supervision and direction. Work that carries some degree of independence will generally involve a limited number of tasks performed on a regular basis where priorities are clear, procedures are well established, and direction is readily available. Subject to any specific qualification and/or training requirement, an education support class employee employed in this range may be progressively required to undertake coordination, specialised student/teacher support tasks, or technical tasks as experience in the role is gained.

### **Responsibilities**

* Provide routine clerical or other administrative support responsibilities including general telephone, front office enquiries, mail deliveries, assisting with stock control, supporting organisation of meetings, receiving and initial processing of standard paperwork
* Maintain, enter and retrieve data from the schools IT systems, such as the school's records system, including computerised student, staff and school records
* Maintain and update office records, enrolment data, diary records, and basic written records
* Support or coordinate the preparation of standard routine internal and external communication according to school procedures (e.g. form letters, newsletters)
* Source basic data or factual information from given sources to support school administrative functions, e.g. books, reports, manuals, catalogues, tables, forms, etc.
* Coordinate the delivery of administrative services within the school
* In consultation with the principal, determine and manage work priorities within the school office
* Develop and implement strategies to ensure effective administration procedures
* Coordinate the implementation of requisitioning, purchasing and issuing procedures
* Manage client reception and office operations
* Liaise with school staff in regard to support requirements
* Coordinate staff timetabling
* Undertakes VASS and/or VET administration support
* Supports the first aid facilities and assists in delivering first aid to students

### **Who May Apply**

Individuals with the aptitude, experience and/or qualifications to fulfill the specific requirements of the position.

### **Diversity and Inclusion**

The department is committed to diversity and inclusion and developing a workforce that is representative of the community we service. We value diversity and inclusion in all forms - culture, gender, religion, ethnicity, LGBTIQA+, disability and neurodiversity. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for roles within the Department. The Department recognises that the provision of safe, respectful and inclusive workplaces is essential to high performance and promotes flexible work and diversity across all schools and Department workplaces. It is our policy to provide reasonable adjustments for staff with disability (see Workplace adjustment guidelines).

Additional support and advice on the recruitment process is available to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander candidates from the Koorie Outcomes Division (KOD) via [email protected]

Applicants seeking part-time employment are encouraged to apply for any teaching service position and, if they are the successful candidate, request a reduced time fraction. Such requests will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis and will be subject to the operational requirements of the school.

### **Child Safe Standards**

Victorian government schools are child safe environments. Our schools actively promote the safety and wellbeing of all students, and all school staff are committed to protecting students from abuse or harm in the school environment, in accordance with their legal obligations including child safe standards. All schools have a Child Safety Code of Conduct consistent with the department's exemplar available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/child-safe-standards/policy

### **DE Values**

The department's employees commit to upholding the department's Values: Responsiveness, Integrity, Impartiality, Accountability, Respect, Leadership and Human Rights. The department's Values complement each school's own values and underpin the behaviours the community expects of Victorian public sector employees, including those who work in Victorian Government Schools. Information on the department values is available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/values-department-vps-school-employees/overview

### **Other Information**

* **Written Applications**
* Applicants are free to structure applications in any manner they choose, but must ensure that the following are included:
* A specific response to all of the Key Selection Criteria and position details. It is suggested that applicants limit their response to no more than 1 page (size 11) per criterion.
* A Cover Letter providing contact information including home address, email and phone number as well as the phone number of the work address at which the applicant can be contacted.
* A CV with a summary of experience and qualifications.
* The names, email addresses and contact details of three referees who can provide information regarding the applicant in relation to the Key Selection Criteria **MUST** be listed on your CV.

Please note: The selection panel may contact referees other than those listed.
* **The Selection Process will involve at least the following steps:**
* Shortlisting of applications
* Interview process (applicants may be invited back for a second interview)
* Referee checks (these may occur prior and/or after the interviews)
* Note: the panel reserves the right to contact others outside of the list of referees provided by the applicant.
* On making a decision to appoint, a job offer will be made to the successful applicant.

### **Conditions of Employment**

* All staff employed by the Department and schools have access to a broad range of employment conditions and working arrangements.
* Appointment of successful applicants will be made subject to a satisfactory pre-employment conditions check.
* A probationary period may apply during the first year of employment and induction and support programs provided.
* Detailed information on all terms and conditions of employment is available on the Department's Human Resources website at http://www.education.vic.gov.au/hrweb/Pages/default.aspx

**SC6** A commitment to professional learning and growth for both self and others.

### **Role**

An education support class position at this range will perform tasks that are carried out in accordance with guidelines, accepted practice, and school policy under supervision and direction. This may include coordination of other education support class staff within the work area or educational program.

An education support class position supports the educational services being provided to students but must not include duties of a teacher as defined in clause 2.6.1 of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006 (Vic) or its successor. Supervision of students can be required individually or in groups up to 4 in controlled circumstances and where the responsibility for students remains clearly with a teacher.

Certification and/or qualifications of up to three years can be required at this level (noting that Registered Nurse is not included at this level, the first level for which is Level 1 range 3).

A role at this range may include:

* Specific support tasks to achieve outcomes. Typically, this will involve accountability for a single function, (e.g. ensuring data is properly maintained) or the co-ordination of a work area under the direction of the principal or a manager.
* Assisting teachers, within an educational program, by undertaking specific support tasks or the coordination of the support function.
* Supervised health and wellbeing support tasks, medical intervention support tasks, or other specialised student/teacher support roles (e.g. enrolled nurses performing the role as described in schedule 3). These roles require specific qualifications and/or training, including roles where further training must be undertaken from time to time. The role is for a specific purpose, for which there will be direct accountability as opposed to support roles that are carried out by a range of staff performing routine tasks under direction.
* Technical tasks that require a sound knowledge of basic technical and/or scientific principles that are used to develop and adapt work methods and make judgements where there are clear guidelines and limited options. Routine technical support in libraries, science, and information technology would be typical examples.

An education support class position at this range commencing at the base will initially be limited to undertaking routine tasks that are carried out under close supervision and direction. Work that carries some degree of independence will generally involve a limited number of tasks performed on a regular basis where priorities are clear, procedures are well established, and direction is readily available. * Experience supporting students with autism and/or complex communication needs, including the use of visual supports and Alternative and Augmentative Communication (AAC) systems.

**Overview**

### **Selection Criteria**

**SC1** Demonstrated knowledge of the relevant curriculum, including the ability to incorporate the teaching of literacy and numeracy skills. Demonstrated experience in responding to student learning needs.

**SC2** Demonstrated experience in planning for and implementing high impact teaching strategies, guided by how students learn, and evaluating the impact of learning and teaching programs on student learning growth.

**SC3** Demonstrated experience in monitoring and assessing student learning. Demonstrated experience in using data to inform teaching practice and providing feedback on student learning growth and achievement to students and parents.

**SC4** Demonstrated interpersonal and communication skills. Demonstrated experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with students, parents, colleagues and the broader school community to support student learning, agency, wellbeing and engagement.

**SC5** Demonstrated behaviours and attitudes consistent with Department values. Demonstrated experience in reflecting upon practice and engaging in professional learning to continually improve the quality of teaching.

### **Role**

The classroom teacher classification comprises two salary ranges- range 1 and range 2. The primary focus of the classroom teacher is on the planning, preparation and teaching of programs to achieve specific student outcomes. The classroom teacher engages in critical reflection and inquiry in order to improve knowledge and skills to effectively engage students and improve their learning.

As the classroom teacher gains experience his or her contribution to the school program beyond the classroom increases. All classroom teachers may be required to undertake other duties in addition to their rostered teaching duties provided the responsibility is appropriate to the salary range, qualifications, training and experience of the teacher.

Classroom teacher Range 2

Range 2 classroom teachers play a significant role in assisting the school to improve student performance and educational outcomes determined by the school strategic plan and state-wide priorities and contributing to the development and implementation of school policies and priorities.

A critical component of this work will focus on increasing the knowledge base of staff within their school about student learning and high quality instruction to assist their school to define quality teacher practice.

Range 2 classroom teachers will be expected to:

* Have the content knowledge and pedagogical practice to meet the diverse needs of all students
* Model exemplary classroom practice and mentor/coach other teachers in the school to engage in critical reflection of their practice and to support staff to expand their capacity
* Provide expert advice about the content, processes and strategies that will shape individual and school professional learning
* Supervise and train one or more student teachers
* Assist staff to use student data to inform teaching approaches that enable targets related to improving student learning outcomes to be achieved.

Classroom teacher Range 1

The primary focus of the range 1 classroom teacher is on further developing skills and competencies to become an effective classroom practitioner with structured support and guidance from teachers at higher levels and the planning, preparation and teaching of programs to achieve specific student outcomes. These teachers teach a range of students/classes and are accountable for the effective delivery of their programs. Range 1 classroom teachers are skilled teachers who operate under general direction within clear guidelines following established work practices and documented priorities and may have responsibility for the supervision and training of one or more student teachers.

At range 1, teachers participate in the development of school policies and programs and assist in the implementation of school priorities.

The focus of a range 1 classroom teacher is on classroom management, subject content and teaching practice. New entrants to the teaching profession in their initial teaching years receive structured support, mentoring and guidance from teachers at higher levels.

Under guidance, new entrants to the teaching profession will plan and teach student groups in one or more subjects and are expected to participate in induction programs and other professional learning activities that are designed to ensure the integration of curriculum, assessment and pedagogy across the school.

Teachers at range 1 are responsible for teaching their own classes and may also assist and participate in policy development, project teams and the organisation of co-curricula activities.

The role of classroom teacher may include but is not limited to:

* Direct teaching of groups of students and individual students;
* Contributing to the development, implementation and evaluation of a curriculum area or other curriculum program within the school;
* Undertaking other classroom teaching related and organisational duties as determined by the School Principal;
* Participating in activities such as parent/teacher meetings; staff meetings; camps and excursions;
* Undertaking other non-teaching supervisory duties.

Teachers currently registered or eligible for registration with the Victorian Institute of Teaching and qualified to teach and/or have demonstrated experience in the curriculum area(s) specified for the position.

The department is committed to diversity and inclusion and developing a workforce that is representative of the community we service. We value diversity and inclusion in all forms - culture, gender, religion, ethnicity, LGBTIQA+, disability and neurodiversity. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for roles within the Department. Victorian government schools are child safe environments. ### **Other Information**

All staff employed by the Department and schools have access to a broad range of employment conditions and working arrangements.

* Induction and support programs provided.

Detailed information on all terms and conditions of employment is available on the Department's Human Resources website at http://www.education.vic.gov.au/hrweb/Pages/default.aspx

### **Qualification Requirements**

To be eligible for employment, transfer or promotion in the principal or teacher class:

* The person must have provisional or full registration approved by the Victorian Institute of Teaching; and
* if the person completed an Australian postgraduate level initial teaching program or course of study on or after 1 January 2024, they must demonstrate that they have satisfactorily completed a postgraduate level accredited initial teacher education program that has been accredited by an Australian State or Territory Teacher Regulatory Authority as satisfying the requirements of the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership 'Accreditation of initial teacher education programs in Australia: Standards and Procedures'; and

Details of qualification requirements as updated from time to time can be found at Recruitment in Schools.

Victoria University Secondary College is a Professional Learning Community (PLC) school. PLC schools approach to learning, is to share ideas, enhance teaching practices and create an environment where all students can reach their full potential.

Victoria University Secondary College empowers members of our learning community to develop control over their own thinking and actions. Our college encourages our members to develop self belief and confidence to persevere with their learning challenges. Victoria University Secondary College focusses on reflective thinking and collaboration. This college focus encourages our students to become independent learners, work collaboratively and share ideas and resources while respecting and recognising individual contributions our accelerated students in programs such as AVID (Advance via Individual Determination), Deep Learning and SEAL, Music and we are also a rugby academy school.
