jobs.title: 2027 Ongoing - Classroom Teacher
jobs.description:
**Overview**

**Work Type:** Ongoing - Full-time

**Salary:** Salary not specified

**Grade:** Classroom Teacher

**Occupation:** Classroom teacher

**Location:** Melbourne - Western suburbs

**Reference:** 1540401

### **Selection Criteria**

**SC1** Demonstrated knowledge of the relevant curriculum, including the ability to incorporate the teaching of literacy and numeracy skills. Demonstrated experience in responding to student learning needs.

**SC2** Demonstrated experience in planning for and implementing high impact teaching strategies, guided by how students learn, and evaluating the impact of learning and teaching programs on student learning growth.

**SC3** Demonstrated experience in monitoring and assessing student learning. Demonstrated experience in using data to inform teaching practice and providing feedback on student learning growth and achievement to students and parents.

**SC4** Demonstrated interpersonal and communication skills. Demonstrated experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with students, parents, colleagues and the broader school community to support student learning, agency, wellbeing and engagement.

**SC5** Demonstrated behaviours and attitudes consistent with Department values. Demonstrated experience in reflecting upon practice and engaging in professional learning to continually improve the quality of teaching.

### **Role**

The classroom teacher classification comprises two salary ranges- range 1 and range 2. The primary focus of the classroom teacher is on the planning, preparation and teaching of programs to achieve specific student outcomes. The classroom teacher engages in critical reflection and inquiry in order to improve knowledge and skills to effectively engage students and improve their learning.

As the classroom teacher gains experience his or her contribution to the school program beyond the classroom increases. All classroom teachers may be required to undertake other duties in addition to their rostered teaching duties provided the responsibility is appropriate to the salary range, qualifications, training and experience of the teacher.

Classroom teacher Range 2

Range 2 classroom teachers play a significant role in assisting the school to improve student performance and educational outcomes determined by the school strategic plan and state-wide priorities and contributing to the development and implementation of school policies and priorities.

A critical component of this work will focus on increasing the knowledge base of staff within their school about student learning and high quality instruction to assist their school to define quality teacher practice.

Range 2 classroom teachers will be expected to:

* Have the content knowledge and pedagogical practice to meet the diverse needs of all students
* Model exemplary classroom practice and mentor/coach other teachers in the school to engage in critical reflection of their practice and to support staff to expand their capacity
* Provide expert advice about the content, processes and strategies that will shape individual and school professional learning
* Supervise and train one or more student teachers
* Assist staff to use student data to inform teaching approaches that enable targets related to improving student learning outcomes to be achieved.

Classroom teacher Range 1

The primary focus of the range 1 classroom teacher is on further developing skills and competencies to become an effective classroom practitioner with structured support and guidance from teachers at higher levels and the planning, preparation and teaching of programs to achieve specific student outcomes. These teachers teach a range of students/classes and are accountable for the effective delivery of their programs. Range 1 classroom teachers are skilled teachers who operate under general direction within clear guidelines following established work practices and documented priorities and may have responsibility for the supervision and training of one or more student teachers.

At range 1, teachers participate in the development of school policies and programs and assist in the implementation of school priorities.

The focus of a range 1 classroom teacher is on classroom management, subject content and teaching practice. New entrants to the teaching profession in their initial teaching years receive structured support, mentoring and guidance from teachers at higher levels.

Under guidance, new entrants to the teaching profession will plan and teach student groups in one or more subjects and are expected to participate in induction programs and other professional learning activities that are designed to ensure the integration of curriculum, assessment and pedagogy across the school.

Teachers at range 1 are responsible for teaching their own classes and may also assist and participate in policy development, project teams and the organisation of co-curricula activities.

### **Responsibilities**

The role of classroom teacher may include but is not limited to:

* Direct teaching of groups of students and individual students;
* Contributing to the development, implementation and evaluation of a curriculum area or other curriculum program within the school;
* Undertaking other classroom teaching related and organisational duties as determined by the School Principal;
* Participating in activities such as parent/teacher meetings; staff meetings; camps and excursions;
* Undertaking other non-teaching supervisory duties.

### **Who May Apply**

Teachers currently registered or eligible for registration with the Victorian Institute of Teaching and qualified to teach and/or have demonstrated experience in the curriculum area(s) specified for the position.

### **Diversity and Inclusion**

The department is committed to diversity and inclusion and developing a workforce that is representative of the community we service. We value diversity and inclusion in all forms - culture, gender, religion, ethnicity, LGBTIQA+, disability and neurodiversity. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for roles within the Department. The Department recognises that the provision of safe, respectful and inclusive workplaces is essential to high performance and promotes flexible work and diversity across all schools and Department workplaces. It is our policy to provide reasonable adjustments for staff with disability (see Workplace adjustment guidelines).

Additional support and advice on the recruitment process is available to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander candidates from the Koorie Outcomes Division (KOD) via [email protected]

Applicants seeking part-time employment are encouraged to apply for any teaching service position and, if they are the successful candidate, request a reduced time fraction. Such requests will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis and will be subject to the operational requirements of the school.

### **Child Safe Standards**

Victorian government schools are child safe environments. Our schools actively promote the safety and wellbeing of all students, and all school staff are committed to protecting students from abuse or harm in the school environment, in accordance with their legal obligations including child safe standards. All schools have a Child Safety Code of Conduct consistent with the department's exemplar available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/child-safe-standards/policy

### **DE Values**

The department's employees commit to upholding the department's Values: Responsiveness, Integrity, Impartiality, Accountability, Respect, Leadership and Human Rights. The department's Values complement each school's own values and underpin the behaviours the community expects of Victorian public sector employees, including those who work in Victorian Government Schools. Information on the department values is available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/values-department-vps-school-employees/overview

### **Other Information**

* All staff employed by the department and schools have access to a broad range of employment conditions and working arrangements.
* Appointment of successful applicants will be made subject to a satisfactory pre-employment conditions check.
* A probationary period may apply during the first year of employment and induction and support programs provided.
* Detailed information on all terms and conditions of employment is available on the Department's Human Resources website at http://www.education.vic.gov.au/hrweb/Pages/default.aspx

Please ensure that your application includes:

* A resume including relevant experience as well as personal details (name, address and contact numbers, business and home)
* A section addressing the selection criteria and the requirements for application under the Who May Apply section
* Names and contact numbers (telephone and email if possible) of two referees who are able to attest to the claims made in your application.

Please note that the selection panel may seek additional referees beyond those you name. Consistent with policy, we shall advise you if we will take this action.

### **Conditions of Employment**

* All staff employed by the Department and schools have access to a broad range of employment conditions and working arrangements.
* Appointment of successful applicants will be made subject to a satisfactory pre-employment conditions check.
* A probationary period may apply during the first year of employment and induction and support programs provided.
* Detailed information on all terms and conditions of employment is available on the Department's Human Resources website at http://www.education.vic.gov.au/hrweb/Pages/default.aspx

### **Qualification Requirements**

To be eligible for employment, transfer or promotion in the principal or teacher class:

* The person must have provisional or full registration approved by the Victorian Institute of Teaching; and
* if the person completed an Australian postgraduate level initial teaching program or course of study on or after 1 January 2024, they must demonstrate that they have satisfactorily completed a postgraduate level accredited initial teacher education program that has been accredited by an Australian State or Territory Teacher Regulatory Authority as satisfying the requirements of the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership 'Accreditation of initial teacher education programs in Australia: Standards and Procedures'; and
* a person who graduated from a Victorian Initial Teacher Education (ITE) program after 1 July 2016 must also demonstrate that they have passed the literacy and numeracy test for initial teacher education (LANTITE) requirements (this condition is satisfied where the LANTITE requirement is part of the Victorian ITE program completed by the person).

Details of qualification requirements as updated from time to time can be found at Recruitment in Schools.

### **Location Profile**

**IF YOU BELIEVE THAT STAFF WELLBEING AND A POSITIVE WORKPLACE SHOULD BE A PRIORITY, LOLLYPOP CREEK PS MIGHT JUST BE THE RIGHT EDUCATIONAL SETTING FOR YOU!**

**OUR STAFF OPINION SURVEY RESULTS SPEAKS VOLUMES ABOUT THE POSITIVE CULTURE AND CLIMATE WE HAVE ESTABLISHED AT OUR AMAZING SCHOOL!**

With shared language around wellbeing, and structures and processes to minimise work-related stress in place, all newly appointed teachers will feel supported and become part of a positive and supportive school community.

Lollypop Creek Primary School was established in 2023 and is located approximately 30 kilometres west of Melbourne. Our school has space for 525 local students and is open for enrolments for students in Prep to Grade 6. Our school grounds are bounded by sparkling waterways and situates itself close to Harpley Town Centre. Most students that attend our school live locally and either walk or ride their bike to school. jobs.description:
**Overview**

**Work Type:** Ongoing - Full-time

**Salary:** Salary not specified

**Grade:** Leading Teacher - Range 3

**Occupation:** Leading teacher

**Location:** Melbourne - Southern suburbs

**Reference:** 1540404

### **Location Profile**

Lyndale Secondary College is a vibrant Years 7-12, single-campus educational institution with a diverse student population of over 850. Established in 1961, Lyndale is a cornerstone of its community, known for progressive educational practices, comprehensive pathway management, and a strong commitment to cultural diversity. With more than 40% of students born in 47 different countries and 64 languages spoken at home, Lyndale provides a rich, multicultural learning environment that enhances the experiences of both students and staff.

Central to Lyndale's success is a consistent focus on high expectations across all areas of school life. Guided by our core values of **respect**, **resilience**, and **responsibility**, we foster an environment where students are supported to achieve personal and academic excellence. Respect ensures every student feels valued, resilience inspires them to overcome challenges, and responsibility encourages ownership of their learning and actions.

Our curriculum is broad and inclusive, offering programs such as ACE Program (Advanced Challenge and Enrichment Program), VCE, VCE VM, VPC, and VET, as well as an English Language Centre catering to the unique needs of international and refugee students. Beyond academics, Lyndale boasts a nationally recognised Performing Arts program, vibrant student leadership opportunities, and a culture that celebrates diversity and inclusion, ensuring every student has the opportunity to thrive.

Lyndale's commitment to excellence is evident in our strong academic results. NAPLAN data reflects consistent improvements, while the Attitudes to School Survey (AToSS) highlights student engagement and satisfaction. Staff and parent opinion data further underscore the school's strong sense of community and effective programs.

Our commitment to continuous improvement is reflected in key measures such as Staff Opinion Data, NAPLAN, AToSS, and Parent Opinion Data. These indicate significant growth in areas like school climate, which has shown substantial improvement since 2020 and now exceeds the state average. This progress is also evident in strengthened collective efficacy and collaborative practices among staff, contributing to enhanced outcomes for students.

Lyndale is committed to fostering a positive, inclusive culture for both students and staff. We support professional growth through collaboration, peer observation, and evidence-based teaching practices. Whether you are a student seeking a dynamic and supportive learning environment or a staff member looking to advance your career, Lyndale Secondary College is a place where potential is realised and excellence is celebrated.

Recent investments in state-of-the-art facilities have transformed our campus, creating an ideal environment for innovative learning. These facilities include a STEM Centre, Technology/Arts Hub, Aviation and VR Centre, a well-resourced library, and a world-class Performing Arts Theatre. These spaces enable modern teaching approaches such as team-teaching, cross-curricular projects, and community engagement, fostering creativity, critical thinking, and collaboration.

**Vision & Values**

At the core of our work is a shared vision: to celebrate diversity, inspire excellence, and equip our students for the challenges and opportunities of tomorrow. Our community is grounded in the values of respect, responsibility, and resilience, which inform our approach to both teaching and learning.

Through our strategic focus on enhancing teacher capacity and implementing a Schoolwide Positive Behaviour Support Framework (SWPBS), we are committed to ensuring that every student experiences measurable growth, regardless of their starting point. We believe in the power of student voice and leadership, empowering our young people to make meaningful contributions within and beyond our school community.

Join Lyndale Secondary College and be part of a future-focused team, where we are driven by our passion for education and our belief in the potential of every student.

### **Selection Criteria**

**SC1** Demonstrated expert knowledge of the relevant curriculum. Demonstrated ability to lead and manage the implementation of school priorities, and the teaching of literacy and numeracy skills across the curriculum.

Leading teachers will be expected to make a significant contribution to policy development relating to teaching and learning in the school. A leading teacher has a direct impact and influence on the achievement of the school goals.

Alkira is a Wurundjeri word meaning Big Sky. It was chosen to highlight the place of our learning high on a hill and also the wide and endless opportunities that we make available to our school community.

The school continues to be a school of choice in the local area forcing us to manage extreme enrolment growth and transition of students across all year levels reflecting a shift in demographics and diversity of our surrounding community. This year the school enrolments have peaked at 1935 FTE enrolments, not including a number of International students and part time students enrolled in online or offsite programs. Our SFOE index is Medium at 0.4337. Our school is highly multicultural with 30 % of students being born overseas. Enrolments also include Aboriginal students, EAL students and NCCD students.

The School vision and statement of purpose and core values from day one recognised our responsibility to provide a personalised education for every child in our emerging community.

To ensure we maintain our sense of community and strong relationships, our school is broken up into sub schools and is also emerging into a senior, middle and junior school. This schools within school SWIS model helps to ensure every student is known and their personal, educational, and social needs are monitored, managed and supported by a staff of over 200. Pastoral Care is a significant aspect of the SWIS model and further supports the notion of securing the entitlements of all students. Pastoral Care has a focus on developing student learning experiences with the notion that the PC teacher and sub school support team continues to plan for student improvement.

We have embraced 21C learning and developed a range of programs and resources to promote independent learning and improved student achievement. All students `bring their own device¿ (BYOD) and work within a dedicated Learning Management system (Compass) while having access to other blended learning resources.

Our dynamic curriculum and teaching and learning programs are supported through Professional Learning Communities and focused professional development and coaching. The College has an agreed model of instruction that supports High Impact Teaching strategies.

An orderly learning environment is created by high and consistent expectations that are guided and supported by our College non negotiables. Our agreed behaviour management processes support a student's right to a safe and secure learning environment, and a teacher's right to direct and establish such an environment. The program is very successful as it focuses on students¿ work and provides an opportunity for reflection and involves a restorative process.

Our school is dedicated to fostering an inclusive and supportive environment for all students. We adhere to the principles of the Berry Street Education Model and The Resilience Project, which emphasize trauma-informed education, resilience, and emotional well-being. Our commitment extends to being ahead of the curve in supporting students with disabilities, ensuring they have access to tailored resources and opportunities for success. We also provide robust support for Koori students, honouring their cultural heritage and promoting educational equity. Additionally, we offer comprehensive assistance to students in out-of-home care, recognizing their unique challenges and providing stability and encouragement. Through these initiatives, we create a nurturing and equitable community where every learner can thrive.

Our teachers are expected to contribute to wider non curricula programs and support and celebrate our student's achievements. We run a system of providing course work support and extra learning opportunities outside our regular timetable.

Pathway programs are established in years 10 -12 and include opportunities for students to be involved in VCE and supplement their programs with a VET program in their chosen vocational area.

We have developed an extensive international partnership or network of sister schools in China and India, international PD, exchange and global collaborative projects are encouraged within our curriculum and teaching programs.

Alkira! a great place to work.

### **Location Profile**

Hallam Primary School is situated within one of the most culturally diverse communities in the City of Casey. Nearly forty languages other than English are spoken within the school community. Hallam Primary School has started a SWPBS journey and continues to promote its values of safe, responsible, learner, kind as key components of school culture and development.

Hallam Primary School provides an inclusive and supportive learning environment. The school ensures a safe and orderly learning and teaching environment, implements school-based wellbeing support that incorporates fair and equitable student management processes, establishes effective curriculum, assessment and reporting procedures and has high expectations that all students can learn and be successful.

Staff work collaboratively and take collective responsibility for students' learning and wellbeing. This is consistent from Foundation, where many students enter the school developmentally vulnerable and make progressive gains through to Year 6. These gains are achieved through a structured learning environment aligned with the VTLM2.0 and purposeful explicit teaching.

Programs in Science-Technology (Science, Coding, Robotics, VR), Physical Education, Visual Arts, Performance Arts and LOTE (Auslan) and cooking and gardening through the Stephanie Alexander Kitchen Graden program. Students are offered participation in a range of extra-curricular experiences such as camps, incursion and excursions throughout the year.

**SC4** Demonstrated exemplary interpersonal and communication skills. Demonstrated ability to engage in collaborative relationships with students, colleagues, parents and the broader school community to support student learning, agency, wellbeing and engagement.

### **Role**

Learning Specialists will be highly skilled classroom practitioners who continue to spend the majority of their time in the classroom delivering high-quality teaching and learning and have a range of responsibilities related to their expertise, including teaching demonstration lessons, observing and providing feedback to other teachers and facilitating school-based professional learning. Learning Specialists are expected to have deep knowledge and expertise in high quality teaching and learning in delivering improved achievement, engagement and wellbeing for students. The role of the Learning Specialist will be to model excellence in teaching and learning through demonstration lessons and, mentoring and coaching teachers in improving the skill, knowledge and effectiveness of the teaching workforce.

The Learning Specialist role is aimed at building excellence in teaching and learning within the Teaching Service.

### **Responsibilities**

In recognition of the importance of exemplary practice for improved student learning outcomes, the key roles of the Learning Specialists may include but are not limited to:

* Demonstrating high-level expertise in teaching and learning practice
* Modelling exemplary classroom practice including through teaching demonstration lessons
* Working with the school leadership team to develop a shared view of highly effective teacher practice
* Leading and modelling the implementation of whole-school improvement strategies related to curriculum planning and delivery
* Playing a key role in the provision of professional learning, including through developing processes and protocols for observation and feedback of teacher practice and peer collaboration
* Modelling effective learning practice and supporting teachers to seek, analyse and act on feedback and on their practice
* Providing evidence-based feedback to teaching staff to inform their effectiveness and development
* Providing expert advice about the context, processes and strategies that will shape individual and school professional learning
* Supervising and training one or more student teachers and mentoring and/or coaching teachers
* Modelling exemplary use of student data to inform teaching approaches
* Developing and promoting school-wide professional learning structures, processes and protocols through Professional Learning Communities
* Modelling exemplary professional learning practice included through seeking feedback from other teachers and leaders on their own classroom practice as part of critical reflection and inquiry to improve practice

### **Who May Apply**

Teachers currently registered or eligible for registration with the Victorian Institute of Teaching and qualified to teach and/or have demonstrated experience in the curriculum area(s) specified for the position.

### **Diversity and Inclusion**

We value diversity and inclusion in all forms - culture, gender, religion, ethnicity, LGBTIQA+, disability and neurodiversity. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for roles within the Department. It is our policy to provide reasonable adjustments for staff with disability (see Workplace adjustment guidelines).

Additional support and advice on the recruitment process is available to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander candidates from the Koorie Outcomes Division (KOD) via [email protected]

Applicants seeking part-time employment are encouraged to apply for any teaching service position and, if they are the successful candidate, request a reduced time fraction. Such requests will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis and will be subject to the operational requirements of the school.

### **Child Safe Standards**

Victorian government schools are child safe environments. Our schools actively promote the safety and wellbeing of all students, and all school staff are committed to protecting students from abuse or harm in the school environment, in accordance with their legal obligations including child safe standards. All schools have a Child Safety Code of Conduct consistent with the department's exemplar available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/child-safe-standards/policy

The department's Values complement each school's own values and underpin the behaviours the community expects of Victorian public sector employees, including those who work in Victorian Government Schools. Information on the department values is available at:

https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/values-department-vps-school-employees/overview

### **Other Information**

**Please upload your cover letter, CV and responses to the key selection criteria in one PDF document.**

### **Conditions of Employment**

* All staff employed by the Department and schools have access to a broad range of employment conditions and working arrangements.
* Appointment of successful applicants will be made subject to a satisfactory pre-employment conditions check.
* A probationary period may apply during the first year of employment and induction and support programs provided.
* Detailed information on all terms and conditions of employment is available on the Department's Human Resources website at http://www.education.vic.gov.au/hrweb/Pages/default.aspx

### **Qualification Requirements**

To be eligible for employment, transfer or promotion in the principal or teacher class:

* The person must have provisional or full registration approved by the Victorian Institute of Teaching; and
* if the person completed an Australian postgraduate level initial teaching program or course of study on or after 1 January 2024, they must demonstrate that they have satisfactorily completed a postgraduate level accredited initial teacher education program that has been accredited by an Australian State or Territory Teacher Regulatory Authority as satisfying the requirements of the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership 'Accreditation of initial teacher education programs in Australia: Standards and Procedures'; and
* a person who graduated from a Victorian Initial Teacher Education (ITE) program after 1 July 2016 must also demonstrate that they have passed the literacy and numeracy test for initial teacher education (LANTITE) requirements (this condition is satisfied where the LANTITE requirement is part of the Victorian ITE program completed by the person).

Law Squared is a leading Human Centred Law firm, founded in 2016 to provide a true alternative to traditional law firms, for clients and lawyers alike.

We work exclusively on an upfront, fixed-fee model, prioritising our client’s success over billable hours and ensuring transparency and strategic control over their legal spend. By focusing on outcomes and value, rather than time and task-based inputs, Law Squared seamlessly bridges the gap between legal expertise and commercial impact.

Trusted by General Counsels, in-house teams, and business leaders across a broad range of industries, Law Squared focuses on those areas crucial to business success, including Corporate, Commercial, Employment + Workplace Relations, Disputes + Litigation, Property + Projects as well as those clients seeking dual jurisdictional support in Australia, the UK and/or NZ.

Law Squared has offices in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Perth, Auckland, and London.

**About the role**

We’re looking for up to 3 experienced Disputes + Litigation lawyers (4-6 PQE) to join our growing national team. You’ll manage your own matters end-to-end – including your own appearances and supported in mediations while acting for Law Squared’s clients. Working directly with a team lead, and the Head of Disputes, we are looking for lawyers who have experience in acting for one or more of the following categories:

* asset and property financier disputes

* debt and asset recovery

* motor vehicle insurance disputes

* property insurance disputes

* insolvency; and

* general commercial disputes.

As a member of the team, you’ll play an active role beyond file management including participating in client retention and acquisition activities, through to working with paralegals and contributing to the team’s ways of working.

This role suits someone who works autonomously yet collaboratively, confident in having a first go, backed by the team, and motivated by shared outcomes rather than individual accolades or the traditional partnership track, in a firm built around outcomes, not billable hours.

**Role Responsibilities**

The core responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

**Delivery of Legal Work**

* Complete legal work and manage a caseload across Disputes + Litigation matters
* Run matters end-to-end, including conducting your own appearances and, where relevant, supported in mediations
* Act for a set of clients which may includes equipment and property financiers, debt and asset recovery agents, corporate clients and other clients with litigious disputes nationally
* Apply technical judgement and attention to detail to progress files efficiently and effectively and adapt to the use of technology, including automation

**Practice Growth and Client Experience**

* Play a positive role in the retention of clients, including engaging and nurturing client relationships
* Participate in client acquisition and retention strategies and activities on behalf of the Disputes + Litigation team
* Deliver legal services in the Law Squared way, providing a consistent, high-quality client experience

**People Development and Management**

* Support, train and mentor team members to build consistent quality and style in the Law Squared way
* Assist with the onboarding of new team members
* Contribute to a collaborative team culture that shares resources and opportunities, rather than working in silos

**Innovation and Continuous Improvement**

* Adapt and harness technology as a key enabler for driving efficiencies and client outcomes
* Support the review and improvement of service offerings and solutions, including ways of working, proposals, knowledge sharing and the use of technology generally
* Identify opportunities to improve precedents, workflows and ways of working within the practice group

**About you**

At Law Squared, we hire for mindset as much as skillset. The ideal candidate will be:

* **Experienced** – You bring 4 – 6+ PQE, with a background in litigation which may include acting for financiers, debt and asset recovery agents, insurers, and/or corporate clients generally
* **Tech and AI proficient** – You are comfortable using technology and enthusiastic about adopting new tools that enhance efficiency and service delivery in a modern, paperless environment
* **Autonomous** – You manage your own file load with confidence, including conducting your own appearances, and are comfortable taking ownership of matters from instruction through to resolution, with supervision
* **Commercially astute** – You understand the practical and financial realities driving clients’ decisions and bring pragmatic, outcomes-focused advice to every matter
* **Detail-oriented** – You bring precision and rigor to your work, with a sharp eye for the detail that protects our clients’ interests
* **A strong communicator** – You communicate clearly and confidently, both in writing and in person, and build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues alike
* **Collaborative** – You work well within a team, sharing resources and knowledge, and thrive in an environment that rewards shared outcomes over individual competition
* **Team-oriented** – You’re motivated by collective success rather than the traditional partnership track, and are comfortable working towards team-based, rather than individual, targets
* **Adaptable** – You thrive in a fast-paced environment, embrace change and are comfortable balancing multiple priorities

Given that we have removed all hierarchical titles from our firm, it is important that becoming a partner isn’t your main priority and that you are open to working in a collaborative firm that values whole team success over individual accolades.

Also importantly, you’re someone who aligns with our values:

**Different on Purpose** – You challenge the status quo and look for better ways of doing things

**Keep It Real** – You communicate openly, honestly and authentically

**Own the Outcome** – You take accountability and follow through

**Find the 1%** – You believe small improvements create extraordinary results over time

**Show Up** – You bring energy, commitment and care to your team, clients and colleagues

**How you’ll benefit**

Law Squared is on a mission to create a more innovative, collaborative, human centred experience for clients and employees alike.

We don’t track billable hours, nor do we have financial budgets for individuals, and we’ve embraced a ‘work from anywhere’ policy since day one.

Free from the barriers of time, tenure, and ego, and aligned by team-oriented goals, we believe our result deliver the best outcomes for our clients and each other.

**Our numerous employee benefits include:**

* Hybrid and flexible work environment
* Competitive salary package
* Tailored team and individual professional development program, including support to meet CPD requirements
* Annual Practising Certificate paid for by Law Squared
* Discounted corporate membership via ClassPass
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Employee Referral Incentive
* A recognition-led culture, where contribution is celebrated and career milestones are genuinely acknowledged
* Leading-edge legal ops and tech to optimise flexible working and client service outcomes
* Team-based KPIs, no timesheets

If you’re ready for a more human centred way of working, experience the Law Squared difference for yourself.

**Apply Now**

To submit an application, please apply directly with your CV and cover letter.

If you have any further questions please contact: dmercieca@squaredgrp.com

### **Company Overview**

Squared Group is the strategic hub behind three purpose-driven businesses: Law Squared, Cubed, and Tetra Claims; each redefining how services are delivered in their industries. Together, we are human-centred, impact-driven, and designed for real-world value. Across legal services, technology and claims management, we’re building something different: better experiences, smarter solutions, and work that makes a meaningful impact for our clients, our communities, and the people who join us.

**Join our team as a Customer Service Officer at Banyule Leisure.**

Are you a friendly, organised and customer-focused person who enjoys helping people feel welcome, informed and supported? Banyule Leisure is looking for a Customer Service Officer to join our team and help create positive experiences for our members, visitors and community.

In this role, you’ll be one of the first points of contact for customers across Banyule Leisure. You’ll provide helpful information about programs, memberships, facilities and services, support day-to-day reception and café operations, and assist with bookings, payments, administration and general customer enquiries

**Why you’ll love this role and what you’ll do:**

* Welcoming customers and providing friendly, accurate and professional service.
* Responding to enquiries and helping customers find the right programs, memberships, products and services.
* Processing bookings, payments, point-of-sale transactions and basic administration.
* Supporting reception, merchandise and café operations, including stock control and coffee making.
* Keeping customer areas clean, tidy, well-presented and safe.
* Assisting with programs, promotional activities and the general running of Banyule Leisure facilities.

**Shifts available:**

* Wednesday 3:30pm - 7:30pm
* Wednesday 6:00pm - 9:15pm
* Thursday 6:00pm – 9:15pm
* Friday 3:30pm - 7:30pm
* Sunday 12:00 noon - 4:15pm (alternating shift, 2nd Sunday of the fortnight)
* Sunday 7:15pm - 9:45pm (Women's only shift - required to enable Council to deliver culturally safe programs. Only female applicants are eligible for this shift).

**What you’ll bring/what we are looking for:**

You will bring a positive, practical and community-minded approach, with the confidence to work in a busy customer service environment. You’ll enjoy helping people, solving day-to-day issues and working as part of a team to deliver a welcoming and reliable service. You’ll have

* **A commitment to Banyule Leisure’s values and a keen interest in promoting health and fitness of our customers and the wider community.**
* **Strong customer service focus and ability to multitask in a busy and dynamic environment, without compromising service to customers.**
* **Excellent phone manner, written communication, and interpersonal skills.**
* **Ability to discuss customer needs and identify the best service for them within Banyule Leisure, including well-developed conflict resolution skills.**
* **Experience in customer service, membership sales, cash handling and administration (desirable)**
* **Experience in the leisure facility industry (desirable)**

**What’s on offer**

* **A permanent part time role with shifts available Wednesday to Sunday.**
* **$36.79 to $38.54 per hour plus super (depending on experience).**
* **Primary work location Ivanhoe Aquatic, and Olympic Leisure Centre.**
* **Consistency in shifts, working on a part time basis with the potential to pick up extra shifts.**
* **Supportive and engaging team.**

**Mandatory Qualifications:**

* **Level 2 First Aid (Apply First Aid).**
* **Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)**

* **Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check (NCCHC)**
* **Pre-Employment Medical Check**
* **Working with children check**

**Why choose Banyule?** **Join a dedicated team committed to making a positive impact on our community. At Banyule Council, you'll have the opportunity to drive service excellence, engage with diverse stakeholders, and contribute to the betterment of our community. We offer a supportive, collaborative, and innovative work environment where your skills and expertise will be valued and rewarded.**

**Banyule City Council is an Equal Opportunity Employer; we value diversity and inclusion, and we welcome candidates from all backgrounds. If you have a reasonable adjustment, support, or access requirement, we encourage you to inform us through your application or email** **employment@banyule.vic.gov.au**

jobs.title: Building Services BIM Manager
jobs.description:
The Team:

We are an award winning global consultancy and have been named Building’s Engineering Consultant of the Year in 2024, 2022 and 2021. Sustainability drives what we do: Through our Zero Carbon Design 2030 goal, we are working towards all our projects meeting our zero carbon design criteria by the end of this decade.

We’re looking for a BIM Manager to lead delivery across our Australian offices,supported by an established APAC team, with a strong focus on building services
projects. You’ll report to our Director of Building Services.

The Role:

Lead BIM Delivery across Australia - and stay hands on.

This role keeps you close to project delivery.Around 30-50% of your time goes into live project work, producing, reviewing and coordinating Revit models and documentation, particularly on complex or delivery-critical jobs. The rest is delivery leadership: planning BIM resources, setting up projects, building workflows and maintaining technical quality.

If you want a role that’s purely strategy and standards, this isn’t it. If you want technical credibility and real influence over how projects get delivered, it is.

* Lead model production, coordination, clash detection and QA/QC using Revit, Navisworks and Autodesk Construction Cloud
* Plan and coordinate BIM resources across our Australian offices and our broader APAC BIM Team, against project priorities, programme and fee
* Set up project BIM requirements and Execution Plans under ISO 19650, applied pragmatically to suit each client and project
* Work closely with engineers and project managers to resolve delivery issues, establish practical workflows and keep projects moving
* Maintain and improve the standards, templates and families that keep our output consistent — and keep them practical enough that teams actually use them
* Grow our digital engineering capability over time, including automation, scripting and AI.

The Skills:

* Strong hands-on Revit experience producing and coordinating multidisciplinary building models, ideally with building services depth
* Practical working knowledge of ISO 19650, BIM Execution Plans and information delivery requirements
* Experience organising multiple projects and BIM resources, including offshore or distributed teams
* Commercial judgement — you understand fees, programme pressure and how to balance BIM effort against the value it delivers
* Excellent communication skills; you influence through credibility and collaboration, not process enforcement

A relevant BIM qualification is a plus.Demonstrated delivery capability matters more.

We’re open to candidates at different career stages who bring the right balance of technical capability and leadership potential.

jobs.description:

We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

**About the Team**

At Workday, we help the world’s largest organisations adapt to what’s next by bringing finance, HR, and planning into a single enterprise cloud. We work hard and we’re serious about what we do, but we like to have fun, too. We put people first, celebrate diversity, drive innovation, and do good in the communities where we live and work.

**About the Role**

As a Senior Solution Consultant specialising in Workforce Management and Payroll, you are essential to the sales cycle and play an important role on the Sales team. You will use your subject matter expertise in the domain to provide support to the Sales team and help drive the sale by providing influence and credibility to C-level executives.

If you are a proven presales Workforce Management and Payroll consultant and have strong functional knowledge and experience gained through roles such as payroll practitioner, HCM enterprise solution Pre-Sales / Sales Payroll Consultant, and/or have a background in payroll application implementation, we’d love to speak to you.

**Responsibilities include:**

* The delivery of relevant technical product presentations, demonstrations, workshops, and seminars.
* Crafts detailed design and implementation specifications for sophisticated products/applications/solutions
* To assist in the closure of sales opportunities by demonstrating a complete understanding of and resolving questions regarding our solution, services, and training.
* To support the qualification of prospects, proposed demonstration criteria, proof of concept system builds and sales cycle closure plans.
* Supporting all sales, marketing, technical and channel objectives.
* To assist sales in the response to RFxs
* Participate in discovery sessions alongside sales to ask qualifying questions and understand struggles, current business processes, and ideal future state
* Uses in-depth ERP-product knowledge to provide technical expertise to sales staff and the customer through sales presentations and product demonstrations
* Ability to travel 50+% of the time

**About You**

You are an exceptional, dynamic presenter with excellent communication and influencing skills, specifically to a C-level Human Resources leadership audience

You possess credibility and passion for presentations and product demonstrations around HCM technology solutions:

* You’re a subject matter expert when it comes to payroll and workforce management
* As a plus, you’re also knowledgeable about HCM enterprise solutions and HCM
* You’re passionate about Workday and believe that businesses and organisations can advance and grow by adopting Workday solutions

**Basic Qualifications:**

. 5+ years in Presales and/or Services Consulting or other technical roles.

* 3+ years’ experience in HCM systems and/or processes
* Strong understanding of the HR Management functional areas such as Core HCM, Time & Attendance, Rostering, Compensation, Payroll, Employee Engagement

**Other Qualifications:**

* Exposure to SaaS HR solutions from Workday, Oracle and SAP would be an advantage
* Knowledge of Generative and Agentic AI as applied to the HR domain and experience in positioning embedded or built-on-AI solutions to business and technology stakeholders
* Strong orientation towards articulating the value of AI-driven solutions
* Ability to work on multiple simultaneous projects individually as well as working cross-functionally
* Outstanding professional discovery, presentation, communication, and influencing skills to C-Level and senior administrators.

. 5+ years in a Solution Consulting, sales consulting AND/OR implementation role.

. Thrives in a fast-paced environment

**Our Approach to Flexible Work**

With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply **spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field** with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.

jobs.title: PT Role in Ballan - Leads Supplied, No Rent
jobs.description:
Personal Trainer Opening | Ballan, VIC

**No Chair Rent. A Full Calendar. A Mentor In Your Corner.**

Casual personal training role in Ballan, VIC, starting immediately. $40.17 to $55 per hour depending on ongoing client hours, plus super and commission. Ramp up to 20 to 30+ paid hours weekly.

**You Got Into This to Coach, Not to Run a Failing Business**

You chose this work to help people get strong and healthy, not to chase invoices and leads.

You did not sign up to:

* Watch your best clients leave because you had no time to actually program for them
* Lose good prospects because there was no one to follow up while you were coaching
* Burn your evenings writing captions nobody books from
* Chase leads who ghost your texts after you spent two hours prepping their free session
* The grind outside the gym floor is what finishes most PTs, long before their coaching ever lets them down.

**Jamie Fitness was built so you can just coach.**

**So, The Catch?**

No catch. One requirement: you have to actually be the kind of coach we can back:

* **Reliable.** People can count on you to be there and be ready.
* **Hungry.** You want a real career, not just a few extra shifts.
* **Consistent.** You show up the same way on the hard days as the easy ones.
* **Accountable.** You own your mistakes, fix them, and do not blame the gym, the client or the weather.
* Not everyone fits this, and we are okay with that. We want people who want to be great at the coaching part.

**Everything You Walk Into**

Yeah. We hear that from every trainer who applies. Here is what you actually get:

**Your own PT assistant.** Books sessions, sends reminders, handles follow ups and passes you notes before every client walks in. You just show up and coach.

**Mentoring that pays for itself.** A coach with 15+ years in the game helping you turn trials into ongoing clients, every single week.

**Fortnightly team workshops.** Programming, sales and coaching skills. Keep sharpening the blade.

**No marketing to run.** We do the ads, the calls and the follow up. You do the sessions.

**Free gym access.** Train yourself and coach your clients with no fees.

**Backed from day one.** Branding, profile, app and admin set up for you before your first client.

**Picture a Normal Week**

Clients are booked and confirmed before you arrive, the paperwork is handled, and your weekly mentoring just helped you sign five new ongoing members. You spend your day coaching, not chasing, and your income keeps climbing.

**That is what the week looks like.**

**About Jamie Fitness**

Across Melbourne and Sydney we have set up 20+ trainers in 20+ clubs with no rent and no solo grind. We run the sales, marketing, admin and lead generation so you can run the coaching. More paid hours, better clients, far less noise.

More about us: https://www.jamiefitness.au

Have a quick look: https://youtube.com/shorts/KrTaR9ctbH8

**Who We Are After**

* Strength focused training for everyday people
* Cert III and IV in Fitness, or finishing soon
* First Aid, CPR and a WWCC sorted
* Ready to build something that actually lasts
* **The right person gets snapped up fast. If that is you, apply now.**

**No Cert Yet? Still Apply.**

No Cert III and IV yet? That is okay. Through our trusted industry partners we can help you get qualified and gain the real world experience to start your fitness career. So if you are interested, **apply anyway.**

Job Type: Casual

Pay: $40.17 – $55.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Gym membership

Licence/Certification:

* Certificate III+IV In Fitness or Equivalent (Required)

Work Authorisation:

* Australia (Required)

jobs.description:
**Employment Type** - Casual

**Hours per fortnight** - 0

**Job Category** - Other Professionals - Podiatry

**Req Id -** 9406

**HAVE IT ALL**
**JOIN OUR ALLIED HEALTH TEAM NOW!**

* Gain a diverse caseload across inpatient, outpatient and community settings
* Ongoing training and professional development in a supported work environment
* Casual opportunity available - apply now!

**About the role**

As a Podiatrist at Grade 2 level, based at the University Hospital Geelong, you will deliver high-quality podiatry services across inpatient and outpatient,programs within the Allied Health Directorate.

This role provides care to a diverse caseload, with a strong focus on high-risk foot management, and chronic condition support. You will work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team to deliver evidence-based interventions that promote mobility, prevent complications, and improve health outcomes for consumers.

You will be responsible for contributing to service improvement, meeting program KPIs, and applying contemporary clinical frameworks (including ADIET) to support safe, effective, and consumer-centred care.

This position also includes supervision of junior staff and Allied Health Assistants, participation in quality improvement initiatives, and collaboration with internal and external stakeholders including aged care teams, GPs, and community services.

**Key responsibilities**

* Deliver independent, evidence-based podiatry assessment and treatment across inpatient, outpatient and rehabilitation settings, with a focus on aged care and high-risk foot presentations.
* Provide clinical management for complex and chronic conditions, including wound care, diabetes-related foot complications and mobility impairment.
* Work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support coordinated care planning, intervention and review.
* Contribute to quality improvement activities, service development initiatives and reporting against program KPIs.
* Provide supervision and support to Grade 1 podiatrists and Allied Health Assistants as required.

**What we’re looking for**

* Qualified Podiatrist with current registration with the Podiatry Board of Australia and at least 4 years’ clinical experience.
* Strong clinical skills in high-risk foot management, wound care, chronic disease and rehabilitation-focused podiatry.
* Experience working in aged care, hospital or complex clinical settings highly regarded.
* Proven ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team and build strong professional relationships.
* Commitment to evidence-based practice, continuous improvement and alignment with organisational values.

**Reference:** VG/200826/1943063CSOC

Deliver an exceptional customer service experience as the first point of contact for our Point Nepean National Park!

* Amazing work location in iconic National Park
* Great supportive team environment
* Part of a broader organisation focused upon the environment, conservation and visitor engagement
* See our Careers Page for more information what we can offer

**About the role**

As the Customer Service Officer, you will be the first point of contact for a customer, including members of the public and Victorian community. You will professionally handle information requests and ensure that issues and enquiries are resolved promptly and thoroughly. This position is responsible for the daily customer service tasks involved in providing an oustanding camping experience at the Point Nepean Discovery Tents. Your daily tasks may include checking in and checking out of campers, attending to camper's questions and requests, providing information to campers regarding the National Park, Flora, Fauna, History, Culture, and the range of services and activities available to them.

This role supports the Commercial Team Leader in providing front-line visitor support at Point Nepean National Park and may be requitred to support all commercial operations, commercial activations and events including customer service, campground operation, cleaning and basic maintenance resposibilities, visitor experience, liaising with key stakeholders, event support, and administrative tasks.

**About the Team**

We are a small, hardworking and fun-loving team with a great customer service ethic. We are very lucky to be working amongst the history, culture and nature of the magnificent Point Nepean National Park and Quarantine Station. Our job is to ensure that all of our campers and park visitors appreciate and enjoy the experience as much as we do, and to ensure they have an amazing camping experience.

**We're looking for someone with:**

* Customer Service, Visitor Information and Community Engagement skills
* Environmental Education or basic Land Management skills or experience
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* Demonstrated ability to work as part of a team
* Problem solving and professional judgement

**Your application will need to include:**

* A Current Resume
* A Cover Letter

Application Close date: Sunday 6th September 2026

**Sound like you?**

For a confidential discussion about the role, call Anthony Gadd on 0434 167 690 or apply online!

If you don't hold every skill or experience detailed above, please don't rule yourself out. We focus on hiring people who value collaboration and integrity. We value a culture where everyone can be themselves at work, regardless of background, orientation, age or gender.

If this resonates with you, then please consider applying or getting in touch to discuss.

**Company Description**

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the worldâs most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

**Job Description**

**Be part of the deals that power the transition**

AECOM's Energy Advisory practice sits at the heart of the energy transition, helping public and private sector clients navigate everything from strategy and business case development through to commercial structuring and transaction support.

As our practice grows, we're looking for a **Commercial Advisor** to strengthen how we deliver rigorous, credible commercial advice, working hand-in-hand with our technical, planning and engineering teams to shape integrated solutions our clients can act on with confidence.

This role is anchored in energy, with the opportunity to flex across other infrastructure sectors as our pipeline demands. If you want your commercial thinking to sit right alongside the engineers shaping renewables, storage, hydrogen and grid infrastructure, this is your seat at the table.

**What you'll be doing**

* Structuring and delivering commercial advice on energy sector engagements, business cases, market analysis, and options and feasibility assessments
* Leading or contributing to commercial and technical due diligence on energy transactions (asset sales, M&A, financing), translating technical findings into commercial risk and value for clients
* Applying working knowledge of energy market fundamentals and transition themes to frame commercial issues with confidence
* Developing and interrogating financial and market models, investment appraisals and feasibility analyses
* Building trusted relationships as a client-facing advisor, representing AECOM's commercial advisory offer to senior stakeholders
* Preparing client-ready deliverables, business cases, due diligence reports, investment memoranda, tender/bid documentation, board and investment committee papers
* Supporting engagements end-to-end, from origination and proposals through to delivery and ongoing client relationships
* Working at the interface of commercial, financial and technical team, translating engineering and planning input into commercially credible advice, and back again

**Qualifications**

**What you'll bring**

* 5+ years' experience in a commercial, financial or transaction advisory function, gained within a professional services/advisory firm (Big 4, engineering/infrastructure consultancy, investment bank, infrastructure fund) or an equivalent in-house commercial team

AECOM's Energy Advisory practice uses quantitative and techno-economic modelling to underpin the advice we give clients on energy transition, market design, investment and policy decisions. As our practice grows, we're looking for a **Quantitative Modeller** who can work hands-on across a range of modelling approaches from established energy market and dispatch tools through to bespoke, purpose-built models and translate that analysis into commercially grounded advice for clients.

This is a client-facing role working closely with a senior advisory team. You'll need to be comfortable working independently, engaging directly with clients, and always connecting your modelling outputs back to the commercial question at hand. We're open to a wide range of experience above our 5-year minimum for a more senior candidate, there's genuine scope to grow into a technical leadership role within the team over time.

**What you'll be doing**

* Building, running and interrogating quantitative models techno-economic, energy market and dispatch modelling, multi-sectoral modelling, or other bespoke analytical models with the judgement to choose the right approach for the question at hand
* Framing modelling exercises around the client's actual decision or advisory question, translating technical outputs into clear commercial insight and recommendations
* Working independently on modelling tasks with minimal oversight, while knowing when to flag assumptions, limitations or emerging findings to senior team members and clients
* Presenting technical analysis to non-technical audiences and defending modelling assumptions under scrutiny, with strong written communication to translate methods and findings into clear reports and deliverables
* Applying your quantitative and problem-structuring skills beyond energy where relevant the underlying capability matters as much as sector-specific tools
* Contributing to, or leading, broader advisory engagements beyond modelling bringing analytical rigour to non-modelling workstreams as needed

jobs.description:
**Delivery Lead, Capability (12 Month FTC)**

Req ID: 119766

Department: Tech Strategy & Execution Technology Business Mana

Division: Technology

Location: Melbourne

**About Us**

At ANZ, we're shaping a world where people and communities thrive, driven by a common goal: to improve the financial wellbeing and sustainability of our millions of customers.

**About the Role**

Fortify is a major regulatory program responding to significant reforms in the financial crime and external fraud landscape, including changes to AML/CTF laws, the Scams Prevention Framework and expanded sanctions expectations. As part of the Program, we’re transforming how we manage Financial Crime risk globally, delivering scalable, compliant and customer-focused technology outcomes that help protect our customers, communities and the Bank.

As the **Delivery Lead – Technology Capability / Platforms**, you’ll lead delivery across a defined technology capability or group of platforms, working closely with the Technology Program Director, Delivery Leads, Value Stream Leads, risk, architecture, business teams and strategic vendors. You’ll turn Fortify outcomes into clear, executable delivery plans, bringing strong project management discipline across scope, sequencing, milestones, dependencies, controls and implementation readiness to help deliver complex capabilities safely and predictably.

Banking is changing and we’re changing with it, giving our people great opportunities to try new things, learn and grow. Whatever your role at ANZ, you’ll be building your future, while helping to build ours.

**Role Type: 12-Month Fixed Term Contract**
**Role Location: Melbourne or Brisbane**
**Work Hours: Full-Time**

**What will your day look like?**

* Lead delivery for a defined technology capability or group of platforms, ensuring work is planned, sequenced and delivered in support of Fortify outcomes.
* Translate value stream priorities and business outcomes into clear technology scope, milestones, delivery plans and implementation roadmaps.
* Coordinate delivery across platform owners, engineers, architects, analysts, testers, release teams, operations and business stakeholders.
* Manage dependencies, RAID, assumptions, decisions and trade-offs, escalating early to protect critical milestones and regulatory outcomes.
* Maintain clear visibility of status, scope, schedule, budget, capacity, constraints and implementation readiness.
* Partner with the Technology Program Director to manage the integrated Technology delivery plan, milestone baseline, risks, budget, resourcing and financial tracking.
* Support strong delivery governance through clear reporting, risk and issue management, decision escalation and delivery controls.
* Partner with architecture and technology teams to ensure solution options, design decisions and delivery approaches are practical, scalable and aligned to strategy.
* Drive disciplined delivery rhythms, including planning, milestone tracking, dependency management, release readiness, implementation planning and transition to BAU.

**What will you bring?**

To grow and be successful in this role, you will ideally bring the following:

* Minimum of 15 years' experience leading complex technology delivery across platforms, services or capabilities in a large enterprise environment.
* Strong understanding of technology delivery lifecycles, including planning, estimation, design, build, test, release, implementation and transition to BAU.
* Strong project management capability, including integrated planning, milestone management, scope control, RAID, dependency tracking, governance and delivery assurance.
* Project management certification in Prince2, PMBOK, Agile methodologies.
* Confidence working with architects, engineers, analysts, testers, release teams, operations and platform owners to turn complex requirements into executable work packages.
* Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence, challenge and align teams around priorities, constraints, trade-offs and delivery commitments.
* Highly organised and outcomes-focused, with the discipline to manage competing priorities, critical paths, risks and regulatory timeframes.
* Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technology delivery information into clear updates, options, decisions and executive messages.
* Experience preparing governance packs, release readiness materials and executive status updates.
* Commercial and strategic thinking, with an understanding of funding, capacity, prioritisation, value drivers and the broader organisational context.
* Financial services, risk, compliance, regulatory change or Financial Crime delivery experience is highly regarded.
* Sound understanding of project controls, change control, benefits alignment, implementation readiness and operational transition in a regulated banking environment.
* Exposure to agile, hybrid or waterfall delivery methods, technology governance and enterprise delivery tooling would be beneficial.
* Familiarity with Jira, MS SharePoint, project planning and reporting tools.

You’re not expected to have 100% of these skills. At ANZ a growth mindset is at the heart of our culture, so if you have most of these things in your toolbox, we’d love to hear from you.

**So why join us?**

From the moment you join ANZ, you'll be doing meaningful work that will shape a world where people and communities thrive.

But it's not just our customers who'll feel your impact. You'll feel it too. Because at ANZ, you'll have the resources, opportunities, and support you need to take the next big step in your career.

We're a diverse bunch at ANZ in different roles, different locations, doing different things. That's why we have a range of flexible working arrangements, so our people can 'make work, work for them'. We also provide a range of benefits including access to health and wellbeing services and discounts on selected products and services from ANZ and more.

At ANZ, you'll be part of an organisation where the different backgrounds, perspectives and life experiences of our people are celebrated. That's because we're committed to building a workplace that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve. We welcome applications from everyone and encourage you to talk to us about any adjustments you may require to our recruitment process or the role itself. If you're a candidate with a disability or access requirement, and have an enquiry about the support provided, please let us know on your application or visit ANZ Accessibility and Inclusion Programs for alternate contact methods.

Working across development, SRE, production support, architecture, security and infrastructure teams, you'll ensure the platform remains stable, scalable and fit for the future whilst enabling the delivery of strategic business outcomes.

This role offers the opportunity to influence technology decisions at scale. Whether you're strengthening observability, reducing operational risk, leading major incident investigations or improving platform governance, your work will have a direct and measurable impact on service performance, customer outcomes and AMP's technology strategy

* Contribute to strategic growth plans and help expand Aurecon's structural market share within the data centre sector
* Mentor and support developing engineers while fostering a collaborative team culture
* Work across multidisciplinary teams to deliver integrated engineering outcomes

**What you'll** **bring**

We know the work we do is key to solving our clients' most complex challenges. It's the technical expertise, commercial mindset and market credibility of our people that sets us apart.

Here are the key things you'll need to bring ideas to life:

* Degree qualification in Civil or Structural Engineering, Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) and/or RPEV registered, with 10-15 years' structural engineering experience
* Strong experience delivering structural projects within a consulting environment
* Demonstrated experience within the data centre sector or closely related complex buildings markets
* Exposure to Design & Construct project environments and working directly with contractors
* Strong understanding of structural design, constructability and commercial project drivers
* Experience in modular and prefabricated structural solutions
* Proven ability to build client relationships and identify new business opportunities
* Confidence representing your organisation in client meetings, workshops and industry forums
* Strong communication, stakeholder engagement and leadership skills
* Experience leading project teams and delivering complex engineering solutions

**How we support your growth**

This is an opportunity to establish yourself as a leader within one of Australia's fastest-growing infrastructure sectors. You'll work alongside industry-leading experts delivering some of the country's most significant and prestigious data centre projects, while helping shape the future direction of Aurecon's structural capability in this market.

As an Associate, you'll be empowered to build your profile, strengthen your industry network and influence both project and business outcomes. You'll be supported by experienced technical leaders who value collaboration, innovation and continuous development.

Recognised by the AFR as a Best Place to Work in 2026, we embrace diverse perspectives and flexible ways of working. You'll be part of a team that values technical excellence, entrepreneurial thinking and creating opportunities for our people to thrive.

**Who we are**

We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is why we are here: to bring ideas to life, the Aurecon way.

**Ready for your next adventure?**

If you're looking for an opportunity to lead, influence and grow a market while working on some of Australia's most exciting digital infrastructure projects, we'd love to hear from you.

We value diverse experiences and welcome applications for part-time or flexible working arrangements. For recruitment adjustments, contact WorkplaceAdjustment@aurecongroup.com.

Our hiring decisions are made by people, not AI. We're most interested in your individual thinking and experiences, so please ensure your application reflects your authentic perspective.

Are you a current Austin Health employee?

If yes, please log in to the Austin Health careers website via ‘Employee Login’ using your network login details to search, view and apply for all career opportunities available.

Permanent position

Part time – 32 hours per week

Convenient Austin Hospital location, close to public transport

Austin Health is the major provider of tertiary health services, health professional education and research across three campuses in the north-east of Melbourne and statewide. We have a highly engaged, diverse and collaborative workforce that is unified by our goal to help people live healthy and fulfilled lives.

About the Surgery, Anaesthesia & Procedural Medicine department

Austin Health’s Surgery, Anaesthesia and Procedural Medicine Division (SAPM) is part of the Operations Directorate. The Division manages a number of specialties and services including theatres, CSSD, vascular/Cath lab; cardiac diagnostics and the surgical wards at Austin and Repatriation sites. SAPM employs over 1,500 staff and is responsible for the provision of approximately 50,000 planned and emergency procedures per year delivered to the community serviced by Austin Health.

SAPM promotes a culture that aims to deliver quality patient care. Staff are encouraged to value lifelong learning and as such are provided with time for education and professional development. The aim of this is to ensure that patients always receive excellent care and staff satisfaction and professional development is maintained.

About the role

Reporting to the Divisional Manager, Access, Planned Surgery & Endoscopy Services, this role combines personal assistance, unit administration, leave coordination and operational support across a diverse portfolio of surgical and procedural services. You will be responsible for helping ensure the smooth operation of key administrative functions.

**A regular day will see you:**
Provide high-level diary, meeting and administrative support to Divisional Managers.

Coordinate meetings, preparing agendas, distributing papers and recording minutes.

Act as a central point of contact for Divisional Managers, Heads of Unit, medical staff and key stakeholders.

Manage end-to-end medical staff leave processes and maintaining unit leave planners.

Support recruitment, onboarding and workforce administration activities.

Monitor mandatory training, performance review and other HR compliance requirements.

Process invoices, purchase orders and other financial administration functions.

About you

You are a collaborative and solutions-focused administrator with outstanding organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities confidently.

**To be successful in this role you’ll bring with you:**
Experience in administration or personal assistance roles

Excellent customer service and stakeholder management skills.

Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills.

Exceptional attention to detail and data accuracy.

Proven ability to prioritise, multitask and meet deadlines.

Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word and Excel.

The ability to work independently and collaboratively within a complex healthcare environment.

Our benefits

Working at Austin Health means enjoying a strong sense of purpose, engaging in meaningful work every day. Our people also receive a variety of rewarding benefits, including:

Greater take-home pay through generous salary packaging, for living expenses, meals, and holiday accommodation.

A suite of wellness initiatives designed to support you, including discounted fitness memberships and special offers on health insurance, and a comprehensive wellbeing program.

Onsite childcare at Austin Hospital, easy access via public transport and car parking options.

Mentoring and career development opportunities.

Work with us!

We are committed to cultural safety and health equity for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander People. We celebrate, value, and include people of all backgrounds, genders, identities, cultures, bodies, and abilities. We welcome and support applications from talented people identifying as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, people with disability, neurodiverse people, LGBTQIA+ and people of all ages and cultures.

If you feel this role is right for you, we encourage your early application. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, we encourage you to apply. What matters most is your passion, your drive and your willingness to learn and contribute. Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and interviews may take place prior to the closing date. This means we reserve the right to close a job ad prior to the advertised closing date.

All appointments are made subject to a satisfactory National Police Check and if required, a Working with Children Check. Austin Health is a child safe organisation, committed to upholding the rights, safety, and wellbeing of children and young people in line with Child Safe Standards. If you require any reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process, you are welcome to reach out to the hiring manager: Naomi Italia, Acting Div Manager - Access Planned Procedures, Endoscopy and Endoscopy Services at Naomi.ITALIA@austin.org.au

Interested in finding out more about this opportunity? Read the position description for further details.
