SC1 Demonstrated ability to build positive relationships with young people and provide effective support for students experiencing wellbeing, attendance or engagement difficulties.

SC2 Demonstrated ability to assess student needs, develop support strategies, coordinate referrals, maintain professional records and monitor student progress.

**SC3** Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively and work collaboratively with students, families, school staff, community organisations and external professionals.

**SC4** Demonstrated ability to plan, deliver and evaluate individual, small-group or broader youth engagement and wellbeing initiatives.

**SC5** Demonstrated understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries, child safety, mandatory reporting, inclusion and culturally responsive practice.

SC6 Demonstrated capacity to model the Department of Education¿s values and contribute positively to a safe, respectful and inclusive school community.

### **Role**

Range 3 is distinguished by the introduction of management responsibility and accountability for the delivery of professional support services. The role will usually impact beyond the work area or professional field. It seeks to gain cooperation of other staff members or members of the school community to achieve specific objectives, such as in school administration, operations or educational programs.

Direction on targets and goals is provided but the position will have some degree of latitude in determining how they are achieved. This latitude will generally be limited by standard procedures and school policy. Deviation from standard procedures and school policy will require guidance and direction from senior management.

The provision of business management responsibilities becomes a feature at range 3. Management of staff to achieve the expected outcomes is a key responsibility. Staff management issues will be resolved with minimal reference to senior management, although guidance will be required in more complex cases. Senior management will be provided with timely reports and advice, although this will generally be confined to matters relating to the immediate work area, service provision or educational program and is unlikely to impact substantially on whole of school operations.

This is the minimum range for positions that carry a mandatory qualification requirement of not less than four years. Professional student support positions become a feature at range 3 (e.g. therapists, psychologists) where standard professional services are delivered. Professional support and guidance will be close at hand and deviation from standard procedures and school policy will require guidance and direction from senior management.

An education support class position supports the educational services being provided to students, but must not include duties of teaching as defined in clause 2.6.1 of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006 (Vic) or its successor. Supervision of students cannot be required except where it is an integral part of the employee¿s position or involves supervision of students individually or in small groups, in controlled circumstances, where the responsibility for students remains clearly with a teacher.

### **Responsibilities**

The Youth Worker supports student engagement, wellbeing, attendance and connection to school. Working as part of the school¿s multidisciplinary wellbeing and sub-school teams, the Youth Worker provides targeted support to students experiencing social, emotional, behavioural or environmental barriers to learning.

The role builds positive relationships with students, families, staff and external services and assists students to develop the skills, confidence and supports required to participate successfully in education.

Consistent with an ES Level 1 Range 3 position, the Youth Worker exercises professional judgement within established school policies and procedures and may coordinate defined wellbeing programs or areas of student support.

**Key responsibilities**

**Student wellbeing and engagement**

* Develop safe, respectful and culturally responsive relationships with students.
* Provide individual and small-group support for students experiencing wellbeing, engagement, behavioural or attendance concerns.
* Assist students to identify barriers, establish goals and develop practical strategies for improving their engagement with school.
* Support students to develop emotional regulation, communication, conflict-resolution and help-seeking skills.
* Provide early intervention and targeted support in response to emerging student needs.
* Assist students during periods of distress and support their safe return to learning.
* Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and work within the scope of the Youth Worker role.

**Case management and coordinated support**

* Manage an allocated caseload of students under the direction of the relevant school leader.
* Develop, implement and review student support plans in collaboration with students, families and relevant staff.
* Participate in Student Support Group meetings, wellbeing meetings, attendance meetings and case conferences.
* Coordinate communication between students, families, school staff and external agencies.
* Maintain accurate, confidential and timely records of student contact, referrals, interventions and outcomes.
* Monitor student progress and provide reports to relevant school leaders and wellbeing staff.
* Escalate complex, high-risk or clinical matters to appropriately qualified staff and school leadership.

**Attendance and re-engagement**

* Identify and follow up students displaying emerging or ongoing attendance concerns.
* Work with students and families to understand barriers to attendance and participation.
* Contribute to attendance improvement, re-engagement and return-to-school plans.
* Support students transitioning back to school following extended absence, suspension or disengagement.
* Collaborate with sub-school teams to monitor attendance, engagement and agreed interventions.

**Programs and group work**

* Plan, coordinate and deliver evidence-informed youth engagement and wellbeing programs.
* Facilitate targeted small-group programs addressing identified student needs.
* Support student voice, leadership, belonging and connection to the school community.
* Evaluate programs using participation information, student feedback and agreed outcome measures.
* Contribute to whole-school prevention and early-intervention initiatives.

**Family and community partnerships**

* Build respectful and constructive relationships with parents and carers.
* Connect students and families with appropriate school, community and government services.
* Develop and maintain effective partnerships with youth services, health providers and community organisations.
* Participate in interagency meetings when required and authorised.
* Advocate for students while maintaining confidentiality, professional boundaries and child-safety requirements.

**Team contribution**

* Work collaboratively with teachers, Heads of Cohort, Heads of School, Disability Inclusion staff and the wellbeing team.
* Provide relevant information and practical advice to staff within the scope of the role.
* Contribute to multidisciplinary planning for students requiring additional support.
* Participate in supervision, professional learning and performance-development processes.
* Contribute to a positive, inclusive and child-safe school culture.

**Level of responsibility**

The Youth Worker:

* works with a degree of independence within established policies, procedures and professional boundaries
* exercises professional judgement when selecting appropriate support strategies
* is accountable for an allocated student caseload or defined wellbeing program
* works collaboratively across teams and gains the cooperation of staff, families and external providers
* refers clinical assessments, diagnoses, therapeutic interventions and high-risk decisions to appropriately qualified professionals
* does not have responsibility for curriculum planning, teaching duties or disciplinary decisions
* operates under the general direction of a nominated school leader.

**Child safety**

The Youth Worker must:

* identify and respond appropriately to concerns about student safety

* immediately escalate disclosures, risks or safety concerns in accordance with school and Department procedures

jobs.description:
Registered Nurse – In Home Care (Community Experience)

* Melbourne Eastern Suburbs
* Casual Position

About the Role

We are seeking a motivated Registered Nurse Grade 3A to join our Victoria team on Casual basis.

We are primarily looking for nurses based in Melbourne Eastern Suburbs and Surrounding areas, although the role may require coverage across neighbouring regions.

The primary purpose of the In-Home Care (IHC) Primary Nurse Registered Division 1 is to provide comprehensive clinical care to consumers in a community setting. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, the role is responsible for delivering high quality, best practice care that meets the expectation of the consumer and demonstrates a commitment to maintaining an optimal level of dignity, respect, comfort and quality of life for consumers.

As a Nurse, you will provide care and support that enhances the health and wellbeing of our customers that continue living in the community, in their own homes and who are committed to the needs of our customers. Focused on delivering high-quality care, and maintaining an optimal level of dignity, respect, comfort, and quality of life for our clients.

Key Duties

Community Nursing services, ensuring person-centred care through assessment, planning, documentation, and evaluation.

Implement the intervention/s identified in the plan of care for each customer and ensure the customer's response to these directives is evaluated, communicated, and documented in the progress notes.

Facilitate a professional and compassionate approach to care.

Maintain clear, consistent communication while respecting individual privacy and dignity.

Safe management of all clinical care tasks, including medication management, Infection prevention and control, wound care etc

About You

You are passionate about continuing to grow your career in the Community Nursing space. Solution focused and wanting to make a difference, you align your approach to achieve organisational and divisional goals. Working as part of a close-knit team, you collaborate with and support others, demonstrating respect in your day-to-day actions.

Must be a Registered Nurse Div1

At least 3 years of Nursing experience in community nursing.

Current registration with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA).

Experience working within the Aged Care Sector or with Elderly people.

Proficient in computer literacy, including Microsoft Word & basic Excel.

Driver’s license with a car

A warm, compassionate, and reliable team member.

ABOUT BAPTISTCARE

BaptistCare is a leading purpose-led care organisation, guided by our Christian identity and serving people and communities across Australia for more than 110 years. We support people to live better through aged care, home care, retirement living, community services, disability support and housing.

We know that life’s challenges can make our world feel smaller. With the right people alongside us, it can feel more connected, supported and hopeful again.

That’s what we work towards every day - enriching lives through communities of care. Today, more than 70,000 customers, 12,000 employees and close to 2,000 volunteers are part of our communities across Australia.

BaptistCare – Inspired by Jesus to champion care for all.

Hit ‘Apply’ now! Applications are reviewed as they are received, so don’t wait.

Questions about the role? Contact Aya Badawy at talent@baptcare.org.au

**Please note:** applications must be submitted through our online system. We are unable to accept applications via email. We kindly ask that recruitment agencies refrain from making contact or submitting candidates for this position. Only short-listed applicants will be contacted.

BaptistCare is dedicated to the safety, empowerment, and participation of all children. We have zero tolerance of child abuse and are committed to a thoughtful, protective environment that supports infants, children, and young people to feel safe and respected.

We have a highly engaged, diverse and collaborative workforce that is unified by our goal to help people live healthy and fulfilled lives.

About the Speech Pathology Department

The Speech Pathology Department is committed to promoting the highest levels of care for our patients. In realising this goal, the department will lead and excel in research, teaching and the use of person-centred evidence-based practice. The department provides services on all three campuses of Austin Health

We have over 40 speech pathologists working across all three sites of Austin Health, in acute care, sub-acute care, rehabilitation and community programs. We function as one department and work in clinical teams in a supportive, friendly environment. Our work includes clinical services, research, quality and improvement, staff and student education.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Speech Pathologist to join our team to fill a grade 3 role and to make a meaningful impact supporting patients, families and their carers

This position is initially based on the Austin site and will work as part of Acute stream under the guidance of the Grade 4 Acute stream leader.

Undertaking a swallowing assessment

Working in the ICU or on our spinal multidisciplinary team

Teaching a staff member to undertake videofluoroscopy

Attending a team meeting

Leading a quality activity

About you

You will be someone who has excellent communication skills and a strong commitment to excellence in patient care. You’ll bring energy and drive to you work, and have a keen interest in leading others. You will have the ability to provide treatment for a wide variety of clinical conditions, and the desire to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team

Our benefits

Greater take-home pay through generous salary packaging, for living expenses, meals, and holiday accommodation.

A suite of wellness initiatives designed to support you, including discounted fitness memberships and special offers on health insurance, and a comprehensive wellbeing program.

All appointments are made subject to a satisfactory National Police Check and if required, a Working With Children Check. If you require any reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process, you are welcome to reach out to the hiring manager: Rhonda Holmes, Speech Pathologist Grade 4 at Rhonda.HOLMES@austin.org.au.

jobs.title: HSEQ Manager
jobs.description:
**HSEQ Manager – Melbourne CBD**

**Location:** Melbourne, VIC

**Company:** BGIS, Government Client

**Employment Type:** Full-Time, Permanent, Hybrid (3 Days Office, 2 Days WFH)

**We acknowledge the Traditional Custodians of the land on which we work, and pay our respects to Elders past, present and emerging.**

**About BGIS**

BGIS is a global leader in integrated facilities management, delivering innovative and sustainable solutions to clients across various industries. We pride ourselves on our collaborative and inclusive culture, and on maintaining high standards of safety, quality, and service.

**Purpose of the Role**

BGIS is looking for an experienced **HSEQ Manager** to establish, implement, and nurture the Health, Safety, Environment, and Quality management systems that support the delivery of a significant government property and facilities management portfolio. Reporting to the Contract Team, you will work closely with both client and BGIS teams to embed a proactive safety culture, ensure compliance, and support high-quality, audit-ready systems across the portfolio.

This is a wonderful opportunity to help shape and strengthen the HSEQ foundations of a recently awarded contract. You'll play a valued part in bringing structure, embedding thoughtful systems, and supporting teams during an important establishment period.

The ideal candidate will be a calm, capable, and collaborative HSEQ professional who genuinely cares about people's safety and wellbeing. You'll combine strong technical knowledge with the ability to build trusted relationships, support and guide teams, and bring clarity and consistency to a busy environment.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop, implement, and maintain the contract's Quality Management System aligned to ISO standards.
* Support compliance with relevant safety legislation, codes of practice, regulations, and BGIS safety frameworks.
* Support contractor and workforce compliance including SWMS, permits, inductions, and training records.
* Coordinate subcontractor induction processes and support emergency management planning across sites.
* Manage the collation and record keeping of site-specific hazardous substances and coordinate the operational team and subcontractors to ensure records are current
* Guide incident response, reporting, and root cause reviews, ensuring corrective actions are completed and verified.
* Manage account incident management system and monitor safety performance, risk trends, and compliance.
* Design and support Power Automate workflows to streamline safety and quality processes.
* Coordinate training programs, safety briefings, toolbox talks, and skills validation activities.
* Maintain safety and quality risk registers, control plans, and risk assessments.
* Build positive relationships with client representatives, operational teams, and subcontractors.
* Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety culture and quality of service.

**Education, Experience & Skills**

**Essential:**

* Tertiary qualifications in Occupational Health and Safety, Quality Management, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
* Experience in safety and quality management within facilities management, construction, infrastructure, or high-risk operational environments.
* Strong understanding of ISO 45001, ISO 9001, and relevant safety legislation.
* Experience in incident management, investigations, and root cause reviews.
* Comfortable using digital systems, technologies, and data-driven insights to improve ways of working.
* Strong Power BI and Microsoft Fabric capability for reporting and performance insights.
* Experience developing Power Automate workflows for safety and quality processes.
* Excellent communication and relationship-building skills at all levels.

**Desirable:**

* Experience working within government portfolios or multi-site operational contracts.
* Auditing qualifications (Lead Auditor preferred).
* Experience with contractor management and critical risk programs.
* A genuine interest in continuous improvement, innovation, and thoughtful use of technology.

**Workplace Flexibility**

To support your success, this position will initially be based from our **Melbourne CBD office** , conveniently located close to public transport and local amenities. Following training, you will enjoy a **hybrid working arrangement of 3 days in the office and 2 days working from home** .

**Why Join BGIS?**

**Key Benefits Include:**

✔ Spot recognition vouchers and $2,000 employee referral bonus.

✔ Access to Flare for discounts across retailers, energy, utilities & much more!

✔ Fitness Passport (access for you and your family to gyms and aquatic centres nationwide), employee discounts, and optional yearly paid flu vaccination vouchers.

✔ AFR Best Places to Work 2024 & 2025.

✔ Winner of Inspiring Workplaces Award 2025.

✔ Endorsed by Work180 as an employer of choice for women.

✔ Career progression through secondments & internal mobility.

✔ Wellbeing programs and family-friendly initiatives.

✔ Recognised by WORK180 as a Top 5 Employer for career development opportunities.

**How to Apply**

If you are a proactive, skilled, and engaging **HSEQ professional** looking to join a forward-thinking company, we would love to hear from you!

BGIS is an equal opportunity employer and we warmly encourage applications from women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, LGBTQ+ individuals, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds.

**Eligibility**

To be successful in the role, applicants must have full working rights in Australia.

**Apply Now**

Be part of a workplace that values diversity, safety, sustainability, and belonging.

Explore more opportunities at https://apac.bgis.com

jobs.company: Victorian Government - Department of Families, Fairness, and Housing
jobs.description:
**THE ROLE**

The Care Support Help Desk (CSHD) Advanced Worker reports to the CSHD Coordinator and works closely with the CSHD team. The position also works closely with Child Protection, Care Services, Kinship Engagement Teams, Out of Home Care Service providers and Peak organizations to support best outcomes for children in statutory care.

The CSHD provides critical support activities for children in all care types with a focus of children entering care. The CSHD improve the consistency and timeliness of information, supports and document sharing, particularly critical identity documents for children in care such as birth certificates and Medicare cards.

A dedicated phone line operates in each division as a contact point to assist carers to navigate care processes and assist in identifying placement vulnerabilities and escalate issues/concerns on behalf of carers to the most appropriate program/services.

The Care Support Help Desk Team provide support to unallocated kinship carers, through active outreach and providing vital documentation relating to the children in their care.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES INCLUDE**

* The Advanced Worker will have specific responsibility to undertake priority care support tasks.
* It will play a critical role in leading the administrative functions for all placement establishments and support earlier identification of care needs to strengthen and support children and young people in statutory care.
* The successful applicant will be organised, relationships-focused, and demonstrate excellent written and verbal communication skills, collaboration, and innovation.

***Please open the position description to read more.***

**This role requires a Working with Children Check.**
Further advice on obtaining this check can be found here: https://www.vic.gov.au/working-with-children-check

For more information on what this means, and all other requirements, please see the Position Description.

**HOW TO APPLY**

Applicants are encouraged to apply online. Attachments can be uploaded in .doc, .docx, .pdf, .txt or .rtf formats.
Applicants are required to submit a CV and Cover Letter (max 2 pages) outlining their suitability to the role in line with the Key Selection Criteria.

Applicants must be an Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident or hold a valid work permit or visa. Work eligibility will be checked as part of the recruitment process.

Preferred candidates will be required to complete pre-employment screening, including a national police check and misconduct screening.

For more information on working with us and our recruitment process, please visit Department of Families, Fairness and Housing Victoria | Jobs (www.dffh.vic.gov.au/jobs)

jobs.title: Employment Consultant
jobs.description:
**Job Description**

Are you passionate about supporting people with disability to secure employment that could change their life? Do you have a knack for identifying and individuals’ employment match? If so, YOU could be our next **Employment Consultant** at our **Werribee VIC** site within our **Inclusive Employment Australia Program**.

Who Are We:

As part of the APM group, you have the opportunity to grow your career in Human Services across multiple global brands and geographies. A diverse team of over 16,000 people across 11 countries with a shared purpose – to enable better lives for our employees and the communities we work in. Our work enables the people we serve to realise their ambitions and aspirations through sustainable employment, independence, better health and wellbeing and increased social participation.

Who You Are:

A champion of diversity and inclusion – you believe that everyone, no matter their abilities, deserves a chance to succeed

A natural connector – you know how to create opportunities for participants and speak to stakeholders with confidence

Innovative and solutions focused – You see the challenge as an opportunity and have experience creating pathways to success

Compassionate and empathetic – You want to make a lasting and positive impact on the lives of others

You may also have experience in another industries or roles like sales, retail, call centre, hospitality, consulting, business development, and administration. These skills can set you up for success in this role!

What You’ll Be Doing:

Find the perfect match – you’ll support participants with disability to prepare for, find and maintain sustainable employment.

Boost Confidence – You will help participants see their strengths, overcome obstacles, and take on their new employment with a renewed sense of purpose

Shake Things Up – You will provide creative solutions to overcome employment challenges, making sure every participant has the tools and support for success

Advocating – You will be an advocate for inclusive hiring practices and workplace adjustments

Celebrate the Moments That Matter – Every successful placement is a success, and we are all about celebrating success, big and small with our participants

Building lasting connections – You will form partnerships with companies that are passionate about diversity and inclusion, making sure everyone has a chance to shine!

Why You’ll Love It

This isn’t your average desk job. We are all about breaking barriers, creating opportunities and helping people with disability thrive by securing and supporting them into employment.

* Competitive salary plus performance-based incentives that reward your success
* Ongoing training and career development – we are committed to your growth
* Supportive and inclusive team environment where your contributions make a difference every day
* Celebrating milestones – we love to recognise and rewards hard work with fun events
* EAP | Employee Wellbeing Program
* Purchased Annual Leave
* Paid Parental Leave
* Funded Certificate IV in Community Services or Mental Health Peer Support (eligibility criteria applies)
* Service recognitions
* APM Family Hub
* Maxxia | Vehicle salary packaging

At APM we are strengthened by diversity. We are committed to providing a work environment in which everyone is included, treated fairly and with respect. We encourage applications from people of all ages, nationalities, abilities and cultures including indigenous peoples, the LGBTQI+ community and people with disability.

Ready to change the game? If you are looking for a role where no two days are the same, where you get to inspire, motivate and create a lasting impact, we want to hear from you! Let’s work together to break down barriers, shatter expectations and build a more inclusive world- one individual at a time.

jobs.title: Insights and Planning Lead
jobs.description:
### **Description**

The **Insights & Planning Lead** helps Client Leads unlock growth with key strategic clients by shaping solution-focused ideas, elevating client conversations, and creating compelling pitch decks that use storytelling to

solve challenges and drive new business opportunities. The role bridges marketing strategy with sales execution, positioning the company as a trusted partner rather than just a supplier.

This is the core focus of your role. Make sure you allocate the right amount time to deliver key tasks effectively.

Remember, you’re empowered to lead in your performance…if something doesn’t feel right, work through options on how best to solve for it. Ask for feedback and feel free to share it.

From time to time, you may need to support other areas. Use these opportunities to show teamwork and leadership and ask for clarity if needed.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Insight Driven Solution Development**

* Translate client insights, challenges, and needs into solution-focused recommendations.
* Think beyond briefs and proactively spot opportunities to add client and commercial value.
* Shape proposals that elevate conversations and position of the company as a strategic partner.

**Client Conversation Partner**

* Support Client Leads to move discussions beyond product or price towards value and outcomes.
* Prepare talking points and decks that reframe client challenges and guide solution-based thinking.
* Participate in strategic conversations as a thought partner when needed.

**Innovation and Ideation Leadership**

* Facilitate innovation workshops and ideation sessions that unlock growth for clients and the company.
* Stay on top of global trends, fresh thinking, and market shifts to drive smart insights and planning.
* Use AI and new tools to solve problems faster and deliver smarter client solutions.
* Inspire fresh thinking and lead ideation sessions where client growth opportunities are being explored.

**Pitch Deck Storey Telling & Visual Communications**

* Lead the development of solution-focused pitch decks that follow a clear narrative flow: Client Problem Bold Idea Clear Solution Why It Matters.
* Ensure decks feel like stories, blending insights, visuals, and data.
* Coach and support Client Leads to confidently present ideas.

**Collaborative Partner**

* Work closely with Client Leads, CXT, Creative, and Production teams to shape commercially viable and operationally realistic ideas.
* Act as a bridge between marketing strategy and sales execution

**AI & Innovation**

* Embrace AI as part of how we work, stay open to new ways of doing things, and be willing to learn, experiment and think differently.

### **Non-negotiable skills and experience**

* Strategic problem framing: can distil an ambiguous client brief into a sharp problem, useful insight and clear opportunity.
* Insight synthesis: knows how to find, test and combine qualitative, quantitative and cultural evidence without relying on a large research budget.
* Commercial solution selling: has worked close to a B2B or agency sales cycle and can connect ideas to client growth, value, revenue, GP and delivery reality.
* Pitch storytelling writes and shapes senior-client decks with a strong narrative, not a collection of slides.
* Facilitation and influence: can lead discovery, ideation and decision-making sessions, challenge constructively and build confidence without formal authority.
* Judgement with AI and data uses approved tools to accelerate research and development, checks sources and protects confidential client information.

### **Helpful, but learnable**

* Experience in branded merchandise, promotional products, shopper marketing, loyalty, experiential, sponsorship, brand activation or retail marketing.
* Familiarity with audience, trend, cultural-insight or social-listening platforms.
* Workshop design, innovation methods and rapid concept development.
* Experience coaching client-service (sales) teammates.
* Understanding of responsible sourcing, sustainability and production constraints in physical brand solutions.

**What everyday work looks like**

* Meet Client Leads to understand priority accounts, live briefs, growth gaps and upcoming client conversations.
* Frame the real client problem, identify the audience or behaviour that needs to shift, and find the most useful insight.
* Use the company's global insight tools, approved AI tools, client data and desk research to build a concise evidence base. This is synthesis and application, not a large primary-research programme.
* Shape solution territories for branded merchandise, promotions, loyalty programmes and brand experiences, working with Creative, Marketing Operations, Production and supply partners.
* Build the strategic narrative and content for proposals and pitch decks: client problem, insight, opportunity, bold idea, deliverable solution, commercial case and why it matters.
* Facilitate ideation sessions, client workshops and internal working sessions that end with decisions and clear next actions.
* Coach Client Leads to present the story confidently and respond to senior client questions.
Create reusable playbooks, insight summaries, case studies and proposal components so good thinking travels across the Australian team and connects with global work.

**Likely day-to-day challenges**

* Turning incomplete or product-led briefs into a clear client problem without slowing the sales cycle.
* Creating credible insight and a strong strategic point of view without a local marketing or research budget.
* Balancing fresh thinking with price, margin, timing, production, sustainability and supply-chain realities.
* Influencing experienced Client Leads and senior clients without formal authority or direct reports.
* Moving between several opportunities at different stages, from early discovery to a near-final pitch.
Avoiding beautiful but generic decks. Every recommendation must be useful, distinctive and sellable.

jobs.title: Software Project Engineer
jobs.description:
Eaton is an intelligent power management company dedicated to improving the quality of life and protecting the environment for people everywhere. Every day, all around the world, people depend on technology, transportation, energy, and infrastructure to live and work. With rapid growth in electrification, an energy transition driven by climate change and explosive growth in connectivity, we’re well positioned to solve the world’s toughest electrical and mechanical power management challenges.

We're looking for a **Project Control Engineer** to join our PMO team and support the successful delivery of mission-critical power monitoring and control projects. This is an opportunity to work across the full project lifecycle, build highly sought-after technical expertise, and contribute to some of Australia's most important infrastructure projects.

**What you'll do**

As part of a high-performing project delivery team, you'll help ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.

You will:

* Coordinate software engineering and project delivery activities
* Support electrical and software system design, documentation, and technical submissions
* Develop testing, commissioning, and quality assurance plans
* Lead or support factory testing and site commissioning activities
* Apply knowledge of power monitoring, control systems, networking, and SCADA environments
* Work closely with customers, engineers, service teams, and project managers
* Support project planning, reporting, and execution

**What we're looking for**

We're interested in professionals from critical power, electrical infrastructure, utilities, industrial automation, data centres, building services, or related industries.

You'll bring:

* 3+ years' experience in project engineering within the electrical industry
* Experience delivering software, controls, SCADA, or electrical infrastructure projects
* Experience in installation, commissioning, fault finding, and maintenance of power monitoring or control systems
* Knowledge of network protocols, power systems, and control technologies
* Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills
* Excellent communication, planning, and organisational capability
* A tertiary qualification in Electrical or Electronic Engineering

**Why Eaton?**

Join a global leader delivering the most critical infrastructure projects, where you'll gain end-to-end project exposure, build highly sought-after technical skills, and grow your career in a business shaping the future of electrification and connectivity.

* Work on mission-critical infrastructure projects across data centres, utilities, and industrial environments.
* Own and influence projects from design through to commissioning and handover.
* Develop expertise across power systems, controls, software, and project delivery.
* Competitive salary package, car allowance, and bonus.
* Global opportunities, local decision-making, and career progression pathways.

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Our recruitment processes encourage diversity by utilising a balanced selection criteria regardless of the applicants age, gender, gender identity, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or any other status protected or required by law. Eaton prides itself in truly representing the people within our communities.

**If this sounds like you, please send through your application. We look forward to hearing from you!**

jobs.title: Vehicle Homologation Engineer
jobs.description:
**About BYD**

BYD is a high-tech company devoted to technological innovations for a better life. BYD is dedicated to providing zero-emission energy solutions.

As a leading battery-electric zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) manufacturer, BYD has created a broad range of battery-electric, hybrid-electric, and internal combustion (IC) passenger vehicles. Developing electric vehicles that are intelligent and connected, BYD is inaugurating a new age of automotive innovation featuring a sleek design and an innovative user experience.

As a division of BYD Auto, BYD Commercial Vehicles Australia (BYD CV) is responsible for the sales and service of BYD buses and trucks in the Australasian market.

**About the Role**

Based in BYD’s Mulgrave Office in Melbourne, the **Vehicle Homologation Engineer** is responsible for supporting the certification and regulatory compliance of BYD vehicles, components, and accessories for the Australian and New Zealand markets.

The role manages vehicle approval activities, technical documentation, regulatory submissions, and ongoing compliance requirements. It works closely with BYD headquarters, government authorities, technical services, test facilities, and internal teams to support the **timely and compliant introduction of new vehicles and product updates**.

The role also monitors proposed and future vehicle regulations, participates in relevant government and industry discussions, and communicates upcoming regulatory requirements to the business and BYD headquarters.

On offer is a **Vehicle Homologation Engineer** position and your day-to-day duties will include but not be limited to:

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Vehicle Homologation & Certification**

* Manage Vehicle Type Approval applications, approval variations, new variants, and model updates.
* Review technical reports, approval certificates, specifications, drawings, and supporting certification evidence.
* Identify certification gaps and coordinate additional testing, documentation, or vehicle changes.
* Ensure relevant approvals are completed before vehicle launch, registration, or customer delivery.

**2. Regulatory Submissions & Vehicle Data**

* Review VIN information, model descriptions, variant data, weights, dimensions, and technical attributes before submission.
* Support evaluation vehicle and other relevant import approval applications.
* Maintain accurate records of approvals, submissions, approval conditions, and regulatory correspondence.
* Coordinate with internal teams to resolve vehicle data or registration discrepancies.

**3. Regulatory Compliance**

* Interpret and apply ADR, RVS, NZTA, AS/NZS, ANCAP, RCM and associated regulatory guidance.
* Assess new vehicles, model changes, components, accessories, labels, and software updates for regulatory impact.
* Provide technical advice on changes required to meet Australian and New Zealand standards.
* Support investigations into potential compliance concerns, certification discrepancies, and regulatory enquiries.
* Escalate and resolve compliance risks that may affect vehicle approval, launch, registration, or continued sale.

**4. Government & Industry Engagement**

* Liaise with Australian and New Zealand government authorities on certification, compliance, and regulatory interpretation matters.
* Participate in relevant government consultations, industry workgroups, technical forums, and stakeholder meetings.
* Monitor proposed legislation, ADR amendments, regulatory consultations, and future vehicle standards.
* Prepare technical summaries, consultation responses, and internal briefing documents where required.
* Communicate future regulatory requirements and potential product impacts to internal teams and BYD headquarters.

**5. Documentation, Reporting & Stakeholder Support**

* Prepare and maintain certification documents, compliance matrices, approval trackers, technical records, and regulatory reports.
* Provide regular updates on approval status, documentation gaps, regulatory risks, and upcoming requirements.
* Work with other internal departments and stakeholders on homologation matters.
* Provide guidance to internal stakeholders on certification processes and regulatory requirements.
* Support regulatory audits, conformity-of-production activities, and post-approval changes where required.

**Key requirements:**

**Qualifications**

* Degree or diploma in **Automotive Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline**.
* Equivalent relevant automotive industry experience will also be considered.

**Essential**

* Experience in **vehicle homologation, certification, automotive engineering, or a related automotive technical role**.
* Understanding of **Australian vehicle regulations, ADRs, and certification requirements**.
* Ability to read and interpret **technical specifications, certification documents, test reports, and regulatory requirements**.
* Good understanding of **vehicle specifications, model variants, tyres, wheels, drivetrain, dimensions, weights, accessories, and vehicle technologies**.
* Strong attention to detail and ability to work accurately with **technical data and documentation**.
* Proficient in **Excel, with strong data management and document control skills**.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks, follow up on outstanding matters, and meet deadlines.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills in **English and Mandarin**, with the ability to effectively communicate and coordinate with **BYD Headquarters, government authorities, testing facilities, and internal teams**.
* Valid Australian driver’s licence and ability to drive as required for the role.

**Desirable**

* Experience with **EVs, PHEVs, or new energy vehicles**.
* Experience with **RVSA, ROVER, RAV, NEVDIS, NZTA, VFACTS**, or other automotive regulatory or reporting systems.
* Experience with **vehicle certification, model launches, product changes, or vehicle approval processes**.
* Knowledge of **Australian and New Zealand vehicle regulations**.
* Experience working with **government authorities, technical services, testing laboratories, or automotive regulatory bodies**.
* Experience in an **automotive OEM, importer, distributor, or certification organisation**.
* Basic understanding of **UNECE/ECE regulations or international vehicle standards**.

If you believe you are a good fit for the role, please don't hesitate to click on APPLY and submit your updated resume.

BYD Australia is under rapid expansion with plenty more opportunities to arise. If you are ready to make the most of everything you’ve learned so far, be challenged, work together with industry leaders, and be a part of a supportive and vibrant team, then BYD is ready for you.

jobs.title: Systems Engineer – Land Capability ﻿
jobs.description:
**About the role**:

Join Saab Australia as a **Systems Engineer – Land Capability.**

Shape the Future of Land Capability.

We are seeking an experienced System Engineer – Land Systems to support the Program Engineering Lead in establishing and managing configuration baselines and delivering systems engineering and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) outcomes across a complex Land Capability program.

You will take ownership of assigned systems and technical work packages, working across the systems engineering lifecycle while supporting the development of ILS and sustainment engineering activities.

* Prepare technical material to support system reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, etc), and present technical outcomes to internal and external stakeholders.
* Contribute to design reviews, workshops, integration, test, site installation, commissioning, and sustainment activities.
* Support systems integration, verification and validation, including test planning, execution and analysis.
* Support technical risk analysis and contribute to major reviews throughout the project lifecycle.
* Support the development and maintenance of Land Capability system configuration baselines and engineering assets.
* Identify and resolve complex technical issues through structured analysis and root-cause investigation.
* Apply configuration and change management processes to maintain engineering baselines and CMCA assets.
* Provide technical input to project reporting, risk management and Earned Value Management activities.
* Act as a technical SME for assigned systems/assets and contribute to the development of less experienced engineers.
* Support technical proposals for, and delivery of, mission-critical capability
* Liaise with customers, end-users, subcontractors and suppliers.

**About you**

You will be a capable Systems Engineer with approximately 5–8 years’ experience, ideally working with complex, software-intensive or mission-critical systems within the Defence environment.

**You will bring:**

* Strong systems engineering capability across requirements, architecture/design, integration, verification and validation, and configuration/change management.
* Experience working across multiple stages of the systems engineering lifecycle; full lifecycle experience is highly desirable.
* Experience with DOORS or equivalent requirements management tools and CAMEO Systems Modeler or equivalent MBSE tools.
* Strong analytical, troubleshooting and root-cause analysis capability.
* Experience developing and managing technical work packages with minimal supervision.
* The ability to work effectively with engineering, project, assurance, customer and industry stakeholders.
* Defence domain experience, particularly C4ISR, combat systems, communications, sensors or complex Land Systems, is highly desirable.
* Familiarity with ASDEFCON engineering deliverables, networking and cyber security considerations is advantageous.
* Experience with Python, MATLAB, test automation or technical data analysis would be beneficial.
* Experience mentoring engineers or leading small technical workstreams is desirable

A Bachelor’s degree in Systems, Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Software/Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline is expected. INCOSE, Engineers Australia or equivalent professional membership is desirable.

**Security & ITAR**

* **Australian Defence Security Clearance – NV1** is required. Information including past and present nationality and citizenship may be requested to check eligibility for access to materials controlled under various export control regimes, including ITAR.
* Ability to access and work with **ITAR-controlled information**

This is an opportunity to work on a nationally significant Land Capability program where your engineering expertise will directly contribute to the integration, deployment and long-term sustainment of complex Defence capability.

jobs.title: Quantitative Analyst - Systematic Hedge Fund
jobs.description:
AI Job Summary

* Masters or PhD in Physics, Atmospheric Science, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent.
* 2–3+ years designing/developing predictive models using rigorous empirical methods (e.g., Bayesian inference).
* Excellent coding skills and deep experience with large complex datasets (MATLAB, Python, C, Fortran or similar).

Sign up or log in to analyse my fit

### **Role Type**

Permanent • Full-time • Associate

### **Description**

**Quantitative Analyst — Systematic Hedge Fund**

Join a systematic hedge fund that trades FX and Futures markets through a combination of top-down fundamental research, machine learning and rigorous quantitative modelling.

As a Quantitative Analyst, you’ll use your expertise in computer modelling to work as part of a team building a deep, shared understanding of financial markets, contributing to the design and development of the predictive models that our quantitative developers and software engineers bring to life. Every model we run is understood and owned by the team that builds it — we don’t deploy black boxes, and as a researcher here, you’re the reason why.

**About the Role**

We’re a Bayesian firm — we value intuitive priors and empirical inference to identify and prove a theory or relationship. We’re not afraid to explore new ideas, and as applied academics at heart, we encourage theoretical and practical pursuits across data science, machine learning, stochastic processes, optimisation, signal processing and control systems, to name a few. Financial markets are the most humbling of all predictive systems, and the optimal place to test and hone your skills.

We’re a small, agile team, and you’ll have the opportunity to work across all areas of the business, collaborating closely with colleagues to design and build solutions with measurable, positive outcomes.

**You’ll:**

* Design and develop predictive models, working closely with quantitative developers to bring them into production.
* Apply rigorous, empirical methods — Bayesian inference, statistical testing, and sound theoretical foundations — to real trading problems.
* Explore new techniques across data science, machine learning, stochastic processes, optimisation and signal processing.
* Work with large, complex datasets, and contribute to how we collect, structure and interpret them.
* Collaborate directly with developers and other researchers to turn ideas into deployed, working models, and to build a deep, shared understanding of the markets we trade.

**About You**

You’re articulate, intelligent, naturally inquisitive, and thrive in environments that encourage new ideas and value thought leadership.

**You’ll have:**

* **A Masters or PhD in Physics, Atmospheric Science, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering or an equivalent discipline.**
* A strong academic foundation with a passion for truth and the scientific method.
* A high level of initiative and self-motivation.
* Excellent coding skills and deep experience with large datasets (MATLAB, Python, C, Fortran or similar).
* A willingness to further develop and specialise your skills, including in financial markets, if you’re new to the industry.

**Nice to have:**

* Comfort in a Unix environment, with knowledge of cluster computing.
* Exposure to financial markets and software development — advantageous, but not essential for the right person.

We’re happy to consider both entry-level and experienced applicants. Full working rights in Australia required. Sponsorship is not available.

**Why Join Us?**

We’re a small, high-achieving team where individual contribution matters, and where the people building the models are trusted to understand them fully — not just deploy them.

You’ll also get:

* A competitive salary, together with an uncapped performance-based bonus.
* A fast, 3-stage interview process: a technical screen, a research problem to work through, and interviews with the team.

**If you’re accountable, professional, and want to work with some of the brightest people in the business on genuinely hard problems, we’d love to hear from you.**

*The AE Capital team does not require recruitment agency support — we have this covered.*

**Job Description Summary**

As a Warehouse Storeperson, you will play a vital role in supporting the efficient operation of Service Stream’s warehouse and logistics functions. This role requires strong organisational skills, a safety first mindset, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. **Job Description Summary**

ServiceStream is looking for an experienced National Warehouse Lead to join our Supply Chain team and play a key role in strengthening the performance, capability and consistency of our national warehouse operations.

Reporting to the National Warehouse Manager, you will work closely with three State Managers and warehouse teams across Australia to deliver national initiatives, improve operational performance and ensure our warehouses consistently meet high standards of safety, service, stock integrity and governance.

This is an opportunity for an experienced warehouse leader who combines strong people leadership with excellent operational, systems and commercial capability.

**About the Role**

As National Warehouse Lead, you will provide hands-on expertise and support to evolve our warehouse operations and deliver initiatives that improve capacity, efficiency and customer service.

**Your responsibilities will include:**

* Supporting the delivery of national warehouse initiatives against agreed timelines, budgets and operational requirements.
* Providing leadership, coaching and development to State Managers, warehouse supervisors and warehouse teams.
* Driving stock integrity and accuracy, with a target of greater than 98% accuracy by SKU.
* Ensuring the safe, timely and cost-effective receipt, storage and dispatch of materials across company and 3PL warehouses.
* Maintaining visibility and availability of stock for business units across the national warehouse network.
* Ensuring stocktakes, cycle counts and spot checks are completed in accordance with company procedures.
* Identifying opportunities to improve warehouse processes, systems and performance and implementing practical solutions.
* Supporting warehouse operations during periods of supervisor absence when required.
* Developing, communicating and reinforcing warehouse procedures, controls and standards.
* Ensuring warehouse operations comply with relevant legislation, licensing requirements, HSE obligations and company policies.

**What You'll Bring**

* Extensive warehouse management experience across multiple sites or complex warehouse environments.
* Strong people leadership skills, with a demonstrated ability to develop supervisors and warehouse teams.

* Strong knowledge of Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), including RF scanning.

jobs.title: Instrument Technician Grade 1 - 4
jobs.description:
**Job Description:**

* **Full Time, Part Time and Casual opportunities available**
* **Part Time applicants must be available to work a minimum of 0.6 FTE**
* **Fitzroy location – close to the CBD and public transport**
* **Excellent employee benefits including salary packaging**
* **Join a highly skilled and supportive Sterile Processing Centre team**

**About the Role**

An exciting opportunity exists for **Instrument Technicians** to join the Sterile Processing Centre (SPC) at St Vincent’s Hospital Melbourne.As an Instrument Technician, you will play an important role in ensuring the safe, effective and efficient reprocessing of reusable medical devices (RMDs) in accordance with Sterile Processing Centre policies and relevant State and National Standards.Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you will rotate across all areas of the Sterile Processing Centre, including supporting the Endoscopy Suite. Your responsibilities will include:

* Decontamination and high-level disinfection of reusable medical devices
* Reprocessing of endoscopy equipment
* Checking reusable medical devices and assembling instrument trays
* Packaging and preparation of sterile barrier systems
* Sterilisation and sterile storage
* Checking, testing and maintaining equipment and resources
* Maintaining accurate documentation in line with operational requirements
* Identifying, troubleshooting and reporting equipment or process variances

The Sterile Processing Centre operates **24 hours a day, 7 days a week**, and successful applicants will be required to participate in a roster covering a range of shifts.

**Classification:** Instrument Technician IN1–IN4 ($57,002.40–$73,502.00 per annum, pro rata for part time).

Casual workers will also receive a casual loading fee of 25%.

**About You**

We are looking for motivated and reliable Instrument Technicians who can work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

You will bring:

* Completion of, or current enrolment in, a **Certificate III or IV in Health – Sterilisation Services**
* The ability to read, understand and interpret reprocessing procedures and guidelines
* Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet operational requirements
* Effective communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with hospital staff, customers and external suppliers
* An understanding of relevant policies and procedures within a sterile processing environment
* A current National Criminal History Check, or willingness to obtain one

**What We Offer**

Working at St Vincent’s means joining a values-driven organisation that supports the wellbeing, development and success of our people. Benefits include:

* Salary packaging to increase your take-home pay
* Access to Fitness Passport
* Employee wellbeing initiatives and programs
* Confidential, solutions-focused employee counselling
* A supportive environment that encourages work/life balance
* Employee discounts and promotions through the St Vincent’s Foundation
* Convenient Fitzroy location close to public transport, cafés and the Melbourne CBD
* A culture of continuous learning and improvement

**About the Sterile Processing Centre**

The Sterile Processing Centre is responsible for the reprocessing of reusable medical devices in accordance with **AS/NZS 4187, AS 5369** and other relevant local, State and National guidelines and policies. As part of St Vincent’s Perioperative Services, the Sterile Processing Centre provides a critical service supporting the operation of St Vincent’s operating theatres and Endoscopy Suite. The department operates **24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year**, with staff rostered across all shifts.

**Working at St Vincent’s**

St Vincent’s Hospital Melbourne (SVHM) is a leading teaching, research and tertiary health service providing a diverse range of adult clinical services. Our work is guided by our values of **Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence**.

Please note that applications submitted without a cover letter will not be considered. Shortlisting will commence immediately. We encourage you to apply promptly, as the advertisement may close early if suitable applicants are identified.

We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and abilities. Inclusion is fundamental to our mission, and we value the diversity that reflects the communities we serve. jobs.title: Identity & Access Management Engineer
jobs.description:
***We're big believers in the power of IRL, so for most roles we ask Campers to work from their local Culture Amp office an average of 2 days a week to unlock connection, pace and culture together.***

**Join us on our mission to make a better world of work.**

Culture Amp is the world's leading employee experience platform, revolutionizing how 25 million employees across more than 6,000 companies create a better world of work. Culture Amp empowers companies of all sizes and industries to transform employee engagement, drive performance management, and develop high-performing teams. Powered by people science and the most comprehensive employee dataset in the world, the most innovative companies including Canva, On, Asana, Dolby, McDonalds and Nasdaq depend on Culture Amp every day.

Culture Amp is backed by leading venture capital funds and has offices in the US, UK, Germany and Australia. Culture Amp has been recognized as one of the world's top private cloud companies by Forbes and most innovative companies by Fast Company.

For more information visit cultureamp.com.

### **How you can help make a better world of work**

As our Identity & Access Management Engineer, you'll help keep Culture Amp secure, connected, and easy to work in. You'll own the day-to-day administration and continuous improvement of our identity and access environment, with a focus on Okta, application integrations, lifecycle automation, and identity governance. Your work will help ensure that every Camper has the right access at the right time, while strengthening our audit readiness and reducing manual effort across the business.

### **As part of this team of amazing humans,**

You'll work across Technology and with stakeholders throughout Culture Amp to make identity and access processes reliable, secure, and straightforward. You'll bring a practical, automation-oriented approach to managing the systems that enable Campers to do their best work.

### **You will**

* Manage day-to-day identity and access administration in Okta, including provisioning, deprovisioning, MFA resets, application access requests, and authentication, session, and device trust policies.
* Full lifecycle management of SaaS applications and maintain existing SAML, SCIM, and OIDC configurations and group mappings as Culture Amp's technology environment evolves.
* Build and own joiner, mover, and leaver workflows end to end, including automated pipelines using Okta Workflows, APIs, and SCIM to connect the HRIS to Okta.
* Configure, deploy, and continuously improve Okta Identity Governance, including access request workflows and self-service or automated approval paths aligned to access policy.
* Support audit and compliance activities by automating access certification reporting, gathering system and directory log evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits, and reviewing inactive SaaS licences and unapproved OAuth integrations.
* Contribute to configuration, optimisation and troubleshooting for other ancillary platforms as required, such as Google Workspace, Active Directory / MS Entra, Island & Jamf.

### **You have**

* Hands-on experience administering Okta or a similar identity provider, including SAML, SCIM, OIDC, MFA, lifecycle policies, and authentication, session, and device trust policies.
* Proven experience onboarding SaaS applications end to end, including SSO setup, SCIM attribute and group mapping, and troubleshooting provisioning issues.
* Experience with Okta Identity Governance or equivalent access request and identity governance tooling.
* Experience building identity lifecycle automation pipelines that connect HRIS systems to an identity provider using tools such as Okta Workflows, APIs, or SCIM.
* Familiarity with SaaS governance practices, including access certification, audit evidence, licence utilisation reviews, and OAuth or shadow IT detection.
* Familiarity with SaaS platforms, cloud providers, networking fundamentals and device management.

### **You are**

* Security-minded and thoughtful about balancing strong access controls with a simple experience for end users.
* Comfortable owning operational systems, troubleshooting issues, and improving processes rather than relying on manual workarounds.
* A clear communicator who can work pragmatically with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
* A systems thinker, who will understand the end to end picture and not just complete the task that's in front of them.

**Perks & Benefits**

At Culture Amp, our people are at the heart of our success. We offer competitive pay and a total rewards package designed to support you at work and in life. This includes:

* Equity through our Employee Share Option Program, so you can share in our long-term success
* Learning programs and coaching to help you thrive and grow
* Quarterly refresh days, an extended end-of-year break and a monthly allowance to support your wellbeing and lifestyle
* Inclusive parental leave from day one
* A MacBook and budget to set up your home workspace, enabling flexibility
* Five annual social impact days to to give back to causes that matter to you
* Medical insurance coverage for you and your family (Available for US & UK only)

Our rewards are designed to support different needs and life stages, recognising that what matters most can vary from person to person.

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds may hesitate to apply if they don't meet every requirement, but your unique experience matters. If you're interested in joining us, we strongly encourage you to apply and help us build a more diverse and impactful team.

**Accommodations & Data Privacy**

If you require reasonable accommodations or adjustments due to a disability to complete the online application or to participate in the interview process, please contact accommodations@cultureamp.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly.

Culture Amp will retain your CV & personal information for a period of two years (four years for the US) from the date of your application process completion. Culture Amp may contact you in relation to future job opportunities during this time period. For further information please see our privacy policy here or contact privacy@cultureamp.com.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer- AI/ML, AI CoE Payments Technology
jobs.description:
**Staff Software Engineer – AI/ML, Payments Technology**

**Sydney or Melbourne**

* **Build AI-powered engineering capabilities within one of Australia's largest and most critical Payments technology environments.**
* **Work at the intersection of software engineering, cloud and applied AI/ML, turning emerging AI capabilities into secure, scalable production systems.**
* **Shape how AI is engineered and adopted across Payments, creating reusable patterns, platforms and capabilities that can scale across teams.**

**Do work that matters**

Payments Technology sits at the heart of CommBank, building and operating platforms that move billions of dollars and support millions of customers and businesses every day.

We're investing in an **AI Centre of Excellence within Payments Technology** and are looking for several Staff Software Engineers to help us shape the next generation of AI-enabled engineering and payment capabilities.

This isn't about experimentation for experimentation's sake.

You'll work on practical applications of AI across Payments — from engineering productivity and intelligent automation through to agentic workflows, operational processes, investigation and exception handling.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll combine strong software engineering fundamentals with hands-on AI/ML and cloud capability to take ideas from experimentation through to secure, reliable and observable production systems.

You'll also help establish the engineering patterns, guardrails and reusable capabilities that enable other Payments teams to adopt AI safely and effectively.

**See yourself in our team**

You'll join the Payments Engineering AI Centre of Excellence, working alongside engineers, architects, product teams and specialists across the broader Payments organisation.

You'll operate as a senior technical leader — remaining hands-on while influencing architecture, engineering standards and the way teams design, build and operate AI-enabled software.

You'll have the opportunity to:

* Design, build and operate **production-grade AI/ML and GenAI solutions** in a cloud environment.
* Build backend services and AI capabilities using **Python** and modern software engineering practices.
* Design and productionise **AI agents and agentic workflows** , including orchestration, tool use, grounding and human-in-the-loop patterns.
* Work with LLMs and cloud AI platforms to solve real engineering and operational problems within Payments.
* Develop **RAG and grounding patterns** , integrating models with enterprise data, APIs and internal systems.
* Establish approaches for **evaluation, guardrails, observability and responsible AI** , helping ensure AI solutions are reliable, explainable and appropriate for a regulated environment.
* Design reusable AI services, frameworks, APIs and platform capabilities that can be adopted across multiple engineering teams.
* Apply strong cloud-native engineering principles across scalability, resilience, security and performance.
* Champion **DevSecOps and design-to-run ownership** , taking solutions from architecture and development through deployment, observability and production operations.
* Explore how AI-assisted engineering can improve software delivery, testing, operational support and developer productivity.
* Mentor engineers and help grow AI engineering capability across Payments Technology.
* Influence technical strategy and contribute to engineering standards and reference patterns for AI adoption across the organisation.

**We're interested in hearing from people who:**

We don't expect you to have experience with every technology or AI framework listed below. We're looking for strong engineers with depth across software engineering, cloud and AI/ML who are comfortable learning quickly as the technology continues to evolve.

You'll ideally:

* Bring strong **Staff-level software engineering capability** , with experience designing, building and operating complex production systems at scale.
* Have strong hands-on programming capability, particularly in **Python** , with experience building production-quality services and applications.
* Have strong experience with **cloud-native engineering** . We primarily use AWS, but experience designing and operating sophisticated solutions on Azure or GCP is also valuable, provided you're comfortable adapting to AWS.
* Have practical experience building or productionising **AI/ML or Generative AI solutions** , rather than solely consuming AI tools.
* Understand modern AI engineering concepts such as **LLM integration, agents, RAG, grounding, prompt engineering, tool use, evaluation and guardrails** .
* Understand the challenges of taking AI from prototype to production, including scalability, latency, cost, security, observability and reliability.
* Bring experience designing **APIs, microservices, distributed systems and event-driven architectures** .
* Have a strong **DevSecOps mindset** , with experience across CI/CD, automated testing, Infrastructure as Code, observability and production operations.
* Be comfortable making architectural decisions, evaluating trade-offs and providing technical direction in ambiguous or rapidly evolving areas.
* Have experience mentoring engineers and influencing technical direction across teams.

**Technology & engineering environment**

Our environment continues to evolve, so we're more interested in strong fundamentals and adaptability than experience with every individual technology.

Exposure across a number of the following would be valuable:

**AI & ML Engineering**
Generative AI, LLMs, AI agents, agentic workflows, RAG, prompt engineering, model evaluation, grounding, guardrails, responsible AI and human-in-the-loop patterns.

**Cloud & AI Platforms**
AWS, Amazon Bedrock and cloud-native architectures. Relevant Azure or GCP AI/cloud experience is also welcomed.

**Software Engineering**
Python, Java, Node.js/TypeScript, APIs, microservices and distributed systems.

**Data & Event-Driven Engineering**
Kafka/event streaming, data pipelines, vector and relational data stores, schema management and integration patterns.

**Platform & DevSecOps**
Infrastructure as Code, Terraform, Kubernetes/containers, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, observability, security and automated engineering controls.

**What great looks like**

You'll thrive in this role if you:

* Are a **strong software engineer first** , with genuine depth in AI/ML and cloud engineering.
* Enjoy turning emerging technologies into practical, production-ready capabilities.
* Can move comfortably between experimentation, architecture and hands-on engineering.
* Think beyond the model itself and consider the entire system around it — data, APIs, security, evaluation, observability, reliability and operations.
* Understand that building AI in a critical, regulated environment requires strong engineering discipline and responsible controls.
* Can take ambiguous problems and turn them into pragmatic technical solutions.
* Create reusable patterns and capabilities rather than solving the same problem independently in every squad.
* Influence engineers and technical leaders without needing direct authority.
* Stay curious and continuously experiment as AI engineering practices evolve.
* Care deeply about engineering quality, customer outcomes and building technology that can be trusted in production.

**Why Payments Technology?**

Few engineering environments combine the **scale and criticality of Payments with the opportunity presented by AI** .

You'll have the opportunity to help shape how one of Australia's largest technology organisations applies AI to real-world engineering and payment challenges — while working on systems where security, reliability and engineering excellence genuinely matter.

If you're an experienced engineer who enjoys building at scale and wants to help move AI from possibility to production, we'd love to hear from you.

If you're already part of the Commonwealth Bank Group (including Bankwest, x15ventures), you'll need to apply through Sidekick to submit a valid application. We’re keen to support you with the next step in your career.

We're aware of some accessibility issues on this site, particularly for screen reader users. We want to make finding your dream job as easy as possible, so if you require additional support please contact HR Direct on 1800 989 696.
