jobs.title: Senior Security Consultant
jobs.description:
**Security Consultant**

At Aurecon, we are optimistic about the future. We are thinkers, solvers and collaborators who work with our clients to deliver the infrastructure and assets that strengthen communities and create a sustainable future.

**What you'll do**

As a Security Consultant, you'll work with clients to design and deliver security solutions that protect some of Australia's most important infrastructure assets.

Joining a nationally connected team with a strong pipeline of work, you'll contribute to projects across Defence, Aviation, Transport, Critical Infrastructure and Data Centres. You'll work closely with clients and multidisciplinary project teams to deliver security strategies, risk assessments and security design solutions that balance operational needs, risk management and user experience.

This is an excellent opportunity for a consultant looking to grow their expertise within a specialist and increasingly important discipline while working on complex, high-profile projects across Australia.

In this role, you will:

* Contribute to security consulting and advisory projects across a range of sectors
* Undertake security risk assessments and threat and vulnerability assessments
* Support the development of security strategies and security plans
* Contribute to physical security system design, including access control, CCTV and intrusion detection systems
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering, defence and infrastructure project teams
* Assist with security compliance and regulatory requirements
* Participate in stakeholder workshops and client engagement activities
* Prepare technical reports, specifications and project documentation

**What you'll bring**

* Experience in security consulting, protective security, electronic security, Defence, law enforcement or critical infrastructure environments
* Understanding of physical security principles and risk-based security design
* Experience contributing to security strategies, assessments or security system projects
* Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
* Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams
* Experience within a consultancy environment will be highly regarded
* Australian Citizenship preferred
* Ability to obtain an Australian Defence Security Clearance

**How we support your growth**

You'll join a growing team with immediate opportunities across Defence, Aviation and Critical Infrastructure projects, including exposure to the rapidly expanding Data Centre sector.

Whether your background has been in consulting, Defence, government, infrastructure or security systems integration, you'll have the opportunity to broaden your experience while working alongside recognised industry specialists.

Recognised by the AFR as a Best Place to Work in 2026, we embrace diverse perspectives and flexible ways of working. You'll be supported by experienced leaders, a collaborative national team and genuine opportunities for career growth and development.

**Who we are**

We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is why we are here – to bring ideas to life, the Aurecon way.

**Ready for your next adventure?**

If this sounds like your next step, we'd love to hear from you. We value diverse experiences and welcome applications from Melbourne and Adelaide, as well as requests for part-time or flexible working arrangements. For recruitment adjustments, contact WorkplaceAdjustment@aurecongroup.com.

Our hiring decisions are made by people, not AI. We're most interested in your individual thinking and experiences, so please ensure your application reflects your authentic perspective.

jobs.title: Reach Legal Consultant | Real Estate Lawyer | Melbourne
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**

Join a leading education organisation in a role that will strengthen your legal career.

* **Duration:** 2 months
* **Arrangement:** Full time (hybrid)
* **Location:** Melbourne

**About You**

You are an experienced transactional real estate lawyer with a minimum of 5 years' experience, bringing a strong track record from private practice or in-house roles within large organisations.

**Your Experience & Expertise:**

* Demonstrated experience advising on a broad range of property law matters within a government, statutory authority, private practice or in-house environment
* Strong experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating leases, licences, easements and other property-related agreements
* Proven ability to advise on complex property transactions and land use matters relating to public infrastructure, education assets and government-owned land
* Experience supporting property development projects, including site feasibility assessments, title reviews and land acquisition matters
* Strong understanding of land title issues and the ability to identify legal risks associated with property ownership, development and occupation
* Experience providing legal advice on leasing and licensing arrangements involving public assets and third-party occupiers
* Familiarity with compulsory acquisition processes, native title matters and Aboriginal cultural heritage considerations
* Ability to provide strategic and practical legal advice on property disputes, land access issues and related regulatory matters
* Strong stakeholder management skills with experience supporting government agencies, project teams, school leadership and operational stakeholders
* Ability to supervise, mentor and provide technical guidance to junior lawyers and team members
* Experience managing multiple matters simultaneously while balancing competing priorities and stakeholder expectations

**Attributes:**

* Strong technical property law capability combined with practical commercial judgement
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate complex legal and operational issues
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to provide concise and practical advice to non-legal stakeholders
* Confident stakeholder manager capable of building trusted relationships across government, project and operational teams
* Collaborative and supportive leadership style with the ability to mentor and guide junior team members
* Adaptable and resilient with the ability to operate effectively in a dynamic and evolving project environment
* Strong attention to detail while maintaining focus on broader strategic and project objectives

**Requirements:**

* Current Australian practising certificate
* Right to live and work in Australia

**About Reach**

Reach is the flexible legal resourcing platform of Ashurst Perkins Coie, a global law firm with more than 3,500 legal professionals across 52 offices. Sitting within Advance, the firm's NewLaw division, we place lawyers and professionals where they're needed most — whether our clients need to meet a surge in demand, cover leave, bridge a recruitment gap, or bring in specialist expertise.

**Why join Reach?**

Reach gives you the flexibility to build a career that fits your life — not the other way around. We work with talented consultants across a broad range of specialties, matching the right people with the right opportunities.

Here's what you can expect as a Reach consultant:

* **Flexibility and choice** — control over how, when, and where you work, on terms that suit your life.
* **A genuine partnership** — a dedicated Reach team who will get to know you and actively champion your career goals.
* **The backing of a global firm** — the resources, reputation, and culture of Ashurst Perkins Coie, including access to clients doing market-leading work and a refreshingly open and inclusive community.

**Interested?**

Ready to find out more? Apply now or get in touch with Adam Saunders, our Talent Solutions Advisor, at adam.saunders@ashurstperkins.com — we'd love to hear from you.

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

With continued growth in the Data Centre sector, we're looking for an experienced Senior Associate Architect – Data Centre to join our Melbourne team and take a key architectural leadership role in the design and delivery of major data centre projects.

Working as part of our APAC Data Centre team, you'll have the opportunity to lead significant architectural design work in Australia while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams locally and internationally. Beyond individual project delivery, you'll help strengthen Jacobs' Data Centre architectural capability in Australia and support our ambition to lead more complex, multidisciplinary Data Centre design opportunities.

As an Senior Associate Architect – Data Centre, you'll lead architectural design and coordination across significant data centre work, from early master planning and concept development through detailed design, procurement and construction.

You'll be responsible for leading design concepts, documentation, specifications and reports, while coordinating architectural requirements with engineering and specialist disciplines to deliver integrated solutions.

Working with senior client stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams, you'll help translate complex operational and technical requirements into high-quality architectural outcomes suited to mission-critical environments.

You'll also:

* Lead architectural design and documentation across the project lifecycle, from concept and schematic design through detailed design and construction.
* Coordinate multidisciplinary design inputs to deliver integrated and technically robust solutions.
* Lead and support architectural and interdisciplinary teams across Australia, APAC and Jacobs' Global Integrated Delivery network.
* Work directly with senior client stakeholders to understand and document project and programmatic requirements.
* Provide design leadership while balancing project requirements across quality, programme, cost and scope.
* Review technical submissions, respond to contractor RFIs and undertake site visits where required.
* Mentor junior and mid-level architects and contribute to knowledge sharing across the wider Data Centre team.
* Proficiency in digital tools such including Revit, with experience in Rhino and BIM coordination workflows.
* Contribute to the continued development of Jacobs' Data Centre architectural capability and our ability to deliver increasingly complex projects across the region.

Here's what you'll need

Demonstrated architectural design and delivery experience on Data Centre projects is essential for this position. We're looking for someone who understands the particular technical, operational, coordination and documentation demands of Data Centre environments and can bring that experience into a senior design leadership role.

You'll also bring:

* A recognised architectural qualification and registration as an Architect.
* A minimum of 15 years' relevant local architectural experience.
* Strong Data Centre architectural design and project delivery experience.
* Strong design management capability from concept through detailed design and delivery.
* Knowledge of construction documentation, contract administration, materials, Australian building codes, relevant standards, particularly within Data Centre environments.
* Experience working directly with senior client stakeholders to establish and document project requirements.
* Strong multidisciplinary coordination skills and experience working with engineering and specialist consultants.
* Demonstrated experience supervising and directing design professionals.
* Strong client management, communication, and leadership capabilities.
* Sound commercial acumen, including experience managing project programmes and budgets.
* The ability to lead effectively across geographically dispersed and international project teams.

**Why Join Us?**

* Strong project pipeline and long-term growth opportunities working on industry-leading data centre projects
* Exposure to our high-profile hyperscale and enterprise clients
* Collaborate with our team of leading architects, engineers, and digital infrastructure specialists
* Develop your career in one of the fastest-growing sectors globally of mission-critical, sustainable, and AI-ready facilities

This role offers the opportunity to combine hands-on design leadership with a broader contribution to the future of Jacobs' Data Centre architecture capability. You'll be part of a connected APAC and global team, with the opportunity to share knowledge, mentor others and help us grow our ability to lead the design of complex Data Centre projects.

**Jacobs. A world where you can.**

With safety and flexibility always top of mind, we’ve gone beyond traditional ways of working so you have the support, means and space to maximize your potential. You’ll uncover flexible working arrangements, benefits and opportunities, from well-being benefits to our global giving and volunteering program, to exploring new and inventive ways to help our clients make the world a better place. We accept people for who they are, and we champion the richness of diverse perspectives, lived experiences and backgrounds in the workplace, as a source of learning and innovation. We are committed to building vibrant communities within Jacobs, including through our Jacobs Employee Networks, Communities of Practice and our Find Your Community initiatives, allowing every employee to find connection, purpose, and belonging. Find out more about our Jacobs Employee Networks here.

Our meticulously curated employee benefits support ALL employees throughout every stage of life. From paid parental leave to a lifetime financial allowance for you and your partner to access family forming Fertility & IVF treatment, adoption and surrogacy assistance along with menopause and Low T treatment.

We are steadfast in our commitment to the wellbeing of you and your loved ones with a comprehensive suite of wellbeing resources supporting you physically, emotionally and financially. This is demonstrated in our company being recognised by WGEA for 12 consecutive years as an employer of choice for gender equality along with our industry leading GOLD employer status by the Australian Workplace Equality Index.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are invited to nominate a cultural representative to participate on the interview panel; please let your recruiter know in your application. jobs.title: Enterprise PM Practice Associate
jobs.description:
*Help keep projects moving across Healthscope - coordinate delivery, support project teams and improve the tools and practices behind our enterprise portfolio. Location - Melbourne.*

* *Hands*-on role helping Project Managers and teams keep delivery organised, visible and moving
* Work across a diverse enterprise portfolio of projects, engaging with business, clinical, technology and supplier stakeholders
* Support Microsoft Planner and improve practical project tools, governance and ways of working

**About the role:**

Healthscope is seeking a full-time Enterprise PM Practice Associate to help our Project Managers and initiative owners deliver projects effectively across the organisation. Reporting to the PM Practice Manager, you will be close to the day-to-day work - coordinating inputs, following up actions, tracking milestones and dependencies, maintaining risks and registers, supporting suppliers, and preparing clear governance and management information.

Alongside this hands-on delivery support, you will support Healthscope’s PPM toolset with primary responsibility for Microsoft Planner and related Microsoft 365 components and help improve the templates, processes and methods used by the project management practice. The role will suit someone who enjoys bringing structure to complex work, solving practical problems and making it easier for others to deliver.

**About us:**

Healthscope is one of Australia’s leading private healthcare providers, with hospitals and support services across the country. Our Support Office works with hospital and corporate teams to help deliver the services and initiatives that support patient care and the communities we serve.

You will join an enterprise project management practice supporting projects and programs across Healthscope. The team is focused on practical delivery: providing useful structure, clear information and fit-for-purpose tools and governance that help teams get work done.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Keep delivery activity organised by tracking schedules, milestones, dependencies, resources, risks, issues and actions, and following up agreed commitments
* Work closely with Project Managers, initiative owners, business and clinical stakeholders, technical teams and suppliers to coordinate inputs and keep delivery on track
* Maintain accurate project and portfolio information, including plans, registers, decision logs, approval records and supporting documentation
* Prepare clear governance papers, management reports and briefing material that highlight progress, risks, exceptions and decisions required
* Coordinate supplier and contractor inputs and escalate material changes to cost, timing, scope or commitments for management review
* Administer and support Microsoft Planner and related Microsoft 365 PPM components, including Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft Lists, Power Automate and Power BI
* Configure and maintain plans, templates, permissions, workflows, integrations and reporting structures, and provide first-line support for user and process questions
* Support onboarding, training and adoption, and identify practical improvements to usability, data quality and management reporting
* Help improve project management frameworks, templates and ways of working so they are consistent, scalable and practical for delivery teams

**What you will bring:**

* A relevant tertiary qualification in project management, business, information technology or a related discipline, or equivalent industry experience
* Project management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2 or AgilePM is also highly regarded
* Experience in a hands-on project, program or portfolio coordination, PMO or governance role within a medium to large, complex organisation, preferably in healthcare, technology or another regulated service environment
* Strong organisation and follow-through, with the ability to keep multiple activities, actions, risks and dependencies moving at the same time
* Confident communication and stakeholder skills, with the ability to work constructively with Project Managers, business and clinical stakeholders, suppliers, technical teams and senior leaders
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to make sense of delivery information, identify issues and produce clear management reporting
* Hands-on experience with Microsoft Planner or a comparable PPM/project delivery tool; experience administering Planner in an organisational environment is highly regarded
* Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 tools such as Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft Lists and Power Automate; Power BI experience is an advantage
* Experience working with project templates, workflows, permissions, data and reporting, and an appreciation of good data quality and access controls
* Practical knowledge of project delivery approaches such as Agile, waterfall or hybrid methods and the governance needed to support them .
* A continuous-improvement mindset and the ability to turn delivery needs into simple, workable improvements to tools, templates and processes
* Sound judgement, attention to detail and resilience in a changing environment

**Why Healthscope?**

When you join Healthscope, you become part of our Community of Care. Our people are at the heart of our organisation - no matter the role, every day our people make a difference to the lives of our patients and their families. Our hospitals are supported by our central Support Office, enabling them to provide an exceptional experience for the communities we care for.

**You’ll also benefit from:**

* Broad exposure to projects and programs across a national healthcare organisation
* A role where you can make a visible difference to how project teams work and how effectively delivery is managed
* The opportunity to work with experienced Project Managers, senior stakeholders and teams across Healthscope
* Discounted health insurance for eligible non-casual employees
* A values-led workplace guided by: We care. We do. We strive. We’re a team

We support each other, share learnings, celebrate successes and face challenges together.

***Come and be the difference in our patients' lives.***

**Applications Close:** 17th September 2026

To apply: Please click on the 'Apply' button to be taken to our online application form. For questions about the role, please contact careers@healthscope.com.au

**More Information:**

Our commitment to quality and safety for our patients, staff and visitors is our highest priority. We are also committed to child safety and to the safety, participation and empowerment of all children. Applicants will be required to provide a current National Police Check, a Working with Children Check where applicable, and evidence of their right to work in Australia before appointment.

Healthscope has been made aware of recruitment scams involving individuals falsely claiming to represent Healthscope. Healthscope will never request payment from candidates.

Any request for payment is fraudulent.

Visit ScamWatch for more information on recruitment scams.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant - Country Road Group
jobs.description:
* 1001932

* Melbourne - CBD & Inner, VIC

* Full-Time

* Closing on: 31 Aug 2026

*As an Executive Assistant, you’ll be a trusted partner to your executive, helping them stay focused, organised and ahead of what’s coming. You’ll bring strong judgement, organisation and attention to detail to a fast-paced role, managing competing priorities, anticipating needs and coordinating across the business to keep things moving.*

Reporting to the Executive Operations Manager and working within a collaborative, team-based Exec Ops model, you'll seamlessly manage complex calendars, communications and day-to-day business activities while building strong relationships across the organisation.

You'll thrive in a fast-paced environment, using sound judgement, initiative and adaptability to anticipate needs, solve problems before they arise, and support your executive.

**How You Will Contribute**

* Partner closely with your executive, anticipating needs so they can stay focused on strategic priorities
* Manage a complex, high-volume calendar — prioritising against business needs, minimising conflicts and protecting time for what matters
* Prepare, review and refine executive presentations, reports and papers, including risk, governance and Board submissions
* Coordinate leadership meetings end to end: agendas, materials, logistics, minutes, actions and follow-through
* Support strategic initiatives, research and special projects — preparing briefing materials so your executive is well prepared
* Track key projects and deliverables across the portfolio, keeping deadlines and commitments visible
* Act as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders, screening and prioritising incoming requests and resolving or redirecting them
* Coordinate domestic and international travel, itineraries, expenses and credit card reconciliations
* Contribute actively to EA meetings and initiatives, working collaboratively with EAs across the business and providing backup support as needed
* Handle highly confidential information — supplier commercials, governance matters and organisational change — with complete discretion
* Support function-wide engagement activities including huddles, offsites and team events, delivered within budget

**What You Will Bring**

* Proven experience as an Executive Assistant supporting C-suite or ELT executives in a fast-paced, complex organisation
* Strong background in complex calendar and travel management, executive-level communication and meeting coordination
* Confident with systems and digital tools, and quick to adopt new ways of working
* Experience supporting governance, risk or Board-level documentation (highly regarded)
* Advanced Microsoft 365 skills — Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive
* Exceptional organisational skills, attention to detail, time management and problem solving
* The ability to engage, influence and build trust with senior leaders and across diverse stakeholder groups
* Adaptability and resilience — managing competing priorities and changing deadlines without losing accuracy
* Complete integrity in managing confidential information
* A genuine partnership mentality, and a collaborative approach to working as part of a function rather than in isolation

**What We Offer**

* Bi-annual product allowance, access to sample sales and 40% discount for you and your immediate family across all CRG brands
* Flex your leave your way, including birthday leave, volunteer leave, personal leave and more
* Access to health and wellbeing support, including Health Insurance, 24/7 EAP counselling and financial advice services
* 18 weeks paid parental leave for eligible employees, with a return-to-work clothing allowance
* Internal career opportunities across our House of Brands
* An annual learning calendar to support your ongoing development
* Support for impactful community and charity partnerships across our House of Brands, including OCRF, Our Watch, First Nations Reconciliation, Movember, Red Cross and Landcare

**Who We Are**

Country Road Group is one of Australia's leading lifestyle group of brands, home to an iconic portfolio including Country Road, Trenery, Witchery, Mimco and Politix. United as One Team, we work collaboratively to create exceptional product and meaningful experiences for our customers. We are Courageously Curious, exploring new ideas, perspectives and ways of working, and Driven by Purpose to make a positive impact — on our customers, our communities and each other. We're proud to foster an inclusive culture where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and has the opportunity to grow.

Recognised as a sustainability leader in Australian fashion, Country Road Group drives positive change through ambitious climate action, ethical sourcing and responsible product innovation.

We encourage you to explore our Current Opportunities and we look forward to connecting with you!

Country Road Group acknowledges the Traditional Owners of Country throughout Australia and recognises their continuing connection to lands, waters and communities. We pay our respects to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures and to Elders past and present.

We're committed to inclusion and accessibility. If we can support you with any adjustments at any stage, please let us know.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer - Azure Cloud & DevOps
jobs.description:
LAB3 is one of the largest Azure engineering practices in the Australasia region with a focus on Cloud & DevOps, Data, IoT & AI, Modern Workplace, Modern Apps & Integration, Security, and Network services.

We are looking for NV1 security cleared Principal Engineers, ideally based in Canberra, with deep experience in Azure Cloud & DevOps to lead, deliver and support the execution of technical solutions that meet our clients’ needs. We are open to permanent and contract employees- with multiple roles open, we are likely to take a mix of both.

The role

* Act as the lead Engineer for technical client engagements in delivering and overseeing Azure assessments, solutions, and implementations for our client(s)
* Engineer, advise and implement on appropriate state-of-the-art technical patterns on Azure
* Provide technical reviews on architecture and design deliverables whilst supporting engagements as a SME.
* Participate in the consultation between LAB3 and clients to understand strategic business requirements and translate those into effective cloud solutions.
* Communicate and present discoveries to senior management and executive stakeholders
* Partner with the Project Managers to provide technical input into scheduling, estimating activities and project delivery
* Support our pre-sales teams with documentation, design and transformative direction. Help setup proof-of-concept prototypes
* Identify, interpret, and communicate meaningful insights via workshops, presentations, and reports
* Run workshops and cloud adoption activities with our customers as necessary.
* Recommend client value creation initiatives and implement industry best practices
* Provide technical leadership and be a role model to the engineers.

**The ideal candidate:**
**Will demonstrate strong engineering skills in the following:**

* Azure IaaS/PaaS/SaaS
* IaC – Terraform, PowerShell
* Azure DevOps
* Cloud Automation – Bash, Python, Ansible
* Azure Resource Manager - ARM Templates and Bicep
* Azure Functions, Key Vault & Back ups
* Azure Network, Azure Security, Azure IAM and RBAC Design
* Azure Security Centre Operations
* Azure Management Groups & Subscription Management
* PowerShell module creation and management

Experience with Open-source containers (AKS Kubernetes) is desirable.

What's in it for you?

* Be part of a team that leverages modern technologies to solve real problems and provides top level of customer satisfaction
* Work with a Microsoft Partner of the Year award winner with multiple specialisations
* Be supported by experienced peers and leaders that value technical expertise and encourage innovation, with clear career pathways and ongoing learning
* Enjoy a supportive workplace that promotes inclusion, flexibility, diversity, and celebrates differences.
* Take advantage of largely working from home in our remote/hybrid workplace and enjoy the flexibility to balance your life
* Thrive in a community with strong values #BeTrue #TeamUp #StandOut #ThinkAhead #FearLessAchieveMore

Apply now, call or connect on LinkedIn for further information.

jobs.title: Research Solutions Architect
jobs.description:
**Acknowledgement of Country**

CSIRO acknowledges the Traditional Owners of the land, sea and waters, of the area that we live and work on across Australia. We acknowledge their continuing connection to their culture and pay our respects to their Elders past and present. View our vision towards reconciliation.

**Role highlights**

* **Bridge biology, data and software to solve complex challenges**
* **Build scalable cloud solutions for genomic research**
* **Work alongside leading scientists and engineers**

**About CSIRO**

As Australia's national science agency, CSIRO is solving the greatest challenges through innovative science and technology. Many of our iconic innovations were once considered impossible until someone, just like you, joined us and took on the challenge.

Visit CSIRO.au for more information.

**The opportunity**

Join CSIRO's Bioinformatics Products team and help shape the future of genomics-enabled biosecurity.

As a Research Solutions Architect, you will work at the intersection of biology, bioinformatics and software engineering to design and deliver innovative cloud-based solutions that enable researchers to manage, analyse and interpret complex genomic data at scale. Working closely with scientists, engineers and external collaborators, you'll translate research challenges into practical technical solutions that support biosecurity research, surveillance and response activities.

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to nationally significant research while applying modern software engineering, cloud computing and data analytics approaches to real-world biological problems. You will play a key role in developing scalable platforms, exploring novel computational and machine learning approaches, and helping researchers make effective use of genomic data across health, environmental and biosecurity domains.

You'll thrive in this role if you're a collaborative problem solver who enjoys working with multidisciplinary teams, communicating across both scientific and technical audiences, and building solutions that have tangible research impact.

**Your high-level duties will include:**

* Collaborating with scientists to design and implement innovative cloud architecture that supports impactful research and addresses challenges in the health and life science domain.
* Contributing to the design, building, testing and maintenance of software applications and platforms that support the management and analysis of genomic data.
* Working closely with researchers and stakeholders to translate scientific requirements into scalable technical solutions, system designs and software architectures.
* Providing technical advice, guidance and support to researchers and stakeholders to facilitate the effective uptake and use of developed solutions.
* Applying contemporary software engineering and DevOps practices, including version control, testing, automation and deployment workflows, to ensure robust and maintainable solutions.

**Role particulars**

**Location and office arrangements:** Sydney, NSW; Adelaide, SA; Brisbane, QLD; Canberra, ACT; or Melbourne, VIC. Hybrid working options available

**Salary:** AU$118k – AU$127k per annum (pro rata for part-time), plus 15.4% superannuation

**Tenure & work schedule:** Specified term of 2 years

**Reference**: 103862

**As the successful candidate, you will bring:**

**Essential criteria**

* A bachelor’s degree (or will shortly satisfy the requirements of a bachelor’s degree) or equivalent work experience in a relevant discipline area, such as Information Technology, Bioinformatics, Electrical Engineering, Data Science.
* Proven impact from developing solutions on public cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) or advanced high-performance compute (HPC) with demonstrated software engineering practices (use of repositories, deployment standards, efficiency analysis).
* Advanced data analytics and programming capabilities in more than one language relevant for bioinformatics (e.g. Python, Rust, Java, C++, Scala, BASH, R, Julia).
* The ability to build productive relationships and work effectively within multidisciplinary, geographically dispersed teams, while exercising initiative and sound judgement to deliver work independently.
* High level written and verbal communication skills including the ability to explain complex technical concepts to scientific and non-scientific audiences and contribute to reports, presentations, or other forms of knowledge sharing.

Candidates who also demonstrate one or more of the following will be particularly competitive:

* Experience/familiarity with Frontend development using React/Angular.
* Background in, or exposure to, biology, genomics, bioinformatics or a related scientific discipline.
* Experience sharing research outcomes with diverse audiences through online media, including blogs, videos, social media or other digital communication channels (e.g. Blogs, X (formally Twitter), YouTube).
* Experience in DevOps.

For full details about this role, and other criteria, please review the **Position Description**.

**Not sure if you meet all the criteria?**

While it is CSIRO policy that the successful candidate must meet all the essential criteria, there are many ways to demonstrate this. Don’t let the list discourage you. If you are unsure about applying, please reach out to the contact person in the Position Description.

**Setting you up for success**

We are committed to providing a recruitment process that is fair, equitable and accessible to everyone. We recognise that it may be helpful for us to adjust our process to make it equitable for your individual situation. Please contact Cristina O’Brien via email at cristina.obrien@csiro.au and let us know how we can support you.

**Life at CSIRO and flexible work arrangements**

We work flexibly at CSIRO, offering a range of options for how, when and where you work. We can discuss flexible work arrangements with you during the recruitment process. CSIRO also offers a range of leave entitlements, benefits and career development opportunities. To find out more, visit Careers at CSIRO.

**Inclusion and belonging**

Solving Australia's greatest challenges takes a diversity of minds and lived experiences. We know diverse teams are more effective and deliver more innovative outcomes. As an equal employment opportunity organisation, we are committed to creating diverse and inclusive teams where people feel they belong. We recognise true diversity encompasses all ages, abilities, cultures, faiths, levels of education, genders, sexualities, diversity of thought and much more. We focus on hiring people who share our values of People First, Further Together, Making it Real and Trusted.

CSIRO holds Gold Status for the Australian Workplace Equality Index for LGBTQIA+ inclusion, and a Science in Australia Gender Equity Bronze Award.

**Eligibility**

Applications for this position are open to Australian Citizens, New Zealand Citizens, and Australian Permanent Residents who are currently onshore. Appointment to this role is subject to provision of a national police check and may be subject to other security/medical/character requirements.

**Child safety**

CSIRO is committed to the safety and wellbeing of all children and young people involved in our activities and programs. View our Child Safe Policy.

**How to apply**

Please apply online and submit a cover letter (maximum 2 pages) and CV that demonstrate your motivation and ability to meet the essential requirements of this role.

**Applications close**

Monday 31 August 2026, 11:00pm AEST

* Hands-on Kubernetes experience, preferably Azure Kubernetes Service
* Experience with internal developer platforms, golden paths, self-service provisioning or reusable platform modules
* Strong infrastructure-as-code capability using Terraform or equivalent tooling
* Working knowledge of continuous integration and delivery, GitOps, cloud-native deployment and Azure

**Salary:** $142,790 - $191,084

**Grade:** VPS 6

**Location:** Melbourne - CBD and Inner Metro suburbs

**Reference:** 2120

This position is part of the Automation and DevOps team responsible for managing the BFS software delivery and operational automation, encompassing the design, implementation, and support of continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, including extensive use of Infrastructure as Code.The Principal DevOps engineer takes a leading role in designing, implementing and supporting software delivery workflows and automation frameworks, primarily within a Microsoft Azure environment, but also including systems hosted within AWS. The responsibilities of this position include the management of CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration, application monitoring, platform and developer team tooling, and release processes, working closely with software, data, and cloud platform engineers to streamline the implementation and support of bespoke solutions built using cloud native technology. * Strong development background in CI/CD strategies and software, particularly with GitHub Actions (or similar).
* Strong understanding of cloud platform services and significant hands-on experience in managing cloud platform infrastructure, ideally in an Azure environment.
* Strong development background with PowerShell, Bash, and/or Python and common platform automation scripting practices.
* Demonstrated experience leading technical implementations, establishing best practices, and mentoring other engineers.
* Experience with version control systems such as Git and GitHub

* Experience with network design, configuration and management, ideally in an Azure environment.
* Familiarity with Ansible.
* A strong understanding of cloud authentication and security principles.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills.

* Experience in multi-cloud environments, especially Azure and AWS.
* Experience designing cloud platform solutions.
* Experience leading technology implementation projects.
* A strong understanding of application monitoring, disaster recovery, backup and availability practices
* Experience using JIRA and Confluence.

jobs.title: Aboriginal Health Worker Trainee
jobs.description:
**Aboriginal Healthcare Worker Traineeship**

### **Salary: $72,000 base salary plus superannuation**

### **Location: Various Sites across Victoria**

**About the Opportunity**

**Launch your career in Aboriginal Health with a fully paid traineeship that's designed to support your success.**

GEO Healthcare is offering a unique opportunity for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to begin a rewarding and meaningful career in healthcare while earning a full-time wage.

As an Aboriginal Healthcare Worker Trainee, you will be employed full-time by GEO Healthcare while we sponsor and support you to complete a nationally recognised qualification in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Primary Health Care.

This is more than just a traineeship it's a pathway to a long-term healthcare career where you can make a genuine difference to the health and wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.

Throughout the program, you will gain practical, hands-on experience working alongside experienced Aboriginal Health Workers and Health Practitioners, while developing the knowledge and skills required to become a qualified Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Health Practitioner.

### **What's on offer?**

* Full-time paid employment while you study
* Salary of $72,000 plus superannuation
* GEO Healthcare-sponsored qualification
* Paid study leave and dedicated learning support
* On-the-job mentoring from experienced Aboriginal Health professionals
* A nationally recognised healthcare qualification
* A clear pathway into a rewarding long-term career in Aboriginal Health
* Guaranteed practical experience in a healthcare setting from day one
* Ongoing employment opportunities upon successful completion of the traineeship

**Why Join GEO Healthcare?**

GEO Healthcare is committed to improving health outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people through culturally safe, holistic and person centred healthcare.

As a Trainee Aboriginal Health Worker, you will play an important role in supporting the health and wellbeing of Aboriginal patients within a correctional healthcare environment. You will work as part of a multidisciplinary healthcare team that is dedicated to delivering culturally responsive care and advocating for the unique cultural and healthcare needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

This is a rare opportunity to build a professional healthcare career while making a meaningful contribution to your community.

**About GEO Healthcare**

GEO Healthcare employs highly skilled multidisciplinary healthcare teams to ensure people in custody can access the healthcare services they need.

GEO Healthcare operates across all Victorian men's public prisons, delivering comprehensive primary healthcare services to people in prison.

GEO Healthcare is a subsidiary of The GEO Group Australia Pty Ltd, a company that has been providing correctional and healthcare services throughout Australia for more than 30 years.

**What You'll Be Doing**

During your traineeship, you will work under the supervision of experienced Aboriginal Health Workers and Aboriginal Health Practitioners, receiving ongoing support and mentoring throughout your learning journey.

Overall supervision of the traineeship program is provided by the Manager, Aboriginal Health within GEO Healthcare.

You will gain practical experience in:

* Delivering culturally safe healthcare services
* Supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients to access healthcare
* Health promotion and education
* Assisting with primary healthcare programs
* Working collaboratively with healthcare professionals
* Advocating for the cultural and health needs of Aboriginal patients
* Developing clinical skills within a professional healthcare environment

**Who Can Apply?**

To be eligible, applicants must:

* Be 18 years of age or older.
* Identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander.
* Be of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent.

*(An applicant's race is a genuine occupational qualification and is authorised under Section 14 of the Equal Opportunity Act.)*

Applicants should also demonstrate:

* A genuine interest in pursuing a career in Aboriginal Health.
* A commitment to undertaking the Certificate IV in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Primary Health Care Practice as part of the traineeship.
* An understanding of the health and social issues affecting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
* The ability to engage and communicate respectfully and effectively with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and communities.

**Qualifications Supported Through the Traineeship**

GEO Healthcare will sponsor and support trainees to complete one of the following nationally recognised qualifications:

* **Certificate III in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Primary Health Care**
* **Certificate IV in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Primary Health Care Practice**

Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) Approved Programs of Study.

### **Course Duration**

**18 months to 2 years**

**Start Your Career in Aboriginal Health**

If you are passionate about supporting your community and want to develop a rewarding healthcare career, this traineeship offers a unique opportunity to earn a full-time salary, gain valuable workplace experience, and achieve a nationally recognised qualification with the support of GEO Healthcare.

**Apply today and take the first step towards becoming an Aboriginal Health Practitioner.**

**How to Apply:**

To apply, we ask that you complete the short questionnaire below and attach a cover letter and current resume. Geo Healthcare offers support to anyone interested in our opportunity.

**To obtain further information about the application and recruitment process, please contact Malcolm Timbery, Manager Aboriginal Health on 0499 314 388.**

**Make a real difference – Apply Now!**

People with diverse backgrounds and Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander applicants are strongly encouraged to apply.

We are always looking for people to join or company who share the values that we stand for:

**UNDERSTANDING RESPECT ACCOUNTABLE TEAMWORK EXCELLENCE**

jobs.title: Account Manager, Enterprise
jobs.description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We're a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can't wait to meet you.

### **WHAT YOU'LL DO**

**Team Overview:**
The Braze ANZ Account Management team drives commercial growth and retention across our existing customer base. In this enterprise role you will act as the senior commercial owner of our largest and most complex customers in the region, operating as a strategic partner to the executives who set their engagement agenda. You will orchestrate teams across Braze to convert product adoption into measurable business outcomes, and turn those outcomes into multi year commercial growth.

**Responsibilities:**

* Own commercial strategy and performance for a portfolio of Braze's largest enterprise customers in ANZ, with full accountability for renewal, expansion and long term revenue growth
* Build and sustain relationships at C suite and functional leadership level, positioning Braze as a strategic partner
* Multi thread across business units, brands and markets so that coverage holds through stakeholder change and reorganisation
* Partner with Customer Success, Solutions Consulting, Services and Partners to run joint account plans and executive business reviews that connect Braze performance to enterprise business outcomes
* Lead complex commercial negotiations, including multi year, multi product and consumption based structures, working with Deal Desk, Legal and Finance through formal procurement processes
* Build the commercial case for expansion, translating usage data, whitespace mapping and maturity assessment into proposals that stand up to executive and finance scrutiny
* Identify and mitigate retention risk early, using account health, adoption signals and stakeholder mapping to protect the base
* Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual expansion and retention targets
* Maintain accurate renewal and expansion forecasts, with a clear view of deal progression, risk, timing and dependencies
* Coordinate Braze executive sponsorship, aligning senior sponsors to the accounts where they carry the most weight
* Lead customer meetings virtually and in person, with regular domestic and occasional international travel

### **WHO YOU ARE**

You are a commercially minded enterprise Account Manager who is credible in the boardroom and rigorous in the detail. You have a proven record of growing and defending large SaaS accounts, you are comfortable navigating complex organisations and long procurement cycles, and you thrive in a high performance, cross functional environment.

**Requirements:**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in SaaS sales, account management or similar, with demonstrated success driving revenue growth, retention and strategic value for enterprise customers
* Minimum 5 years owning complex enterprise relationships end to end, including full accountability for renewals, upsell and expansion across multi product, multi brand or multi region portfolios
* Experience managing portfolios or individual accounts with annual contract values from 500K to 2M+
* Proven success negotiating multi year enterprise agreements through procurement, legal and finance, including commercial restructures and consumption based models
* Demonstrated ability to influence at C suite level, with a clear track record of value based selling and enterprise account growth
* Experience in the Martech, Adtech or broader CX space is highly regarded, including CRM, marketing automation, customer analytics, email or content marketing
* Strong commercial and financial fluency, with the ability to build ROI and value cases that survive executive scrutiny
* Excellent collaborator with a proven ability to work across Customer Success, Services, Marketing, Partnerships and Sales to drive customer outcomes and commercial impact
* Exceptional communicator, a confident presenter, persuasive writer and trusted relationship builder with strong verbal, written and numerical fluency
* Strong organisational discipline, comfortable holding several complex commercial cycles in motion at once
* Self starter with a high level of accountability, drive and commercial judgement

**WHAT WE OFFER**

*Braze benefits vary by location, and we encourage you to review our specific benefits offerings for each country* *here**. More details on benefits plans will be provided if you receive an offer of employment.*

From offering comprehensive benefits to fostering hybrid ways of working, we've got you covered so you can prioritize work-life harmony. Braze offers benefits such as:

* Competitive compensation that may include equity
* Retirement and Employee Stock Purchase Plans
* Flexible paid time off
* Comprehensive benefit plans covering medical, dental, vision, life, and disability
* Family services that include fertility benefits and equal paid parental leave
* Professional development supported by formal career pathing, learning platforms, and a yearly learning stipend
* A curated in-office employee experience, designed to foster community, team connections, and innovation
* Opportunities to give back to your community, including an annual company-wide Volunteer Week and donation matching
* Employee Resource Groups that provide supportive communities within Braze
* Collaborative, transparent, and fun culture recognized as a Great Place to Work®

**ABOUT BRAZE**

Braze is the leading customer engagement platform that empowers brands to Be Absolutely Engaging™. Braze helps brands deliver great customer experiences that drive value both for consumers and for their businesses. Built on a foundation of composable intelligence, BrazeAI™ allows marketers to combine and activate AI agents, models, and features at every touchpoint throughout the Braze Customer Engagement Platform for smarter, faster, and more meaningful customer engagement. From cross-channel messaging and journey orchestration to Al-powered decisioning and optimization, Braze enables companies to turn action into interaction through autonomous, 1:1 personalized experiences.

The company has been consistently recognized as a Leader in marketing technology by industry analysts, and was named a G2 "Best of Marketing and Digital Advertising Software Product" in 2026. Braze was also named a 2026 Best Places to Work by Built In, a 2025 America's Greenest Companies by Newsweek, and a 2025 Fortune Best Workplace in Technology™ by Great Place To Work®. Braze is also proudly certified as a Great Place to Work® in the U.S., the UK, Australia, and Singapore.

The company is headquartered in New York with offices in Austin, Berlin, Bucharest, Chicago, Dubai, Jakarta, London, Paris, San Francisco, São Paulo, Singapore, Seoul, Sydney and Tokyo.

**BRAZE IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER**

At Braze, we strive to create equitable growth and opportunities inside and outside the organization.

Building meaningful connections is at the heart of everything we do, and that includes our recruiting practices. We're committed to offering all candidates a fair, accessible, and inclusive experience – regardless of age, color, disability, gender identity, marital status, maternity, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or status as a protected veteran. When applying and interviewing with Braze, we want you to feel comfortable showcasing what makes you *you*.

We know that sometimes different circumstances can lead talented people to hesitate to apply for a role unless they meet 100% of the criteria. If this sounds familiar, we encourage you to apply, as we'd love to meet you.

**OUR AI-POWERED BRAZE RECRUITMENT PROCESS**

At Braze, we're committed to a fair and transparent candidate experience. To help our recruitment teams focus on what matters most — the person behind each application — we use AI-assisted tools at certain stages of our recruitment process.

This includes using AI to analyze the experience, skills and qualifications in your application materials to help with screening and prioritizing candidates. Such screening may amount to a form of solely automated decision-making. We also use AI for administrative support, like scheduling and recording interviews and summarizing interview notes. Our recruiting teams remain responsible for all hiring decisions and are involved throughout the process.

Depending on where you are located, you may have the right to request further information about how AI is used in our recruitment process, to opt out of AI-assisted review, to request a manual review of any decision made or to contest a decision.

Please contact us at talentdata.privacy@braze.com for any requests or questions.To find out more about our hiring process, check out this page.

**Notice Regarding Automated Employment Decision Tool (NYC Local Law 144)**

Our use of AI during the application review process may include the use of automated employment decision tools. Pursuant to New York City Local Law 144, for roles based in New York City, or if you reside in New York City, you have the right to request an alternative selection process or a reasonable accommodation instead of AI-assisted review. Please submit any such request to our Talent Acquisition team at talentdata.privacy@braze.com promptly after applying. A summary of the most recent bias audit results for such tool is available here*.*

*Please see our* *Candidate Privacy Policy* *for more information on how Braze processes your personal information during the recruitment process and, if applicable based on your location, how you can exercise any privacy rights.*

This role plays a key part in cost estimation, procurement, supplier coordination, material tracking, quality assurance and project administration, ensuring facade packages are delivered safely, efficiently and to the highest standard. Acting as a central point of coordination between project teams, subcontractors, suppliers, international manufacturing partners and clients. The role is instrumental in maintaining accurate project documentation, managing procurement and logistics activities, supporting tender submissions, and ensuring compliance with project specifications, quality standards and regulatory requirements.**

###### **WHAT HICKORY CAN OFFER**

* Previous exposure to international suppliers, manufacturing partners or global supply chains will be highly regarded.

jobs.title: ServiceNow Support Analyst
jobs.description:
**Overview**

**Work Type:** Fixed-term - Full-time

**Salary:** $81,496 - $98,955

**Grade:** VPS 3

**Occupation:** IT and telecommunications

**Location:** Melbourne - CBD and Inner Metro suburbs

**Reference:** VG/DE/FPIS/1944764

An exciting opportunity is available at the Department of Education for a ServiceNow Support Analyst to assist with the support, development, and maintenance of the platform and the hosted applications. You will continue to build on your experience and knowledge of system administration, configuration, troubleshooting, and issue resolution on the platform.

This role will work closely with senior developers and other team members to develop and support ServiceNow solutions across the entire application development lifecycle. Our team prides itself on a fun and inclusive culture, with team members passionate about providing service excellence, and building fit for purpose solutions to support our corporate and school staff.

**About the Role**

An exciting opportunity is available at the Department of Education for a ServiceNow Support Analyst to assist with the support, development, and maintenance of the platform and the hosted applications. You will continue to build on your experience and knowledge of system administration, configuration, troubleshooting, and issue resolution on the platform.

This role will work closely with senior developers and other team members to develop and support ServiceNow solutions across the entire application development lifecycle. Our team prides itself on a fun and inclusive culture, with team members passionate about providing service excellence, and building fit for purpose solutions to support our corporate and school staff.

This is a **Fixed Term Full-time opportunity until 30 June 2028.**

**Skills, Experience and Qualifications**

To be successful in the ServiceNow Support Analyst role you will be able to demonstrate your passion, skills and experience across the following:

* Understanding of ServiceNow tables, fields, forms, lists, business rules, client scripts, UI policies, workflows/flows and access controls.
* Demonstrated ability to undertake simple ServiceNow configuration and development tasks under established standards and guidance.
* Understanding of software development and testing practices, including requirements analysis, development, testing and deployment.
* Demonstrated ability to triage, queue manage, troubleshoot and resolve straightforward ServiceNow platform and application issues.
* Understanding of IT service management principles (ITIL), particularly incident, request, problem and change management.
* Experience working in an Agile/Scrum development environment.
* Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to manage and prioritise competing tasks.
* Good written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work collaboratively with developers, technical specialists and business stakeholders.
* Commitment to information security, privacy and appropriate handling of organisational information.

**You will also ideally have (desirable):**

* ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) or other relevant certifications
* Experience with JavaScript and web technologies such as HTML/CSS.
* Experience with ServiceNow Flow Designer, Business Rules, Client Scripts, Script Includes, UI Policies and ACLs.
* Experience developing or maintaining ServiceNow catalogue items, record producers, forms and workflows.
* Experience with automated testing, particularly Automated Test Framework (ATF).
* Experience working with ServiceNow update sets, application repositories or other ServiceNow deployment mechanisms.
* ITIL Foundation certification or equivalent knowledge.
* Relevant tertiary qualification in IT, computer science, information systems or a related discipline.

**Why this role?**

This opportunity offers exposure to senior leadership, involvement in large-scale digital transformation, and the chance to make a meaningful contribution to outcomes that impact students, educators and communities across Victoria.

You'll be part of a collaborative, high-performing environment where initiative is valued, ideas are welcomed, and your work makes a real difference.

**What you'll bring**

You are a proactive, highly organised professional who thrives in a fast-paced, complex environment and enjoys working at the centre of decision-making.

**Mandatory skills and experience:**

* Demonstrated experience in executive administration or business support within a complex organisation
* Proven abilit y to provide high-level executive support in a multi-stakeholder environment
* Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, workflows and deadlines with minimal supervision
* Excellent communication skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgement and maintain confidentiality
* Experience supporting governance processes, including meeting coordination, record-keeping and compliance
* Proficiency in Microsoft 365, including document and records management systems such as SharePoint
* Demonstrated ability to identify and implement process improvements using digital tools and data
* Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to build productive working relationships and contribute to a positive team culture

**About us**

At the centre of this work is the Information Management and Technology Division (IMTD) a dynamic and forward-thinking division delivering technology services at scale. Supporting over 1,500 government schools, 50,000 teachers, 650,000 students and 6,000 corporate staff, IMTD drives the department's digital capability, business systems and digital transformation agenda. Working in an agile environment, the division focuses on user experience, security, and integration, delivering innovative solutions across cloud infrastructure, enterprise platforms, information management, artificial intelligence and software services.

**About the Department**

The department provides a wide range of learning and development support and services.

The department provides policy leadership, plans for the future of education in Victoria and leads key cross-sector collaboration. The department plays an important system steward role by providing support, guidance, oversight and assurance across early childhood and school education systems.

**How to Apply**

Please click the **Apply Now** button on this advertisement.

Applications should include a cover letter which addresses the key selection criteria (no longer than 2 pages) and resume.

**Further Information**

For more details regarding this position please see attached position description.

The Department values diversity and inclusion in all forms - gender, religion, ethnicity, LGBTIQ+, disability and neurodiversity. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. For more information about our work, working for the Department, diversity and inclusion, and our employment conditions visit the Department website and our Diversity and Inclusion page

Applicants requiring adjustments can contact the nominated contact person.

Information about the Department of Education's operations and employment conditions can be located at www.education.vic.gov.au.

For further information pertaining to the role, please contact **Leon Hooken** at **[email protected]**

Preferred applicants may be required to complete a police check and may be subject to other pre-employment checks. Information provided to the Department of Education will be treated in the strictest confidence.

Please let us know via phone or email if you require any adjustments to ensure your full participation in the recruitment process or if you need the ad or any attachments in an accessible format (e.g large print) due to any viewing difficulties or other accessibility requirements.

jobs.title: Database Administrator
jobs.description:
At Centorrino Technologies (CT), we’re more than just tech—we’re a community that goes beyond expectations. We’ve been recognised as a Great Place to Work in 2024-2025 and one of the Best Places to Work Medium & Large Size in Australia for 2025, with an outstanding eNPS score of 68. And we’re not stopping there.

We’re looking for an experienced **Database Administrator (DBA)** to join our team on a **3-month contract based on-site in Melbourne, VIC.**

This is a great opportunity for a hands-on DBA with strong **SQL Server** experience who enjoys working across database operations, performance, troubleshooting, upgrades and project support.

**Requirements**

What You’ll Do

* Provide SQL Server administration and operational support across production and non-production environments.
* Monitor database performance, capacity and overall health, proactively identifying and resolving issues.
* Manage database backup, restore and recovery processes, including disaster recovery testing.
* Monitor SQL Agent jobs, database services and routine maintenance activities.
* Plan and execute database upgrades, migrations and approved changes.
* Apply SQL Server patches, cumulative updates and security fixes.
* Support application and project teams with database deployments, troubleshooting and technical advice.
* Support monthly operating system patching and validate database services following maintenance.
* Assist with incident resolution through established service management processes.
* Maintain database documentation and ensure operational, security and governance requirements are met.
* Collaborate with infrastructure, application support, project teams and external vendors.
* Assist with broader infrastructure and operational activities as required.

What You’ll Bring

* **3–5 years’ experience** in a DBA or similar database-focused role.
* Strong hands-on **Microsoft SQL Server** administration experience.
* Experience supporting enterprise production and non-production environments.
* Strong knowledge of database monitoring, performance tuning and troubleshooting.
* Experience with database backup, restore and recovery processes.
* Experience with SQL Server patching, upgrades and migrations.
* Knowledge of SQL Agent jobs, database maintenance and health checks.
* Exposure to **Veeam** and disaster recovery processes would be highly regarded.
* Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to manage incidents and competing priorities.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
* The ability to work collaboratively across infrastructure, application and project teams.
* A proactive approach, with a focus on maintaining secure, stable and high-performing database environments.
* Australian-based candidates preferred.

**Benefits**

**Why You'll Love Working Here:**

**Our company is more than just a workplace, it's a hub of inspiration and creativity where employees love to work! Here's why:**

* Hybrid working with team anchor days to support collaboration
* Extensive training and development opportunities that enable continual growth as part of your career planning.
* Extensive discounts and benefits to maximise your money.
* A choice of your IT equipment to maximise your success and access to cost-price tech for your personal needs.
* Fun team events to celebrate achievements and connect with colleagues outside work as part of our engaging culture.

CT celebrates diversity and enables every voice to be heard as we drive to create the world we want. Apply today and be part of a team that values innovation, inclusivity, variety and diverse backgrounds.

*Note: A valid* Vulnerable People / *Working with Children Check (WWCC) and Police Check are required.*

jobs.title: Receptionist/Administrator – Brighton Honda, Geely & Chery (Full-Time)
jobs.description:
Brighton Honda, Geely & Chery, part of the award-winning, family-owned Jowett Motor Group, is looking for a fun, bubbly and organised Reception & Administration professional to join our team.

This is a full-time opportunity for someone who enjoys being the first point of contact for customers while also having an interest in administration and keeping things organised behind the scenes.

You’ll spend approximately 18–20 hours per week on reception, with the balance of your hours supporting stock control and general administration.

**Why Jowett Motor Group**

We back our people properly. Here’s what that looks like:

* Paid Parental Leave – 12 weeks primary carer, 2 weeks secondary.
* Ongoing training and development (online and face-to-face) with real internal career pathways.
* Recognition and team events (BBQs, birthdays, group Christmas party)
* Retailer discounts across major brands.
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* A genuine commitment to supporting women in automotive through our Women in Automotive partnership.
* Leaders who set clear expectations, back you, and want you to succeed.

**About the role**

As part of our team, you’ll play an important role in creating a great customer experience while also providing administrative support to help keep the dealership running smoothly.

Your time will be split between:

* **Reception:** Welcoming customers and visitors, answering calls and assisting with general enquiries.
* **Administration & Stock Control:** Supporting the team with stock-related administration, data entry, record keeping and general office tasks.

You’ll work closely with our Sales, Service and Management teams, with customers always being the first priority.

**Key responsibilities**

* Meet and greet customers and visitors warmly and professionally.
* Answer, screen and direct incoming phone calls and enquiries.
* Provide general administrative and reception support to the dealership.
* Assist with appointment enquiries and customer requests.
* Support stock control processes and related administration.
* Maintain accurate records and complete data entry as required.
* Work closely with Sales, Service and Management to ensure customers are assisted promptly.
* Maintain the reception and showroom areas.
* Follow dealership processes, systems and compliance requirements.
* Assist with other general administration tasks as required.

**About you**

You might be coming from reception, administration, retail, hospitality, customer service or another people-focused environment.

What matters most is that you:

* Are a people person who enjoys interacting with others.
* Are organised and thorough, with great attention to detail.
* Are confident, professional and well presented.
* Are adaptable and able to multitask.
* Are comfortable with administrative tasks and data entry.
* Are familiar with Microsoft 365.
* Are reliable, punctual and keen to learn.
* Hold a current driver’s licence.

Automotive experience is a bonus, but not essential.

**About Jowett Motor Group**

Since 2001, Jowett Motor Group has grown into a leading automotive group representing BMW, MINI, Motorrad, Honda, Audi, Geely, Chery and JMG Used Cars. Our culture is built on family values, accountability, and continuous improvement. We care about performance, but we care just as much about our people.

**Apply now**

Ready to take the next step with Brighton Honda, Geely & Chery? Apply today.

Learn more about careers at Jowett Motor Group: www.jmgpl.com.au/careers

**Diversity & inclusion**

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, ages, genders and cultures.

**Pre-employment checks**

A National Police Check is required prior to commencement.

### **Company Overview**

Jowett Motor Group was born from the experience and forethought of Tony Jowett in 1995 with brands Audi, Volkswagen and Subaru, before opening Eastern Honda Doncaster in 2000 which remains today. JMG has continued as a family-owned and operated business with its award-winning group of BMW and Honda dealerships across Victoria, South Australia and now the Australian Capital Territory. JMG is an established retail partner of Honda Australia, operating three metro Honda Centres: Eastern Honda, Northern Honda & Brighton Honda Centre. The JMG journey with Honda has been recognised by multiple National Dealer of the Year and Customer Excellence awards, to now leading national sales and service volumes. A new era was marked in 2013 for JMG with the opening of its first BMW dealership, Waverley BMW. Fast establishing itself as a key member of the BMW dealership network through a strong customer focused approach and commitment to excellence, JMG acquired South Yarra BMW in 2020. This was followed by the greenfield development of Berwick BMW opening in late 2020 and the recent introduction of Berwick MINI Garage. 2021 marked the opening of Glenelg BMW and MINI Garage in South Australia with a full redevelopment of the Glenelg site underway - due for completion in the second half of 2025. In September 2024, JMG will officially take over all existing business operations in Canberra BMW - including Canberra MINI Garage and Canberra BMW Motorrad. The growth plan for JMG continues with the opening of Chery Doncaster in July 2024 and Chery Brighton in early 2025. The JMG Executive Team is committed to fostering growth and excellence in the automotive retail operations sector. The Group aims to continue to collaborate with current and future Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to deliver award-winning retail experiences for customers while creating job opportunities for the automotive industry and current JMG employees.
